customising/multi-language.title: Multi-language support
customising/multi-language.description: Handling meetings that mix Japanese and English, choosing the output language, and the list of supported languages.
customising/multi-language.html:
You can set which language transcription and summaries come out in, for Japanese meetings, English meetings, and meetings that mix the two. This article concentrates on the decisions that actually arise in a Japanese setting, covering how to choose and where the limits are.

There are two settings. Both are changed in the desktop app under Settings > Preferences > Language.

  • Transcription language: which language what is spoken in the meeting is recognised as
  • Summary language: which language the note generated after the meeting is written in
The interface is in English only

The app's interface — menus, buttons, settings — is currently in English only. Transcripts and summaries can be produced in Japanese, but the interface itself has not been localised. This article gives the Japanese alongside the English items on screen.

#Settings by kind of meeting

What the meeting is like Transcription language Summary language
Everyone speaks Japanese Multi-language Auto
Japanese with English words and proper nouns mixed in Multi-language Auto
Japanese and English speakers alternating Multi-language Auto or English
An English-only meeting, but you want the minutes in Japanese Multi-language Auto produces an English summary, so use chat to turn it into Japanese
An English-only meeting, and English minutes are fine English English

Choosing “English” as the transcription language gives the highest quality for English but does not expect Japanese speech. To record a Japanese meeting, choose “Multi-language”.

#Transcription language

There are two options in the desktop app.

  • English: gives the highest quality where most of the meeting is in English.
  • Multi-language: handles all the languages listed later in this article. Where several languages are spoken within one meeting, it switches between them as it transcribes.

In a discussion that mixes Japanese and English — someone at an overseas office explaining the position in English while the Japanese side confirms in Japanese — choosing “Multi-language” puts both into the same transcript.

This setting applies only to meetings recorded after you change it. A transcript already recorded cannot be translated into another language afterwards. To read what was said in a past meeting in Japanese, ask chat to translate that passage.

#Summary language

  • English: the note is generated in English regardless of the language spoken in the meeting.
  • Auto: the note is generated in whichever language was spoken most in the meeting.

For a Japanese note from a Japanese meeting, choose “Auto”. In a meeting that is roughly half Japanese and half English, the output language may vary from meeting to meeting. To fix the output, either choose “English” or read the generated note and correct what you need.

To change the language of a past note, change this setting, open the note and run regenerate.

#Switching language mid-meeting

You can also change language after a meeting has started. Reselect the language from the meeting controls on the recording screen.

Just after switching, transcription may pause briefly while the new language's recognition model loads. In meetings where the languages divide clearly — Japanese in the first half, English in the second — timing the switch to a break between agenda items makes any gap less noticeable.

A language changed mid-meeting is also saved as the default for later meetings. To make it a temporary change for that meeting only, set it back afterwards under Settings > Preferences > Language.

#Improving accuracy in Japanese meetings

With the language set correctly, keeping the following in mind means fewer corrections when you read the transcript back.

  • Register proper nouns in advance: company names, department names, product names and external contacts can be registered under Customising transcription. In Japanese, the right sound written with the wrong characters is a common error, and registration makes a noticeable difference. Note that registration makes a word more likely to be recognised; it does not standardise variant spellings such as “サーバー” and “サーバ” onto one form. Where your company has settled on a spelling, replace it after exporting.
  • The transcript keeps what was actually said: back-channel responses, restarts and the exchange of pleasantries are all recorded as spoken. Where you need something readable, share the enhanced note rather than the transcript.
  • Output is horizontal: even where your internal forms and minutes use vertical writing, transcripts and summaries are produced as horizontal text. If you need vertical layout, set it in your word processor after exporting.
  • When people talk over each other: recognition accuracy drops when several participants speak at once. For attributing speech to each speaker, see Speaker labels.

#Supported languages

The desktop app (macOS / Windows) supports 31 languages. These are the languages the transcription provider currently supports.

Region Languages supported
East and South-East Asia Japanese, Chinese (Mandarin), Chinese (Cantonese), Korean, Vietnamese
South Asia Hindi, Marathi, Urdu
Middle East and West Asia Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Turkish
Africa Afrikaans, Xhosa, Zulu
Europe English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Catalan, Galician, Danish, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Estonian, Romanian, Russian

If you need a language not on this list, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. We will let you know if the transcription provider adds support.

#Related articles

Customising transcriptionRegistering company and department names to improve accuracy→How transcription worksWhen and what audio is captured→AI-enhanced notesGenerating and regenerating summaries→Transcription problemsWhat to check when accuracy is poor→

customising/profile-and-preferences.title: Profile and preferences
customising/profile-and-preferences.description: Personal settings: display name, default template, appearance and shortcuts.
customising/profile-and-preferences.html:
This collects the settings that adjust how {{PRODUCT}} behaves to suit you: filling in your profile, deciding whether your data is used for model training, and whether you receive early releases.

Open settings by clicking your workspace name at the bottom left and choosing Settings. Changes here apply only to your own account. Settings that affect the whole workspace are on a separate screen only administrators can change.

#Filling in your profile

Open Profile from the settings sidebar and enter information about your work. Recording your role, what you are responsible for, and the areas you work in gives the summary generator something to go on, and makes the points you care about more likely to end up in your notes.

For someone in sales, for instance, exchanges about budget and timing during a deal are more likely to be kept; for someone in engineering, exchanges about specifications and defects. Summaries are generated whether or not you fill this in, but the more varied your meetings, the more difference it makes.

The role you set here also affects which templates are shown as standard. The role you chose when you first installed the app can be changed from this screen, and changing it swaps the template list over. How to choose templates is in Shape your notes with templates.

What to put in your profile

What you enter here is used as context when generating notes. Keep it to describing your role at work, and do not write personal circumstances irrelevant to producing minutes, such as health conditions or family matters.

#The model training setting

Whether meeting data is used to improve {{PRODUCT}} — that is, to train models — is handled differently depending on your plan.

Plan Default Can the user change it
Free and Personal plans on Settings > Preferences > Data and sharing lets you switch it off at any time
Team and Enterprise plans off not used for training; there is no setting for users to enable it

Data held on the Team and Enterprise plans is held by {{COMPANY}} under a delegation of handling from the organisation. Using it for training would go beyond the scope of that delegation, so it is not done on these plans. The setting is not shown at all, so an administrator wanting to confirm the state of the whole workspace should check from the workspace settings screen.

On no plan do we permit external AI model providers to use users' data to train their own models. The purposes for which data is acquired and the details of how it is handled are in AI models and training data and the Privacy policy.

#Receiving early releases (Labs)

To try features before they are released, you can turn on early releases under Settings > Preferences > Labs.

With it on, new versions are delivered earlier than general release. To go back to the normal channel, switch it off on the same screen. Not every update contains new features; some are only bug fixes or small adjustments towards the next major update.

If you find a problem in an early release, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Knowing which meeting it happened in and what you were doing makes the cause quicker to find.

Early releases on machines used for work

Early releases are delivered while still being validated. On machines used to record important meetings, we recommend staying on the normal channel. How updates work where the app is distributed centrally is covered in Bulk installation and updates for admins.

#Other settings worth configuring

What you want to set Article to read
The language spoken in meetings, and the language of summaries Multi-language support
Registering easily misheard words such as company and department names Customising transcription
Templates that set the heading structure of your notes Shape your notes with templates
Notifications for meeting start and note generation Notification settings
The default sharing scope Sharing controls

#Related articles

sharing/exporting-notes.title: Exporting notes in bulk
sharing/exporting-notes.description: How to export past notes and transcripts to CSV. Also usable for disclosure requests and data portability.
sharing/exporting-notes.html:
The notes and transcripts you have accumulated in {{PRODUCT}} can be exported together as a CSV file. As well as backup and migration to another tool, it can be used directly to answer a disclosure request under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information.

Security, privacy and data FAQsHow personal data is handled, and where to send disclosure requests→Privacy policyPublished matters regarding retained personal data, and fees→
Note

Export is run from the settings screen of the desktop app (macOS / Windows). Only notes you own can be exported; notes owned by other members, and notes merely shared with you, are not included. On the Enterprise plan, an administrator may have disabled export.

#Running an export

  1. 1

    Open settings

    Click your avatar at the bottom left to open settings.

  2. 2

    Open your profile

    Open Profile under Preferences in the sidebar.

  3. 3

    Choose the workspaces

    Tick the workspaces you want to export. If you belong to several, you can select only the ones you need.

  4. 4

    Generate the CSV

    Generate CSV. Generation can take several hours.

When generation finishes, a download link is emailed to the address registered on your account. The file is not produced directly in the app, so wait a while and then check your email.

Check
  • Generate CSV showed an acknowledgement on screen after you clicked it
  • the email address registered on your account is one you can currently receive mail at
  • once the email arrives, you download within the link's 24-hour validity

#What the CSV contains

Each note is one row, with basic fields such as the title, the AI-enhanced summary, the transcript and the date and time. It covers only the notes you own in the selected workspaces.

On screen, the free plan does not list notes older than 30 days, but the export includes your full history, including those not shown. The differences in what each plan displays are covered in Plans and billing.

Some things are not included. Notes with no summary generated, and deleted notes, are out of scope. The number of rows exported can therefore be lower than the number shown in the app. If the counts do not match, check these two things first.

Avoiding garbled characters when opening the CSV in Excel

The exported CSV is UTF-8. Double-clicking a CSV to open it in Excel on Windows can, in some environments, read it as Shift_JIS, turning Japanese text into unreadable symbols. Open it in one of these ways instead.

  • In Excel's “Data” tab choose “From Text/CSV”, select the file, and set the file origin to “65001: Unicode (UTF-8)” before loading
  • Import it into Google Sheets to check the contents, and if necessary download it again from there in Excel format
  • Open the CSV in a text editor and save it again as UTF-8 with BOM before opening it in Excel. In Windows Notepad, choose “UTF-8 with BOM” in the encoding field of “Save As”

Transcript cells contain line breaks and quotation marks. If you process the file with something other than a spreadsheet, use a CSV parser that handles fields containing line breaks.

#Download links and reissuing

Item Detail
Link validity The link in the email expires after 24 hours. It cannot be opened after that
Signed-in state Open it in a browser signed in to the account that requested the export. If you are signed in as another account, or not signed in, the download does not happen
How often it can be reissued You can request regeneration at any time, but only once every 24 hours per account

If the link has expired, or you need a file with newer content, generate again from the profile screen in settings using the same steps. If 24 hours have not passed since the previous generation, you cannot create a new export until they have.

#Plan and administrator restrictions

On plans other than Enterprise, export is enabled by default. On the Enterprise plan it is disabled by default, and only an Enterprise workspace administrator can use the workspace setting Allow exporting data to enable or disable it for members.

If you cannot find “Generate CSV” in settings, an administrator may have disabled this toggle. Check with your workspace administrator.

#Can an administrator export everyone's data?

No. There is no bulk export covering a whole workspace, and no export on someone's behalf using administrator rights. An export always contains only the notes owned by the person who ran it.

What happens when someone leaves depends on where their notes are. Notes they added to a folder in a team space remain accessible from that folder after they leave. Personal notes they never shared are accessible to neither administrators nor other members. Where you need them to export or share something, one approach is to re-invite them to the workspace temporarily so they can do it. The steps are in Workspaces.

Where notes should be kept ahead of someone leaving or moving teams is also a question of folder design. When to review it, and the specific steps, are under “Reviewing permissions” in Spaces and folders.

#Using it to answer a disclosure request

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 33 (disclosure)

An individual may request a business handling personal information to disclose the retained personal data by which they are identified. It provides that the individual may specify the method, including provision by electromagnetic record and other methods prescribed by Personal Information Protection Commission rules (Article 30 of the Enforcement Regulations). The Guidelines on the Act (General Rules) give attaching to email and download from a members' site as examples of provision by electromagnetic record, and state that provision in a readable and searchable format is desirable, as is provision in a format portable to other businesses where technically possible.

CSV export is designed as a means of that provision by electromagnetic record. Because the format opens in a spreadsheet and can be imported into other services, requesting disclosure of your own notes and transcripts through this feature is the surest and quickest route.

The scope of what an export can retrieve is limited, however. Notes with no summary generated, deleted notes, and notes owned by other members are not included. Items other than notes, such as account information and settings, are also out of scope. To request disclosure of those, contact {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. We may ask for documentation confirming your identity. Requests may also be made by an agent.

How fees are handled where we charge for a disclosure request is set out in the Privacy policy. No fee is charged for requests to correct or stop using data.

Where to send requests for business use

On business plans, {{COMPANY}} provides {{PRODUCT}} as a party to whom the contracting company has delegated the handling of personal data. Where an employee requests disclosure of their own personal data, they should as a rule apply to their employer. Where {{COMPANY}} receives a request directly, we handle it through the contracting company.

#If something is not working

  • The email does not arrive: generation takes several hours. Check your spam folder, and if it still has not arrived, check that the email address registered on your account is one you can currently use. How to change it is in Changing your account and email address.
  • The link gives an error: either more than 24 hours have passed since it was issued, or you are opening it in a browser signed in as a different account. Sign in again as the account that requested the export.
  • I cannot generate again: 24 hours have not passed since the previous generation. Try again later.
  • “Generate CSV” is not shown: on the Enterprise plan, an administrator may have disabled export.
  • The count does not match what the app shows: notes with no summary and deleted notes are not included.
  • It opens with unreadable Japanese: follow “Avoiding garbled characters when opening the CSV in Excel” in this article and load it with the encoding specified.

If that does not resolve it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the date and time you requested the export and your account's email address.

#Related articles

Sharing notesSharing individual notes inside and outside your company→Spaces and foldersHow notes are organised, and sharing scope→Automatic transcript deletionSetting a retention period→Deleting your accountWhat happens to data after you close your account→

On the Enterprise plan, an administrator may have disabled export. # Running an export 1 Open settings Click your avatar at the bottom left to open settings. 2 Open your profile Open Profile under Preferences in the sidebar. 3 Choose the workspaces Tick the workspaces you want to export. If you belong to several, you can select only the ones you need. 4 Generate the CSV Generate CSV . Generation can take several hours. Figure Screenshot: the profile tab in settings, with the workspace selector and the “Generate CSV” button When generation finishes, a download link is emailed to the address registered on your account. The file is not produced directly in the app, so wait a while and then check your email. Check Generate CSV showed an acknowledgement on screen after you clicked it the email address registered on your account is one you can currently receive mail at once the email arrives, you download within the link's 24-hour validity # What the CSV contains Each note is one row, with basic fields such as the title, the AI-enhanced summary, the transcript and the date and time. It covers only the notes you own in the selected workspaces. On screen, the free plan does not list notes older than 30 days, but the export includes your full history , including those not shown. The differences in what each plan displays are covered in Plans and billing . Some things are not included. Notes with no summary generated, and deleted notes, are out of scope. The number of rows exported can therefore be lower than the number shown in the app. If the counts do not match, check these two things first. Avoiding garbled characters when opening the CSV in Excel The exported CSV is UTF-8. Double-clicking a CSV to open it in Excel on Windows can, in some environments, read it as Shift_JIS, turning Japanese text into unreadable symbols. Open it in one of these ways instead. In Excel's “Data” tab choose “From Text/CSV”, select the file, and set the file origin to “65001: Unicode (UTF-8)” before loading Import it into Google Sheets to check the contents, and if necessary download it again from there in Excel format Open the CSV in a text editor and save it again as UTF-8 with BOM before opening it in Excel. In Windows Notepad, choose “UTF-8 with BOM” in the encoding field of “Save As” Transcript cells contain line breaks and quotation marks. If you process the file with something other than a spreadsheet, use a CSV parser that handles fields containing line breaks. # Download links and reissuing Item Detail Link validity The link in the email expires after 24 hours . It cannot be opened after that Signed-in state Open it in a browser signed in to the account that requested the export. If you are signed in as another account, or not signed in, the download does not happen How often it can be reissued You can request regeneration at any time, but only once every 24 hours per account If the link has expired, or you need a file with newer content, generate again from the profile screen in settings using the same steps. If 24 hours have not passed since the previous generation, you cannot create a new export until they have. # Plan and administrator restrictions On plans other than Enterprise, export is enabled by default. On the Enterprise plan it is disabled by default, and only an Enterprise workspace administrator can use the workspace setting Allow exporting data to enable or disable it for members. Figure Screenshot: the workspace settings screen, showing the “Allow exporting data” toggle If you cannot find “Generate CSV” in settings, an administrator may have disabled this toggle. Check with your workspace administrator. # Can an administrator export everyone's data? No. There is no bulk export covering a whole workspace, and no export on someone's behalf using administrator rights. An export always contains only the notes owned by the person who ran it. What happens when someone leaves depends on where their notes are. Notes they added to a folder in a team space remain accessible from that folder after they leave. Personal notes they never shared are accessible to neither administrators nor other members. Where you need them to export or share something, one approach is to re-invite them to the workspace temporarily so they can do it. The steps are in Workspaces . Where notes should be kept ahead of someone leaving or moving teams is also a question of folder design. When to review it, and the specific steps, are under “Reviewing permissions” in Spaces and folders . # Using it to answer a disclosure request Legislation Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 33 (disclosure) An individual may request a business handling personal information to disclose the retained personal data by which they are identified. It provides that the individual may specify the method, including provision by electromagnetic record and other methods prescribed by Personal Information Protection Commission rules (Article 30 of the Enforcement Regulations). The Guidelines on the Act (General Rules) give attaching to email and download from a members' site as examples of provision by electromagnetic record, and state that provision in a readable and searchable format is desirable, as is provision in a format portable to other businesses where technically possible. CSV export is designed as a means of that provision by electromagnetic record. Because the format opens in a spreadsheet and can be imported into other services, requesting disclosure of your own notes and transcripts through this feature is the surest and quickest route. The scope of what an export can retrieve is limited, however. Notes with no summary generated, deleted notes, and notes owned by other members are not included. Items other than notes, such as account information and settings, are also out of scope. To request disclosure of those, contact {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. We may ask for documentation confirming your identity. Requests may also be made by an agent. How fees are handled where we charge for a disclosure request is set out in the Privacy policy . No fee is charged for requests to correct or stop using data. Where to send requests for business use On business plans, {{COMPANY}} provides {{PRODUCT}} as a party to whom the contracting company has delegated the handling of personal data. Where an employee requests disclosure of their own personal data, they should as a rule apply to their employer. Where {{COMPANY}} receives a request directly, we handle it through the contracting company. # If something is not working The email does not arrive : generation takes several hours. Check your spam folder, and if it still has not arrived, check that the email address registered on your account is one you can currently use. How to change it is in Changing your account and email address . The link gives an error : either more than 24 hours have passed since it was issued, or you are opening it in a browser signed in as a different account. Sign in again as the account that requested the export. I cannot generate again : 24 hours have not passed since the previous generation. Try again later. “Generate CSV” is not shown : on the Enterprise plan, an administrator may have disabled export. The count does not match what the app shows : notes with no summary and deleted notes are not included. It opens with unreadable Japanese : follow “Avoiding garbled characters when opening the CSV in Excel” in this article and load it with the encoding specified. If that does not resolve it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the date and time you requested the export and your account's email address. # Related articles Sharing notes Sharing individual notes inside and outside your company → Spaces and folders How notes are organised, and sharing scope → Automatic transcript deletion Setting a retention period → Deleting your account What happens to data after you close your account →

sharing/folders/spaces-and-folders.title: Spaces and folders
sharing/folders/spaces-and-folders.description: The difference between spaces and folders as ways to organise notes, and how to design sharing and permissions.
sharing/folders/spaces-and-folders.html:
{{PRODUCT}} organises notes in two levels: spaces and folders. A space sets the broad question of who can see something; a folder is the unit of classification and team sharing within it. This article covers the difference, creating folders, designing permissions, and automatic posting per folder.

Sharing notesActions and permissions for sharing individual notes→User groupsGranting access in bulk by department→Sharing controlsThe three levels of sharing scope, and administrator restrictions→
Note

Folders are created and shared from the sidebar of the desktop app (macOS / Windows). Any member of the workspace can create a folder, but creating and deleting spaces, and ownership of folders in the team space, are limited to administrators.

#Using the sidebar

Open and close the left sidebar with ⌘S (Mac) or Ctrl+S (Windows). Opening a meeting note closes the sidebar automatically, widening the area for the body. Widen the window and the sidebar pins to the left edge, shown alongside the body. When the window is narrow it appears as an overlay on top of the body.

#Spaces

The sidebar is made up of two kinds of space.

Space Who can see it Main use
My notes you alone, plus any private folders explicitly shared with you personal meetings, and notes you have not yet decided whether to share
The space named after the workspace (team space) every member of the workspace meeting notes the team refers to

The workspace administrator automatically becomes the owner of folders in the team space. An administrator can also move a team space folder into My notes to make it private again.

You choose which space to put a folder in when you create it. You can change the space afterwards from the folder's sharing settings. Moving a folder between spaces changes who can see it all at once, so check the notes inside before moving a folder containing anything sensitive.

#Custom spaces (administrators only)

As well as My notes and the team space, a workspace administrator can create their own spaces. Custom spaces exist to separate permissions in larger organisations. They let you design things so that notes and folders are shared only with a particular group — a department, a site, a project — and not with the whole workspace.

To manage spaces, open Settings → Spaces, or click Manage spaces in the sidebar.

  • Creating a space: Create space, enter a name, icon and description, and add members. Anyone added to the space can see the notes and folders in it.
  • Deleting a space: choose Delete space from the space's menu. Deletion cannot be undone, but the notes and folders inside are not deleted — they simply leave that space.

Only administrators can create and delete spaces.

Check the default for API access

Where a space has Allow API access enabled, it can also be read using the workspace's API key. This setting is enabled by default on newly created spaces. If you do not want the notes in a space retrievable through the API, switch it off when creating the space, or afterwards under Settings → Spaces. For details see API.

#Creating a folder

Open the sidebar and click the + button beside the space name. Set the folder name and icon, and enter a description. The description helps other members understand what the folder is for, and also gives chat something to work with when answering across that folder. Descriptions that make clear what is inside — “regular sales meetings with key customers”, “records of recruitment interviews” — are the useful ones.

#Subfolders

Creating a subfolder inside a folder gives you one more level of classification — a subfolder per customer under a “Sales” folder, say, or one per initiative under a “Product” folder.

There are two ways to create one.

  • From the menu: click the three-dot menu beside a folder name in the sidebar and choose Create folder.
  • Drag and drop: drag an existing folder onto another and it goes inside. Only folders you own can be nested. Folders you have joined as a member through sharing cannot be dragged into another folder.

Subfolders go one level deep; you cannot create a subfolder inside a subfolder. Folders can also be dragged to reorder them in the sidebar.

A subfolder inherits its space and sharing settings from its parent. If the parent is in the team space, every subfolder under it belongs to the team space too. A subfolder cannot be made private on its own, so to separate visibility, separate the parent folders.

#Adding notes to a folder

In the notes list, click Add to folder, or drag and drop the note onto a folder in the sidebar.

To add several notes at once, select them in the list.

  • Click the checkbox that appears when you hover over a note.
  • Shift-click another note to select the range between them.
  • Select all selects every note in the current list. Then click Add to folder.

A single note can go in several folders, so you can keep parallel views by theme, by project and by customer.

#Adding recurring meetings automatically

When you add the note for a recurring meeting such as a weekly review to a folder, you are asked whether to add automatically the notes for later instances to the same folder. Turning it on removes the manual step each time.

Turning automatic adding on

  1. Put the recurring meeting's note into the folder with Add to folder or by dragging and dropping.
  2. When asked “add future meetings automatically?”, click Add automatically.
  3. From then on, that recurring meeting's notes go into the folder automatically.

Stopping it, or changing the destination

  • To stop: open the folder selector on any note from that recurring meeting and untick the folder. That also cancels automatic adding for that recurring meeting.
  • To change folder: remove it from the current folder as above, then add it to the new folder and choose Add automatically when asked.

#Sharing and permissions

Access to a folder is determined by three settings.

  1. Space — which space the folder is in sets its default visibility. You can change it from the sharing settings at any time.
  2. Members — add specific people to the folder directly by email address.
  3. Link visibility — decides who can get in from the folder's link when you share it.

The sharing scope set on individual notes is managed separately from the folder's settings. For per-note sharing scope and defaults, see Sharing controls.

#Adding members

  1. Open the folder's sharing settings.
  2. Enter the person's email address.
  3. Add.
  4. They receive an email telling them they have been added to the folder.

If they already use {{PRODUCT}}, the folder appears in their sidebar as it is. If not, they can view the folder in a web browser and are guided through creating an account to open it in the app.

#Link visibility

Setting Who can get in When to use it
Invited people only only folder members can get in from the link folders containing anything sensitive. We recommend this as the default
Everyone in the workspace {{PRODUCT}} users with an account on your own domain can get in. People outside the workspace see “folder not found” after signing in folders meant to be widely available internally
Anyone with the link anyone holding the link can view it in a web browser, including people without a {{PRODUCT}} account the widest setting. Use it only when sharing outside the company, having checked the contents

#Owner and member permissions

Whoever created a folder is its owner. People added later are members, and can do less.

Action Owner Member
Add your own notes yes yes
Remove someone else's notes yes no
Remove your own notes yes yes
Change the sharing settings yes no
Add and remove members yes yes
Delete the folder yes no
Nest it inside another folder yes no
Leave the folder — leave from the three-dot menu and remove it from your own sidebar

Note that members can add and remove members too. People the owner did not intend can therefore end up in a folder, so for folders involving anyone outside the company we recommend reviewing the member list in the sharing settings periodically.

Someone you add to a folder can also see the full meeting transcripts when they open it in the desktop app. How it looks when opened from a link in a web browser is covered in Sharing notes. Choose between adding them to the folder and sending them a link according to whether the transcript needs to be shared too.

#Reviewing permissions

A common problem in Japanese companies is permissions not following people when they move. Someone who transfers but remains a member of their previous department's spaces and folders can still read past sales and HR notes afterwards. To manage by department rather than person, use User groups.

Check

Review your space and folder settings at these points.

  • Around a departmental transfer: whether the person who moved is still on the member lists of custom spaces and folders
  • When someone leaves: whether notes the business needs are left in My notes folders owned by the person leaving
  • When a project ends: whether folders set to “anyone with the link” have been set back to “invited people only”

Because an administrator owns team space folders, they keep working after the person responsible leaves — but personal folders in My notes do not. Ask people to move the notes the business needs into team space folders before they leave. What to do when notes have to be retrieved after someone has left is covered in Exporting notes in bulk.

#Chatting with a folder or space

Chat can take a whole folder or space as its scope, not just an individual note. My notes and the team space themselves can be the scope too.

Open the folder or space and type your question, and the answer is generated across the notes it contains. You can use it to gather what was said about a particular point across past meetings, pull the matters under consideration out of several sales meetings, or organise the topics that keep coming up.

You can leave the model on automatic selection or choose one from the dropdown. For questions spanning many notes, choosing a model that handles long context can make the result more consistent. How to choose is covered in Choosing a model.

#Automatic posting from a folder (integrations)

You can set rules that send notes added to a folder to other tools automatically. Supported are Slack, HubSpot, Attio and Zapier.

To set it up, open the folder, click the Integrations button in the folder header, and choose from the list which integration to use for this folder.

Once set up, new notes added to that folder are sent automatically to the connected integration. The integration itself has to be set up first, so complete the connection following the articles for Slack, HubSpot, Attio and Zapier before configuring this. The data each integration sends is set out in Integrations overview.

Automatic posting fires the moment a note is added to the folder. Before enabling it, check that it is not set to post to a channel with external people in it, or somewhere referred to across departments.

#If something is not working

  • I cannot drag a folder into another folder: only folders you own can be nested. Folders shared with you cannot be moved. Folders cannot be put inside a subfolder either.
  • The person I shared with cannot see the folder: if they do not use {{PRODUCT}}, it does not appear in a sidebar and they view it in a web browser. They also cannot get in if link visibility is still “invited people only” and you have not added them as a member.
  • The person I shared with cannot see the transcript: transcripts are not shown when viewing in a web browser. Ask them to open the folder in the desktop app.
  • The link says “folder not found”: visibility may be set to “everyone in the workspace” while they do not have an account on your domain.
  • Recurring meeting notes are not added automatically: either Add automatically was not chosen at the prompt, or the setting was cancelled when the note was later removed from the folder. Add the note to the folder again and set it up once more.

#Related articles

Sharing notesSharing scope and permissions for individual notes→User groupsGranting access by department→Exporting notes in bulkExporting past notes→WorkspacesInviting members and administrator permissions→

sharing/integrations/affinity.title: Affinity integration
sharing/integrations/affinity.description: Setting up sending meeting notes to Affinity records, and what can be sent.
sharing/integrations/affinity.html:
Connecting Affinity lets you send notes from sales and customer meetings to Affinity person and company records from within {{PRODUCT}}. All {{PRODUCT}} does is add notes; it never modifies or deletes notes already in Affinity.

#Issuing and registering an API key

Connecting to Affinity uses an API key. An API key is tied to the account that issued it, so where several people in a workspace use it, each person should issue their own API key. Sharing someone else's key causes connection failures, or records in Affinity attributed to whoever issued it.

What you need first
  • the {{PRODUCT}} desktop app (macOS / Windows). Both the connection setup and sending are done from the desktop app
  • an Affinity account, with permission to issue your own API key
  1. 1

    Create an app in Affinity

    Affinity and open “Settings” from the left-hand navigation.Developer Tools, click “Manage Apps” and choose “+ New App”.

  2. 2

    Copy the API key

    Enter a name for the app (for example {{PRODUCT}}). The description is optional. Click “Add App” and an API Key Created dialog appears.This key cannot be displayed again. Copy it while it is on screen.

  3. 3

    Register the API key in {{PRODUCT}}

    In {{PRODUCT}}'s settings (opened from your avatar at the bottom left), choose “Connectors” and paste the API key into the Affinity field. What you enter is saved automatically.

Check
  • Affinity shows as connected under Settings > Connectors
  • Affinity appears among the sharing options at the top right when you open a note
Handling the API key

An API key is a credential with access to your Affinity data. Do not paste it into chat tools, documents or source code to share it. If you suspect it has leaked, delete that app on Affinity's “Manage Apps” screen, issue a new key, and register it in {{PRODUCT}} again.

#Sending a note to Affinity

Once connected, an Affinity item appears at the top right when you open a note. Sending is a manual, one-at-a-time action; this integration has no setting to send notes automatically when they go into a folder.

  1. Open the note you want to send and click Affinity at the top right.
  2. Matching person and company records are suggested, based on the email addresses of the calendar event's attendees.
  3. Review the suggestions and remove any you do not want. If a record is missing, you can search for and add it.
  4. Save, and the content is added as a note on the records you chose.

If there is no record in Affinity with a matching email address, no suggestion appears. Create the record in Affinity first and then send.

What is sent to Affinity is the content of the AI-enhanced note. It contains attendees' names and what was said, so check that the people who can see that record in Affinity match the people the meeting content may be shared with. How to account for sending to external services as handling of personal data is covered in Integrations overview.

#If something is not working

Q. The integration will not connect

A. Check these two things.

  • that you are signed in to {{PRODUCT}} and Affinity with the same email address
  • that the API key you are using is your own. Keys issued by other users will not work.
Q. An integration that was working has suddenly stopped

A. Disconnect Affinity under Settings > Connectors and register the API key again. If that does not fix it, check whether the API key has been deleted on the Affinity side.

Q. I get “Something went wrong. Check your key or try again”

A. First check you are using your own API key — registering someone else's produces this error. It can also appear where your organisation as a whole has hit Affinity's API usage limit. If that seems likely, check with your team's administrator.

Q. It still does not work

A. Contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. A screenshot or screen recording of the error makes the cause quicker to narrow down.

sharing/integrations/attio.title: Attio integration
sharing/integrations/attio.description: Connecting an Attio workspace and sending notes to it.
sharing/integrations/attio.html:
Connecting Attio lets you keep meeting notes against person and company records. You can set up both sending notes one at a time and sending notes in a folder automatically.

#Setting up the connection

What you need first
  • the {{PRODUCT}} desktop app (macOS / Windows). Both the connection setup and sending are done from the desktop app
  • the Attio workspace to connect to, and permission to authorise a connection to it
  1. 1

    Open connectors in settings

    In {{PRODUCT}}'s settings (opened from your avatar at the bottom left), choose “Connectors”. Attio is in the list of services you can connect.

  2. 2

    Connect the Attio workspace

    Click connect on the Attio card and a browser opens with Attio's authorisation screen. Choose the workspace to connect and approve it, and the connection is made. Close the browser tab and return to {{PRODUCT}}.

Check
  • Settings > Attio shows the name of the workspace you connected
  • an Attio item appears at the top right when you open a note

#Sending notes one at a time

  1. Open the note you want to send and click Attio at the top right.
  2. Choose the person or company to send it to. Suggestions are offered based on the meeting's attendees.
  3. Confirm, and the content is added as a note on the record you chose.

#Sending notes in a folder automatically

Notes added to a particular folder can be saved automatically to the matching person or company record.

  1. Open the folder.
  2. Click the “Integrations” button in the folder header.
  3. Switch the Attio item on.
  4. Choose which kind of record to link to (company, person, related deal).

Once set up, notes added to that folder are added automatically to the Attio records matching your criteria.

Past notes are not sent retrospectively

Automatic sending covers only notes added to the folder after you switched the integration on. Notes already in the folder beforehand are not synced. To send past notes, open each one and send it individually with the Attio button at the top right.

What is sent to Attio is the content of the AI-enhanced note. It contains attendees' names and what was said, so check that the people who can see that record in Attio match the people the meeting content may be shared with. How to account for sending to external services as handling of personal data is covered in Integrations overview.

#If something is not working

Q. “Save to Attio” is greyed out

A. You cannot send until the AI-enhanced note has been generated. If it has not been, regenerate using the steps in AI-enhanced notes and try again.

Q. Notes from a folder are not appearing in Attio

A. Check the following in order.

  • {{PRODUCT}} matches Attio records using the attendees' email addresses. Where there is no matching record, nothing is created in Attio. Check that the attendees' email addresses are registered as people or companies in Attio.
  • Settings > Attio shows the most recent sync status. Where an error has occurred, the details are shown on that screen.
  • Notes already in the folder before the integration was switched on are out of scope. Send those individually.

sharing/integrations/api.title: API
sharing/integrations/api.description: An overview of the API for retrieving notes and transcripts from external systems, its scopes, and managing keys.
sharing/integrations/api.html:
The API lets your own systems and scripts retrieve meeting notes, transcripts and AI-enhanced notes programmatically. When you create an API key, you choose the range of notes that key can read.

Team plan Enterprise plan

For some purposes MCP is simpler

If all you want is for an AI tool such as Claude or ChatGPT to consult your notes, the MCP server suits better. MCP uses OAuth in a browser and is designed for interactive AI tools. Use API keys for scripts, scheduled automation, and calls from your own systems.

#What you can build

  • Your own AI agents — build your own processing to aggregate trends across sales meetings, extract recurring themes from product requests, or combine meeting context with other internal data.
  • Internal knowledge bases and wikis — feed meeting notes into Notion, Confluence or an internal wiki and keep them searchable and current.
  • Task and follow-up automation — extract decisions and tasks from notes and create them automatically in Linear, Jira, Todoist and similar.
  • CRM updates and reporting — send meeting summaries and tasks to CRM records, dashboards and internal reporting.

#Plans that include it

API keys can be created by workspace members on the Team or Enterprise plan.

On the Enterprise plan, administrators can control the scopes members are allowed under Settings → Workspace → General → API access for members.

About plan names

The plan names are provisional within this help centre. Adjust them to match {{COMPANY}}'s actual plans.

#Access scopes

An API key specifies the range of notes it can read.

Scope Notes it can read
Personal notes notes you own / notes shared directly with you / notes in private folders shared with you
Public notes notes everyone in the workspace can see / notes in the team space

{{PRODUCT}} notes are private by default. To make a note readable under the public notes scope, it has to be in a folder everyone in the workspace can see, such as a folder in the team space. A note left in a private folder can be read only under the personal notes scope of a user who could already access it.

#Creating a personal API key

What you need first
  • to be a workspace member on the Team or Enterprise plan
  • the {{PRODUCT}} desktop app (macOS / Windows). Keys are issued from the desktop app
  • on the Enterprise plan, that an administrator has enabled the relevant scope
  1. 1

    Open the API keys screen in settings

    In the desktop app, open Settings → Connectors → API keys.

  2. 2

    Create a new key

    Click “Create new key” and choose the scopes to include in it.

  3. 3

    Generate and copy the key

    Click “Generate API Key”, copy the key shown, and register it in the system that will use it.

Check
  • the key you created appears in the list under Settings → Connectors → API keys with the scope you expected
  • with the key registered in your system, it retrieves the notes you can see in {{PRODUCT}}
Do not paste API keys anywhere

An API key is a credential that can read every note and transcript within its scope. Do not paste it directly into source code, chat tools, issue trackers or shared documents. Store it using environment variables or a secrets manager, and take care not to commit it to a repository. If there is any possibility a third party has seen it, revoke that key immediately regardless and issue a new one.

On the Enterprise plan you cannot create a key with a scope an administrator has not enabled. If the scope you want is not offered on the creation screen, check with your workspace administrator.

#Administrators controlling scopes (Enterprise plan)

  1. Settings → Workspace → General.
  2. API access for members.
  3. Click “Manage”.
  4. Choose the scopes members may use.

There are four options: personal notes only, public notes only, both, or neither. Setting it to neither means members cannot create new API keys.

#Workspace API keys

A workspace API key is managed by administrators and belongs to the workspace rather than an individual. It is available on the Team and Enterprise plans. Unlike a personal API key it does not expire and is not tied to a particular person's account, so it keeps working after the administrator who created it leaves. It suits uses where a departure must not break things, such as a permanent integration with a core system.

A workspace API key can read the following.

  • Public notes — notes everyone in the workspace can see, such as those in the team space. If an administrator has switched the workspace's allow public folders setting off, these notes are not exposed to the API.
  • Notes in spaces with API access enabled — switching “Allow API access” on when creating a space, or afterwards under Settings → Spaces, makes that space's notes readable with a workspace API key. That includes folders and subfolders under the space.

Private notes and folders falling under neither of these cannot be read with a workspace API key.

“Allow API access” is enabled by default when you create a new space. If you do not want that space's notes readable with a workspace API key, switch it off at creation or afterwards under Settings → Spaces.

Only workspace administrators can create and manage workspace API keys. The steps are as follows.

  1. 1

    Open the workspace API keys screen in settings

    In the desktop app, open Settings → Connectors → Workspace API keys.

  2. 2

    Create a new key

    Click “Create new key”.

  3. 3

    Copy the key and register it

    Copy the API key shown and register it in the system that will use it.

#Revoking a key

Personal and workspace API keys are managed on separate pages, so revoke each from its own page.

Revoking a personal API key

  1. Settings → Connectors → API keys.
  2. Find the key you want to revoke and click “Revoke”.
  3. Confirm in the dialog.

Revoking a workspace API key (administrators only)

  1. Settings → Connectors → Workspace API keys.
  2. Find the key you want to revoke and click “Revoke”.
  3. Confirm in the dialog.
Revocation cannot be undone

A revoked key is permanently invalid and moves to the “Revoked” section of the list. It cannot be restored. Integrations using it stop working, so check which systems use the key before revoking it.

#API reference

The reference covering endpoints, authentication, and example requests and responses is published in the developer documentation. For the terms on which the API and integrations may be used, see the API and platform terms of service.

#About the data involved

What the API retrieves is meeting notes and transcripts, which normally contain personal data such as attendees' names, email addresses and what they said. If you store retrieved data in your own systems, design where it is stored, how long it is kept, and who can access it in line with your own personal data handling rules.

For how to account for passing retrieved data on to another provider, see Integrations overview.

#Frequently asked questions

Q. Which plan do I need?

A. Creating API keys requires the Team or Enterprise plan.

Q. How does the API differ from MCP?

A. The API issues API keys for scripts, scheduled automation and calls from your own systems. MCP uses OAuth in a browser and is designed for interactive AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT.

Q. Can it access private notes and private folders?

A. Only where the key includes the personal notes scope and the key's owner could already see that note in {{PRODUCT}}. The public notes scope covers only notes everyone in the workspace can see.

Q. Can one key retrieve both the team's notes and my own?

A. Yes. Select both “personal notes” and “public notes” when creating the key.

Q. The API returns no notes at all

A. The API returns only notes matching the key's scope. If you are using the public notes scope, check the notes are in a folder visible to everyone in the workspace, such as one in the team space. If you are using the personal notes scope, check the key's owner can open those notes in {{PRODUCT}}.

Q. Is there a sandbox for testing?

A. Not at this time. We suggest creating a test folder and checking the behaviour against a small number of notes.

Q. Are there rate limits?

A. Yes. API keys are limited to 25 requests in a burst and 5 requests per second sustained. Whether the limit applies per user or per workspace depends on the key's scope.

Q. Are webhooks available?

A. Yes, on the Team and Enterprise plans. For registering endpoints, choosing which events to subscribe to, verifying signatures and handling retries, see the webhook guide in the developer documentation.

sharing/integrations/hub-spot.title: HubSpot integration
sharing/integrations/hub-spot.description: Setting up linking and automatic posting of notes to HubSpot deals and contacts.
sharing/integrations/hub-spot.html:
Connecting HubSpot lets you keep meeting notes against contact, company and deal records. You can send notes one at a time, or send notes in a folder automatically.

#Setting up the connection

What you need first
  • the {{PRODUCT}} desktop app (macOS / Windows). Both the connection setup and sending are done from the desktop app
  • a {{PRODUCT}} account signed in with a Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account. Consumer Gmail and Outlook.com accounts cannot be used
  • the HubSpot account to connect to, and permission to authorise that connection
  1. 1

    Open connectors in settings

    In {{PRODUCT}}'s settings (opened from your avatar at the bottom left), choose “Connectors”. HubSpot is in the list of services you can connect.

  2. 2

    Connect the HubSpot account

    Click connect on the HubSpot card and a browser opens with HubSpot's authorisation screen. Choose the account to connect and approve it, and the connection is made. Close the browser tab and return to {{PRODUCT}}.

  3. 3

    Choose the record type

    Under Settings > HubSpot, choose whether a synced meeting is created in HubSpot as a Meeting or as a Note. The default is Meeting. Choosing Meeting where you want it kept as sales activity history, and Note where it is supplementary, fits better with HubSpot's own reporting.

Check
  • Settings > HubSpot shows the connected HubSpot account and the record type
  • a HubSpot item appears at the top right when you open a note

#Sending notes one at a time

  1. Open the note you want to send and click HubSpot at the top right.
  2. Choose the contact, company or deal to link it to.
  3. Confirm, and the meeting content is linked to the record you chose.

#Sending notes in a folder automatically

Notes added to a particular folder can be saved automatically to the matching contact, company or deal.

  1. Open the folder.
  2. Click the “Integrations” button in the folder header.
  3. Switch the HubSpot item on.
  4. Choose which kind of record to link to (contact, company, deal).

Once set up, notes added to that folder are added automatically to the HubSpot records matching your criteria.

Past notes are not sent retrospectively

Automatic sending covers only notes added to the folder after you switched the integration on. Notes already in the folder beforehand are not synced. To send past notes, open each one and send it individually with the HubSpot button at the top right.

What is sent to HubSpot is the content of the AI-enhanced note. It contains attendees' names and what was said, so check that the people who can see that record in HubSpot match the people the meeting content may be shared with. How to account for sending to external services as handling of personal data is covered in Integrations overview.

#If something is not working

Q. I cannot connect to HubSpot

A. Check that you use the same email address for your {{PRODUCT}} and HubSpot accounts. With different addresses the connection can fail. Also check you are signed in to {{PRODUCT}} with a Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account.

Q. An integration that was working has suddenly stopped

A. Disconnect and reconnect from Settings > HubSpot. Where the authorisation has expired, this restores it.

Q. I cannot send a meeting to HubSpot

A. You cannot send until the AI-enhanced note has been generated. If it has not been, click the refresh icon beside “Auto” to regenerate it and try again.

Q. The share item is greyed out

A. Check the note's sharing settings. Notes set to “private” cannot be shared. Change it to a shareable setting before sending. How to set it is in Sharing controls.

Q. Notes from a folder are not appearing in HubSpot

A. Check the following in order.

  • {{PRODUCT}} matches HubSpot records using the attendees' email addresses. Where there is no matching record, nothing is created in HubSpot. Check that the attendees' email addresses are registered as contacts or companies in HubSpot.
  • Settings > HubSpot shows the most recent sync status. Where an error has occurred, the details are shown on that screen.
  • Notes already in the folder before the integration was switched on are out of scope. Send those individually.

Both the connection setup and sending are done from the desktop app a {{PRODUCT}} account signed in with a Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account. Consumer Gmail and Outlook.com accounts cannot be used the HubSpot account to connect to, and permission to authorise that connection 1 Open connectors in settings In {{PRODUCT}}'s settings (opened from your avatar at the bottom left), choose “Connectors”. HubSpot is in the list of services you can connect. 2 Connect the HubSpot account Click connect on the HubSpot card and a browser opens with HubSpot's authorisation screen. Choose the account to connect and approve it, and the connection is made. Close the browser tab and return to {{PRODUCT}}. 3 Choose the record type Under Settings > HubSpot, choose whether a synced meeting is created in HubSpot as a Meeting or as a Note . The default is Meeting. Choosing Meeting where you want it kept as sales activity history, and Note where it is supplementary, fits better with HubSpot's own reporting. Figure Screenshot: the workspace settings under Settings > HubSpot The record type options (Meeting / Note) and the most recent sync status. Check Settings > HubSpot shows the connected HubSpot account and the record type a HubSpot item appears at the top right when you open a note # Sending notes one at a time Open the note you want to send and click HubSpot at the top right. Choose the contact, company or deal to link it to. Confirm, and the meeting content is linked to the record you chose. # Sending notes in a folder automatically Notes added to a particular folder can be saved automatically to the matching contact, company or deal. Open the folder. Click the “Integrations” button in the folder header. Switch the HubSpot item on. Choose which kind of record to link to (contact, company, deal). Figure Screenshot: the folder's integration settings The integration settings opened from the folder header, with the HubSpot toggle and checkboxes for choosing the kind of record to link to. Once set up, notes added to that folder are added automatically to the HubSpot records matching your criteria. Past notes are not sent retrospectively Automatic sending covers only notes added to the folder after you switched the integration on. Notes already in the folder beforehand are not synced. To send past notes, open each one and send it individually with the HubSpot button at the top right. What is sent to HubSpot is the content of the AI-enhanced note. It contains attendees' names and what was said, so check that the people who can see that record in HubSpot match the people the meeting content may be shared with. How to account for sending to external services as handling of personal data is covered in Integrations overview . # If something is not working Q. I cannot connect to HubSpot A. Check that you use the same email address for your {{PRODUCT}} and HubSpot accounts. With different addresses the connection can fail. Also check you are signed in to {{PRODUCT}} with a Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account. Q. An integration that was working has suddenly stopped A. Disconnect and reconnect from Settings > HubSpot. Where the authorisation has expired, this restores it. Q. I cannot send a meeting to HubSpot A. You cannot send until the AI-enhanced note has been generated. If it has not been, click the refresh icon beside “Auto” to regenerate it and try again. Q. The share item is greyed out A. Check the note's sharing settings. Notes set to “private” cannot be shared. Change it to a shareable setting before sending. How to set it is in Sharing controls . Q. Notes from a folder are not appearing in HubSpot A. Check the following in order. {{PRODUCT}} matches HubSpot records using the attendees' email addresses. Where there is no matching record, nothing is created in HubSpot. Check that the attendees' email addresses are registered as contacts or companies in HubSpot. Settings > HubSpot shows the most recent sync status. Where an error has occurred, the details are shown on that screen. Notes already in the folder before the integration was switched on are out of scope. Send those individually. # Related articles Integrations overview What data each integration sends externally → Spaces and folders Creating the folder that triggers automatic sending → Attio integration Setting up a different CRM →

sharing/integrations/overview.title: Integrations overview
sharing/integrations/overview.description: The external services {{PRODUCT}} can connect to, and what data each integration sends.
sharing/integrations/overview.html:
There are times when you want meeting notes to reach the tools you already use rather than staying inside {{PRODUCT}}. Several integrations exist for that, and you can choose between sending notes manually and sending notes in a folder automatically. This article lists the services you can connect and what each integration sends out.

Note

Integrations are connected and disconnected under Connectors in the desktop app's settings (macOS / Windows). The only integration available on the free plan is Slack. The others require a paid plan. For the differences between plans, see Plans and billing.

#Services you can connect

Zapier integrationrun processes in other services automatically, triggered by a note→Notion integrationsend notes to a Notion database→Slack integrationpost a note's link and summary to a channel→Attio integrationadd notes to CRM person and company records→HubSpot integrationlink notes to contacts, companies and deals→Affinity integrationadd notes to person and company records→MCP serverlet MCP-compatible external AI tools consult your notes→APIretrieve notes and transcripts from your own systems→

The CRM integrations (Attio, HubSpot, Affinity) automatically look for the matching record in the CRM using the calendar attendees' email addresses and offer it as a suggestion. Where no record has a matching email address, no suggestion appears and no data is created.

The setting for sending notes added to a folder automatically is on the folder itself. The steps are under “Automatic posting from a folder” in Spaces and folders.

#What each integration sends externally

Before deciding which integrations to enable, check what leaves your company through each. The table below summarises what each typically sends. The details per field are in the individual articles. Fields can change when the destination service changes its own specification, so confirm the exact scope against each integration's article and the destination service's published documentation.

Destination Data sent When it is sent Can administrators restrict it
Slack the share link to the note, and the body of the AI-enhanced summary when sent manually from a note / where automatic posting is set on a folder, notes added to that folder after it was configured partly. Controlled by whether the app is added to the workspace and to each channel on Slack's side. Whether rich previews apply across the organisation is set by the {{PRODUCT}} workspace administrator
Notion the note's content (created as a page in the destination database) when a note is sent to Notion controlled by the permissions granted to the integration on Notion's side and the sharing scope of the target database
Zapier the note title, the author's name and email address, attendees' names and email addresses, calendar event details, your own notes, the AI-enhanced summary, the full transcript, and the note's share link when the Zap's trigger fires (a folder addition, or a note sent manually to Zapier) partly. The Zap's creator chooses whether to share it within the workspace. A Zap targeting a folder can only be configured by that folder's collaborators or owner
Attio the AI-enhanced note (added as a note on the target record) when sent manually from a note / where automatic sending is set on a folder, notes added to that folder after it was configured partly. Controlled by whether the Attio workspace connection is permitted
HubSpot the AI-enhanced note (created as a meeting or note record) when sent manually from a note / where automatic sending is set on a folder, notes added to that folder after it was configured partly. Controlled by whether the HubSpot account connection is permitted. A Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account is required
Affinity the AI-enhanced note (added as a note on the target record) when sent manually from a note partly. Controlled by whether API keys can be issued on Affinity's side
MCP server in response to queries from the connected AI tool: the list of notes, their bodies, attendees, folder information and transcripts each time the AI tool queries yes. On the Enterprise plan, administrators can set the scopes members are allowed; disabling both means members cannot use it
API the notes, transcripts and AI-enhanced notes within the API key's scope each time an external system makes a request yes. Available on Team and above; on the Enterprise plan administrators can set the scopes members are allowed. Whether a space is readable through the API can also be toggled per space

#What to check before sending data out

The destination services are operated by providers other than {{COMPANY}}. Meeting notes and transcripts normally contain personal data such as attendees' names, organisations, email addresses and what they said. How sending a note containing personal data to an external service should be accounted for depends on your contract with the destination and how the destination handles data. The reasoning is covered in the section on external sharing in Sharing notes and in Sharing controls. Where the destination is an overseas provider, cross-border transfer of personal data can come into play. See also Security and privacy FAQs.

Check

Before enabling an integration, check the following.

  • that you have checked, in the table above, what data that integration sends out
  • that it falls within your own personal data handling rules and the purposes of use you have published
  • that the people who can see the destination channel or record are appropriate for the content of the notes
  • that you have a plan to try it with a limited team first, check what actually gets written, and widen from there

#Data after you disconnect an integration

Disconnecting an integration does not remove data already sent to the destination. A summary posted to Slack, for example, is a Slack message in its own right, so changing the note's sharing setting to private in {{PRODUCT}} afterwards does not remove the posted text. Where sent data has to be deleted, delete it in the destination service itself.

#Related articles

Sharing notesSharing note by note without an integration→Sharing controlsDefault sharing scope, and restricting sharing outside the organisation→Spaces and foldersCreating the folder that triggers automatic sending→
