consent-security-privacy/security-privac.text: These are the questions users and IT teams ask us most often about security and privacy in {{PRODUCT}}. Use them for pre-adoption review, processor selection, and explaining the service internally. For anything specific, write to {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Note This article gives short answers. The detail of each category of security control measure and the certifications we hold are in Our security standards , and the detail of provision to third parties in foreign countries (cross-border transfer), including the destination countries, is in our Privacy policy . Our security standards The detail of our security control measures → How far you can rely on AI meeting notes The lawfulness of recording, and announcements → AI models and training data Whether data is used for training → Use in healthcare, finance and professional services Sector-specific regulation → # Where data is stored, and transfer overseas Legislation Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 28(1) (restriction on provision to third parties in foreign countries) Providing personal data to a third party in a foreign country requires the individual's prior consent as a rule. Without consent, the destination must either be a country recognised as having a level of protection equivalent to Japan's, or a party that has put in place arrangements meeting the standards set by Personal Information Protection Commission rules. These rules apply to provision accompanying delegation too. Article 27(5), which sets out the exceptions to the restriction on provision to third parties (delegation, business succession, joint use), is not among the exclusions from Article 28. Q. Where is data stored? A. The meeting notes, transcripts and account information held in {{PRODUCT}} are stored in a database in the Tokyo region. Application hosting and the encrypted backups are in the Tokyo region too. Stored data is held encrypted, and communication between devices and servers is encrypted too. Transcription and AI processing, however, are carried out by providers in the United States (see “Is personal data transferred overseas?” below). If a recording could not be uploaded, the desktop app keeps its audio on your computer so it can be sent again. Protect the device with disk encryption and screen locking. Q. Can we specify the storage region? A. Not at present, on a per-customer basis. If you have a requirement here, speak to your account representative. Q. Is personal data transferred overseas? A. Yes. Transcription (including live captions) and AI processing such as writing notes and summaries, extracting information and answering chat questions are delegated to providers located in the United States (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, ElevenLabs and AssemblyAI), and the processing takes place there. PostHog (United States), which we use for usage analytics, also receives users' account details and records of how the app is used. Personal data is therefore transferred abroad. There are three points worth understanding. The cross-border rules apply even where the provision accompanies delegation. Delegation within Japan is analysed as not constituting provision to a third party, but that exception does not operate where the recipient is a third party in a foreign country. The test is not where data is stored. Saying “the servers are in Japan, so there is no cross-border transfer” is not accurate; what matters is whether personal data is provided to a third party in a foreign country. Sending data to an inference API can be such a provision. {{COMPANY}} relies on having arrangements in place, not on consent. Obtaining individual consent from every meeting participant is impractical, so we provide data only to providers that have put in place arrangements meeting the standards set by Personal Information Protection Commission rules. A comparison of the approaches, how often we verify destinations, what happens if we stop providing data, and the scope of information provided to individuals are set out under “Provision to third parties in foreign countries” in our Privacy policy . To request that information, contact {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. Q. Where can I see the destination countries? A. The destination country is the United States. The names of the destination countries, and the measures taken in the light of an understanding of those countries' regimes, are listed in our Privacy policy . For how {{COMPANY}} goes about that, see the “Understanding the external environment” section of Our security standards . Q. Can we use it at overseas offices? A. {{PRODUCT}} can be used from outside Japan. This article and the related ones are, however, written on the basis of Japanese law. If you need to address regulation specific to a location outside Japan, speak to your account representative. # Requests relating to individuals' rights Legislation Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 33 (disclosure) / Article 34 (correction) / Article 35 (cessation of use) / Article 38 (fees) An individual may request disclosure of retained personal data, its correction, addition or deletion, the cessation of its use, its erasure or the cessation of provision to third parties, and disclosure of records of provision to third parties. For disclosure, the individual may specify provision by electromagnetic record. Under Article 35(5), cessation of use may also be requested where there is no longer a need to use the data or where a leak has occurred. Fees may be charged only for notification of the purpose of use and for disclosure, not for correction or cessation of use. Q. How do you handle disclosure, correction and cessation-of-use requests? A. Write to {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}} with documentation confirming your identity. We accept requests from statutory representatives and from authorised agents. Disclosure is made by provision of an electromagnetic record as a rule — either a download within {{PRODUCT}} or an email attachment. Tell us if you would prefer it on paper. For requests for notification of the purpose of use and for disclosure, we may charge a fee reflecting our actual costs. No fee is charged for correction or cessation-of-use requests. Q. Can I export all my own data? A. Yes. You can download your own data in one go from Settings. Workspace admins can export the whole organisation's notes (Markdown) and data (JSON), and the data about one person (JSON). Much of a disclosure request can be handled by yourself this way. Where you need disclosure of personal data not included in an export, write to {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}} marking it as a disclosure request. Q. I want to change my name or email address A. You can change it yourself in account settings. The steps are in Changing your account and email address . For fields you cannot change yourself, contact {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. No fee is charged for correction requests. Q. A meeting participant has asked me to delete what they said A. Part of a transcript cannot be deleted on its own. Move the meeting's note to the trash and delete it permanently (a note's owner or an admin can do this). The steps are in Deleting notes . If everything {{PRODUCT}} has gathered about that person has to go, an admin can delete everything about the person from their person page; the person is then recorded so that later meetings do not rebuild them. Notes and transcripts that mention the person are not deleted by this, so delete those notes too if the request requires it. Note that for meeting data held in {{PRODUCT}}, the authority to decide on deletion rests with the customer (the contracting company). A request from a meeting participant should as a rule be made to the organisation that created the record. Q. How do I delete my account and all my data? A. In the app, go to Settings → Profile → Delete account. The deletion takes place 30 days after you ask, and you can cancel it until then. Meetings placed in the organisation's folders and the like stay as the organisation's records. A whole organisation can be deleted by an admin in settings, with a 30-day grace period. If you cannot reach the app, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} and we will process it. For details see Deleting your account . # If a leak occurs Legislation Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 26(1) and (2) (reporting leaks) Where a leak, loss or damage of personal data occurs that is likely to substantially harm individuals' rights and interests, reporting to the Personal Information Protection Commission and notification of the individuals are required. For personal data handled under delegation, a processor is relieved of its own reporting duty once it has notified the delegating party. The Enforcement Regulations define four categories of reportable event: where sensitive personal information is involved, where there is a risk of financial harm, where the act was for an improper purpose, and where more than 1,000 individuals are affected. Each includes events that “may have” occurred. Q. What are your arrangements for reporting a leak? A. Where a leak, loss or damage of personal data occurs (including where it may have), {{COMPANY}} follows the Act on the Protection of Personal Information and its Enforcement Regulations. For personal data handled under delegation from a customer (such as meeting data) : we notify the customer promptly after becoming aware (as a guide, within roughly three to five days). That notification relieves {{COMPANY}} of its own duty to report to the Commission. A contract can also provide that {{COMPANY}} reports on the customer's behalf. For personal data {{COMPANY}} handles on its own account : we make a prompt initial report to the Personal Information Protection Commission and submit the full report within 30 days of becoming aware (60 days where the act was for an improper purpose). Affected individuals are notified of the outline of the event, the categories of personal data involved, the cause, any secondary harm or risk of it, and other relevant matters. “Promptly” for the initial report is a guideline benchmark; the 30 and 60 days for the full report are deadlines set by the Enforcement Regulations. Q. Does a meeting transcript raise the reporting threshold? A. Yes. Meeting transcripts can pick up sensitive personal information such as medical history or a criminal record. A leak of personal data containing sensitive personal information is reportable to the Commission even if it affects a single individual . That is what lowers the reporting threshold compared with other business SaaS. Encrypting data at rest is, among other things, a practical measure for managing that threshold. Q. Are past incidents published? # Security control measures Q. What security control measures do you take? A. {{COMPANY}} has a basic policy and handling rules for personal data in place, and implements measures following the categories set out in the guidelines under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (organisational, personnel, physical and technical security measures, and understanding the external environment). The main ones are encryption in transit and at rest, access control limiting permissions to what the work requires, capturing and retaining access records, and continuous checking for vulnerabilities. The specifics for each category are collected in Our security standards . You can use that page as-is for processor assessments and security questionnaires. # Processors and sub-processors Q. How do you supervise processors? A. Where {{COMPANY}} delegates the handling of personal data externally, we do three things. set criteria for selecting a processor and confirm the standard of their security measures before selecting them enter into a contract covering security measures, the conditions for sub-processing, and reporting duties in the event of an incident review periodically how the processor handles personal data Equivalent conditions are imposed on sub-processors. Q. Are sub-processors disclosed? A. Yes. The main sub-processors used to deliver {{PRODUCT}} are listed below. The current list, with each one's purpose, the personal data involved and where it is processed, is on our website's subprocessor list , where changes are announced at least 30 days in advance as a rule. Vercel (application hosting, temporary storage of recordings; Tokyo region) Supabase (database; Tokyo region) Wasabi (encrypted backups; Tokyo region) Anthropic, OpenAI and Google (writing notes and summaries, extracting information, answering chat questions and similar; United States) ElevenLabs and AssemblyAI (transcription and live captions; United States) PostHog (usage analytics; United States) Stripe (payments) and Resend (sending email) Q. Is {{COMPANY}} a processor or a third party? A. For customers' meeting data, {{COMPANY}} acts as a party to whom the customer (the contracting company) has delegated the handling of personal data. Provision accompanying delegation is not provision to a third party, so the customer does not need to obtain third-party provision consent from meeting participants. Instead, the customer supervises us as a processor. By contrast, where you use {{PRODUCT}}'s integrations to send a note to another service, the destination is not {{COMPANY}}'s processor but a separate provider. That send can constitute provision to a third party. For details see Integrations overview . Q. Do you have a data processing addendum (DPA)? A. If your organisation needs data processing terms, contact {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}. For your meeting data, your organisation is the business handling the personal information, and {{COMPANY}} handles it on your behalf as a processor. # Certifications and audits Q. Which certifications do you hold? A. {{COMPANY}} does not currently hold any certification or third-party assessment. The position on each scheme is collected in one place, in the “Certifications and third-party assessments” table in Our security standards . Please check that table for ISMS certification (ISO/IEC 27001), ISO/IEC 27017, ISO/IEC 27018, the Privacy Mark, a SOC 2 Type II report and ISMAP. The schemes differ in nature. ISO/IEC 27001 is a third-party certification; ISO/IEC 27017 is an add-on to ISMS certification; ISO/IEC 27018 is a code of practice; the Privacy Mark is a domestic accreditation scheme run by JIPDEC; SOC 2 Type II is an audit firm's report, not a certification. ISMAP is an assessment scheme for government procurement, and anyone can check registration on the public list at the ISMAP portal. {{PRODUCT}} is not currently on the ISMAP cloud service list. We never describe ourselves as “compliant with”, “equivalent to” or “meeting the criteria of” a scheme we do not hold. Whatever the certification position, the controls we implement are described specifically in Our security standards . Q. Will you complete an audit or a security questionnaire? A. Yes. Email {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the form and the deadline. We will tell you what we can answer and whether a non-disclosure agreement is needed first. Material you can pass to your IT department includes this article, Our security standards and Network troubleshooting . Q. Our internal security product has blocked {{PRODUCT}} A. Network troubleshooting lists the destinations that need adding to an allowlist, and the symptoms that appear when traffic is blocked or rewritten. Pass that page to your IT department. It also helps, when explaining the service in a review, that {{PRODUCT}} sends no recording bot into meetings, runs on the user's own device, and encrypts its traffic. Q. Is there a contact for reporting vulnerabilities? A. {{SECURITY_EMAIL}}. For vulnerabilities found in Japan, we also accept reports through the Information Security Early Warning Partnership run by the Information-technology Promotion Agency (IPA). # The Telecommunications Business Act Legislation Telecommunications Business Act, Article 27-12 (notification regarding instructions to transmit information) Where a party intends to instruct a user's device to transmit information about the user to a third party, it must notify the user in advance, or put in a state where the user can readily ascertain, the content of the information transmitted, the name of the party handling it at the destination, and the purpose for which it is used. The services covered are set out in the Enforcement Regulations as four categories: services mediating others' communications, services transmitting at the request of unspecified users, search services, and services making content available for viewing by unspecified users. Q. How do you comply with the external transmission rules? A. {{PRODUCT}}'s website, web app and desktop app may send some information from your device to servers operated by providers other than {{COMPANY}}, for analytics and error detection. The information sent, the names of the providers handling it at the destination, and the purposes of use are listed on our “Disclosures regarding external transmission” page. If you would rather it were not sent, you can opt out by the method given on that page. Meeting audio, transcribed text, and the body of the notes {{PRODUCT}} generates are not part of that analytics transmission. They are handled only to the extent needed to provide {{PRODUCT}}. Q. Are you intercepting communications? A. The {{PRODUCT}} desktop app captures the meeting audio playing on your computer and your microphone audio inside the computer itself. It is not a mechanism by which {{COMPANY}} sits in the meeting service's communication path intercepting the call. The audio captured is sent to {{PRODUCT}}'s servers for transcription and summary generation. We treat the parts of {{PRODUCT}} that mediate exchanges between users — sharing and notification features — as subject to Article 4 of the Telecommunications Business Act (protection of secrecy). {{COMPANY}}'s officers and employees do not acquire, use or disclose information subject to the secrecy of communications learned in the course of their work, except where required by law or where there is other justifiable cause. That obligation continues after employment ends. # Recording, consent and audio Q. Is recording a meeting a criminal offence? A. The Penal Code contains no provision punishing the recording of a conversation as such. Article 133 (opening sealed letters) covers opening a sealed letter, and Article 134 (disclosure of secrets) covers disclosure by members of a limited list of professions such as doctors and lawyers; neither applies to recording a meeting. The Act on Wiretapping for Criminal Investigation likewise governs interception carried out by investigative authorities under a warrant issued by a judge, and does not apply to recording by a meeting's participants. For the full analysis, see How far you can rely on AI meeting notes . Q. Is consent required from everyone present? A. Japanese law contains no provision generally requiring consent from everyone present to record a meeting. The legal obligations that do arise are: notifying or publishing the purpose of use of the personal information acquired; obtaining the individual's consent where sensitive personal information is acquired; and obtaining the individual's consent where the case amounts to provision to a third party. That said, {{COMPANY}} strongly recommends telling participants that recording and transcription are taking place, even where there is no legal obligation. Wording you can use as-is is in How far you can rely on AI meeting notes . For the notice {{PRODUCT}} shows when you start recording, which you can paste into the meeting chat, see About telling people you are recording . Q. Does a recording bot join the meeting? A. No. {{PRODUCT}} runs on the user's own device and captures audio directly from the microphone and system audio. No unfamiliar account appears in the participant list for others to see, and the meeting host does not need to allow a bot to join. Q. Is the audio stored? A. Recorded audio is sent to {{PRODUCT}}'s servers (Tokyo region) for transcription and deleted as soon as transcription is finished. Audio left over from an upload that failed partway is deleted within 24 hours. What is stored is the transcript text. For transcription and live captions, the audio is also sent to providers in the United States (ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI and OpenAI). If a recording could not be uploaded, the desktop app keeps its audio on your computer so it can be sent again. Q. Can conversations be recorded unintentionally? A. {{PRODUCT}} records when you take the action to start recording. If you have turned on “Start recording automatically” in settings (it is off by default), however, recording starts without a confirmation when the call of a meeting on your calendar starts (desktop apps). Calls with no scheduled meeting still ask first. Recording can also continue where a meeting overruns or you forget to stop it. Press [Stop] when the meeting finishes. The steps are in Sharing controls . Q. Can an administrator or a colleague see my private notes? A. Admins can open private notes too, for managing the organisation. When an admin opens a private note, it is recorded in the audit log and the note's owner is notified. A colleague who is not an admin cannot see your private notes unless the note is in a folder they belong to, shared with them, has link sharing turned on, or they attended the meeting. Q. consent-security-privacy/sharing-control.title: Sharing controls
consent-security-privacy/sharing-control.description: Who can see a note, how to share it, what administrators can do, and what to check before content leaves your organisation.
consent-security-privacy/sharing-control.html:
A {{PRODUCT}} note starts out private. Until it is shared, it can be opened only by the person who created it, members of the same workspace who are attendees of that meeting, and admins. This article covers how to widen who can see a note, what admins can do, and the legal points to check when a note's content leaves your organisation.

Sharing notesThe basics of sharing→Spaces and foldersOrganising notes for a team→Security and privacy FAQsWho can see what→Automatic transcript deletionSetting a retention period→
Note

Sharing works the same in the web app and the desktop app (macOS / Windows): use Share at the top right of the note.

#Who can see a note

State Who can view it
Private (the default) the person who created it, members of the same workspace who are attendees of the meeting, and admins
Placed in a folder (space) the members of that space. In the default space, everyone in the workspace except guests
Shared with a member the people you share it with
Link sharing turned on members of the same workspace who have the link (guests excepted). View only

There are no public links that let people outside the organisation, or people who are not signed in, open a note. New notes and recordings start out private on every plan.

#Changing an individual note's scope

  1. 1

    Open the note

    Open the note whose scope you want to change.

  2. 2

    Click Share

    Click Share at the top right (Shared for a note that is already shared) to open the sharing menu. People with access lists who can see it now.

  3. 3

    Choose people or a folder

    Search by name, email or folder to share with a member or place the note in a folder. To pass it on as a link, switch the link scope to everyone in the workspace with the link and press Copy link.

A note's sharing can be changed by its owner and by admins. Changes are recorded in the audit log.

#The default for new notes

New notes and recordings always start out private. There is no setting to change the default scope. Meetings imported from a calendar are also created private, and members of the same workspace who are attendees can see them.

#Sharing through folders

Create a space for a team or a deal and place notes in it, and its members can see them all. Space members have one of two roles: editor (can work with notes and recordings) or viewer (read only). For details see Spaces and folders.

#Organisation-wide restrictions

There is no setting to put an organisation-wide ceiling on sharing. Even with link sharing on, only members of the workspace can open a note. If you want limits on placing notes in folders or using link sharing, set them as internal rules.

#What administrators can see

Item What an administrator can do
Members' private notes open them, for managing the organisation. Opening one is recorded in the audit log and the note's owner is notified
Notes placed in spaces open them
An individual note's sharing change it, as the owner can
Audit log review it under Settings → Workspace → Audit log. It does not contain note content

Open members' private notes only when managing the organisation requires it. The note's owner is told that you opened it.

#Where this sits among security control measures

The settings above correspond to two of the security control measures required by the Act on the Protection of Personal Information. For the whole picture, see Our security standards.

Category What it corresponds to
Organisational security measures an administrator setting and maintaining the scope of who may view which notes
Technical security measures restricting access by those without permission, technically, through the sharing scope setting

Personnel security measures (training and confidentiality obligations), physical security measures, and understanding the external environment are described as measures on {{COMPANY}}'s side in Our security standards.

#What to check before sharing outside your organisation

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 27(1) and (5) (restriction on provision to third parties)

Providing personal data to a third party requires the individual's prior consent as a rule. Provision accompanying delegation, provision accompanying a business succession, and joint use meeting the stated requirements are treated as not involving a “third party”.

Meeting notes and transcripts contain personal information such as attendees' names, organisations and what they said. Sharing that with someone outside your own organisation can constitute provision to a third party. The following three are treated differently under the rules, so keep them distinct.

Form of sharing Analysis
Sharing within your own workspace handling within the organisation; not provision to a third party. Check it falls within the purposes of use you have specified
{{COMPANY}} holding the data {{COMPANY}} acts as a party to whom handling has been delegated; not provision to a third party
Exporting a note to an external service, sending it through an integration, or sending it by email the recipient is a separate party, not {{COMPANY}}'s processor. This can constitute provision to a third party

Where the third case applies, responsibility for securing lawfulness rests with whoever did the sharing — usually the user's employer. Before sharing, check it against your own personal data handling rules and that it falls within the purposes of use you have specified. For integrations with external services, see also Integrations overview.

#Handling link sharing

Link sharing lets only members of the same workspace who have the link open the note; people outside the organisation cannot. A note's content leaves the organisation when it is exported to Slack, Notion, Google Docs and similar, or sent by email. Exporting and sending can be done only by people who can edit the note, ask for confirmation for a private note, and are recorded in the audit log.

When exporting notes from client meetings, recruitment interviews and meetings with external attendees, check where they are going and who will see them.

#What remains after you stop sharing

Setting the scope back to private stops the link being viewable from that point on. If the recipient copied or exported the note's content while it was shared, however, that copy is not under {{COMPANY}}'s control. Ending sharing does not recover what has already reached them.

The same applies to data sent to an external service through an integration. Disconnecting the integration leaves data at the destination, which has to be deleted there.

#If something is not working

  • I cannot change the sharing: only a note's owner and admins can change it. A note in the trash cannot be changed until it is restored.
  • The person I shared with cannot open it: link sharing works only for members of the same workspace, not for guests or people outside the organisation. Someone who belongs to several workspaces is offered a switch to the workspace the note is in.
  • I want to show the content to someone outside the organisation: there are no public links. Export the note to Slack, Notion, Google Docs and similar, or send it by email.

consent-security-privacy/transcript-auto.title: Automatic transcript deletion
consent-security-privacy/transcript-auto.description: Setting your organisation's retention period, what happens to data past it, and what remains after deletion.
consent-security-privacy/transcript-auto.html:
{{PRODUCT}} keeps notes (including their transcripts), imported emails and chat messages for a retention period set for each organisation, and deletes what is past it automatically. Retention applies to every organisation, and the default is 12 months. This article covers setting the retention period, what happens to data past it, and what remains after deletion.

Note

The default retention period is 12 months. A workspace admin can choose 6, 12, 24 or 36 months, or keep forever (no automatic deletion). Meeting audio is deleted as soon as it has been transcribed, whatever the retention period.

Sharing controlsWho can see a note→Deleting notesDeleting note by note→Deleting your accountWhat happens to data when you close your account→Security and privacy FAQsQuestions about retention→

#Setting the retention period (admins)

The retention period is a workspace setting, and only a workspace admin can change it. Individual members cannot set a different period for their own notes.

  1. 1

    Open settings

    Sign in to {{PRODUCT}} and open Settings.

  2. 2

    Open the workspace's General page

    Open Workspace → General.

  3. 3

    Choose the retention period

    Under Data retention, choose 6, 12, 24 or 36 months, or keep forever (no automatic deletion).

  4. 4

    Save

    Once saved, the new period is used from the next automatic run (every 15 minutes). The change is recorded in the audit log.

Check
  • the retention period is longer than the period the business refers to the records
  • notes you want to keep have been exported before shortening the period
  • the period matches the record retention period set in your internal rules
Note

Shortening the period moves notes that are now past it to the trash, a batch at a time. Notes can be restored from the trash for 30 days, but imported emails and chat messages cannot be restored.

#What happens to data past the period

Data Counted from Once past the period
Notes (including transcripts, summaries and your own notes) the date of the meeting moved to the trash automatically. They can be restored from the trash for 30 days and are then permanently deleted
Imported emails the date sent permanently deleted automatically
Chat messages (Slack and others) the date of the messages permanently deleted automatically

Information that rested only on those notes, emails or chat messages (such as facts about people and companies) is deleted with them. Information that also rests on other meetings or sources stays as long as those remain.

The deletion runs a little at a time every 15 minutes, so when there is a lot to process, such as the first time the period is shortened, it can take a while to finish.

#What to know

Please note

Notes, emails and chat messages that have been permanently deleted cannot be restored.

Effect Detail
Retention applies to every organisation the default is 12 months. Unless keep forever is chosen, data past the period is deleted automatically
Notes can be restored from the trash for 30 days a restored note whose meeting date is still older than the period goes back to the trash on the next run. To keep it, lengthen the period first, then restore it
Emails and chat cannot be restored imported emails and chat messages past the period are permanently deleted without going through the trash
Notes being written wait a meeting whose note is still being generated is processed once generation has finished
Deletion runs automatically there is no confirmation each time. The number of items processed is recorded in the audit log
What was exported stays notes exported to Slack, Notion, Google Docs and so on, and anything written to a CRM, stay where they were sent

#What you see after deletion

  • notes past the period no longer appear in lists or search, and go to the trash
  • a note in the trash can be opened read-only and restored by its owner and by admins. Other members cannot see it
  • a permanently deleted note disappears from the trash too. Information that rested only on it is no longer used in chat answers or briefs

#What remains after deletion

Even once data has gone from the screen, the following remain. These are the parts that need explaining in processor reviews and audits.

What remains Purpose Until
Backups recovery from failures kept encrypted in the Tokyo region for 30 days. Deleted data disappears from the backups within 30 days
Audit log investigating misuse, recording actions does not contain the body of notes or transcripts. A record of a deleted note's title and date, and counts, is kept
Usage cost records totalling costs records of what AI processing cost, without meeting content
Data outside retention — web research results about external participants, imports such as business cards, and information that also rests on other meetings are not deleted by retention
Recordings that failed to upload sending again if a recording could not be uploaded, the desktop app keeps its audio on your computer so it can be sent again

#Relationship to the Act on the Protection of Personal Information

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 22 (ensuring accuracy of data, etc.)

This provides that where there is no longer a need to use personal data, a business must endeavour to erase it without delay. It is a duty of effort, but keeping records indefinitely with no retention period drifts away from its intent. Automatic deletion is the feature that addresses that duty in practice.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 35(5) (cessation of use)

An individual may also request cessation of use or erasure where there is no longer a need to use the personal data, where a leak has occurred, or where their rights or legitimate interests may otherwise be harmed. Automatic deletion after a meeting, and erasure on account closure, function as practical preparation for such requests.

When deciding a retention period, start from how long the business needs the record. The period until minutes are finalised, the period during which an audit or acceptance check might refer to them, and record retention periods set in contracts with clients are all relevant.

#Where this sits among security control measures

Setting a retention period corresponds to the following categories of security control measure required by the Act on the Protection of Personal Information. For the whole picture and {{COMPANY}}'s own measures, see Our security standards.

Category What it corresponds to
Organisational security measures setting the retention period as policy, and confirming data is deleted once the period passes
Technical security measures the mechanism that automatically deletes notes, emails and chat messages past the retention period
Personnel security measures making the retention and deletion practice known to employees
Physical security measures erasing data by a method that prevents recovery when equipment and electronic media are disposed of
Understanding the external environment where processing is delegated outside Japan, understanding that country's regime and agreeing limits on retention

#Frequently asked questions

Q. Can a deleted note be restored?

A. A note moved to the trash because it was past the period can be restored from the trash by its owner or an admin within 30 days. If its meeting date is still older than the period, though, it goes back to the trash on the next run, so lengthen the period first. Permanently deleted notes, and emails and chat messages deleted because they were past the period, cannot be restored.

Q. Can I delete only the transcript and keep the note?

A. No. Retention applies to the whole note (including its transcript, summary and your own notes). There is also no way to delete part of a transcript.

Q. Can automatic deletion be stopped?

A. If a workspace admin sets the retention period to keep forever, nothing is deleted automatically. Data already permanently deleted is not restored by changing the setting back.

Q. Can I set a different period for my own notes?

A. No. The retention period applies to the whole workspace. If you have a particular need, speak to your workspace admin.

Q. Is there guidance on choosing a retention period?

A. There is no uniform legal standard. Start from how long the business refers to those records, and factor in whether you handle meetings where sensitive personal information is likely to arise. In departments handling sensitive matters — healthcare, HR, legal — we suggest a shorter period, or deciding which meetings are not recorded at all.

Q. A meeting participant has asked for deletion

A. Move the meeting's note to the trash and delete it permanently (a note's owner or an admin can do this). Part of a transcript cannot be deleted on its own. What {{PRODUCT}} has gathered about that person can be deleted in one go by an admin from the person's page. For meeting data held in {{PRODUCT}}, the authority to decide on deletion rests with the customer (the contracting company). A request from the individual should as a rule be made to the organisation that created the record.

#If something is not working

  • I cannot change the retention period in settings: only a workspace admin can change it. Ask your admin.
  • I shortened the period but old notes are still there: deletion runs a little at a time every 15 minutes, and a meeting whose note is still being generated waits. Check again after a while.
  • There are notes in the trash I did not put there: notes whose meeting date is older than the retention period move to the trash automatically. They can be restored within 30 days (to keep one, lengthen the period first).

#Related articles

Deleting notesDeleting note by note→Deleting your accountWhat happens to data after you close your account→Exporting notesExporting before deletion→Sharing controlsSetting who can view→Our security standardsThe whole picture of our security control measures→

consent-security-privacy/transparency-so.title: Making recording notices a rule in your organisation (for admins)
consent-security-privacy/transparency-so.description: What admins can do today about telling people they are being recorded: internal rules, making the notice known, and related settings.
consent-security-privacy/transparency-so.html:
{{PRODUCT}} has no way to send a recording notice to a whole organisation centrally, or to force a post in the meeting chat or a mark on the camera feed. Because {{PRODUCT}} sends no recording bot into meetings, it cannot post in the meeting chat, edit invitations or email participants. Notice is given by the person recording, using the notice shown when recording starts. What an admin can do is set how notice is given as an internal rule, make the notice known, and put the related settings in order. This article covers how to go about that, with internal announcement templates and likely questions and answers.

#What admins can do today

What you can do Detail
Set how notice is given as an internal rule decide which of a spoken announcement, pasting the notice into the chat, and a line in the invitation are mandatory. Draft clauses are in How far you can rely on AI meeting notes (a guide for teams)
Make the notice known tell people about the notice shown when recording starts (below) and how to use it
Decide on “Start recording automatically” each user's own setting, off by default. There is no setting for an admin to turn it on or off for everyone, so decide in your internal rules whether it may be used
Decide on live captions with live captions on (Settings → Workspace → General), the audio of a recording is also streamed in real time to ElevenLabs / AssemblyAI (United States) for captions. Consider whether to cover that in what you tell participants and staff
Decide the data retention period set how long records are kept under Settings → Workspace → General → Data retention (12 months by default). See Automatic transcript deletion

The notice shown when recording starts reads as follows. Its wording cannot be changed.

この会議は {{PRODUCT}} で録音・文字起こしし、議事録を作っています。音声は文字起こしの後に削除します。

This call is being recorded and transcribed with {{PRODUCT}} to take notes. The audio is deleted after transcription.

#There is no centrally deployed notice

{{PRODUCT}}'s notice is only the card shown on the device where recording started. There is no setting for an admin to switch a notice on for everyone, or to stop users skipping it. {{PRODUCT}} does not record whether the notice was sent, so an admin cannot check that either. Making notice a rule rests on internal rules and on telling people.

#Using your meeting app's own notices

Zoom and Microsoft Teams have features of their own, separate from {{PRODUCT}}, that display a notice of their own wording when a meeting starts or is joined. These are administration features provided by those companies, and they are configured by your own organisation, not by {{COMPANY}}. They can be used alongside {{PRODUCT}}'s notice where you want the same wording company-wide, or a uniform notice that covers tools other than {{PRODUCT}}.

  • Zoom: an account owner or administrator can set a custom disclaimer shown on joining. The title and body are editable, and you can target it at participants inside your organisation, outside it, or both. Plan conditions apply.
  • Microsoft Teams: an IT administrator can change the wording of the in-meeting recording and transcription notice, and the privacy policy URL shown to participants.

These are configured in each platform's admin console; {{COMPANY}} cannot configure them on your behalf. Deciding what notice to give is a matter for the organisation using the product.

#How to go about it

  1. 1

    Decide the notice rule

    for internal and external meetings, decide which of a spoken announcement, pasting the notice, and a line in the invitation are mandatory.

  2. 2

    Decide on “Start recording automatically”

    decide which departments or kinds of meeting may use it. Ask users who turn it on to say it out loud at the start of meetings as well.

  3. 3

    Check retention and sharing

    check the data retention period, and how notes are placed in folders and shared.

  4. 4

    Tell people

    use the templates below to announce the rule and how to use the notice.

  5. 5

    Check how it is working

    check periodically that notice is being given as the rule says. {{PRODUCT}} does not record whether notice was given, so ask users.

#Internal announcement templates

Two templates you can use as they are: one for email and one for an intranet post. Replace the parts in 〔　〕 with your own details.

#For email

Subject: Please tell participants when you record a meeting (from 〔start date〕)

To all staff

This is 〔sending department〕. From 〔start date〕, the following rule applies when recording meetings with {{PRODUCT}}, which we use for meeting notes.

What we ask of you When you start recording, a notice appears above the recording button. Press Copy and paste it into the meeting chat. In meetings with external attendees, say it out loud at the start of the meeting as well. 〔If a line should also go in invitations, add it here〕

If a participant objects Stop recording there and then. If you are asked to delete the record, contact 〔contact department〕.

These records are not used for attendance management or performance reviews We do not tally who held which meetings when, or use the records to evaluate individuals. The rules of use are set out in 〔name of internal policy〕.

If anything is unclear, contact 〔contact department and address〕.

#For an intranet post

Tell participants when you record a meeting

From 〔start date〕, when you record a meeting with {{PRODUCT}}, paste the notice shown when recording starts into the meeting chat. In meetings with external attendees, say it out loud at the start as well. The rule is there so participants know a record is being kept, and to avoid misunderstandings later.

  • Who: all staff in 〔department〕
  • Starts: 〔start date〕
  • Rules of use: 〔name of internal policy〕
  • Contact: 〔contact department and address〕

If a participant objects to being recorded, stop recording there and then. How to do it is described at 〔URL of the help centre page〕.

#Likely questions and answers

Questions likely to come from users or from employee representatives, with outline answers. Adjust them to your own rules.

Q. Why are meetings being recorded?

A. To keep accurate minutes and share what was discussed with members who could not attend. The aims are to cut the time spent producing minutes and to keep a record of what was said so decisions can be traced. It is not for monitoring individual employees.

Q. Can I refuse to be recorded?

A. Make it the practice that recording stops there and then when a participant objects. If deletion of what has been recorded is requested, delete that meeting's note (part of a transcript cannot be deleted on its own). For meetings with external attendees, we recommend stating in your internal rules that recording always stops when someone objects. Whether employees can ask for recording to stop in meetings they attend is for each company's rules to decide.

Q. Will records be used in performance reviews?

A. We recommend expressly prohibiting use for performance review, attendance management or any other monitoring of individual employees in your internal rules. Include a clause prohibiting use beyond the stated purpose, and configure viewing to be limited to meeting attendees and project members.

Q. Who can see the records?

A. A note starts out private and can be seen by the person who recorded it, members of our side who are attendees of the meeting, and admins. Placing it in a folder or sharing it with members widens who can see it. When an admin opens a private note, it is recorded in the audit log and the note's owner is notified. For details see Sharing controls.

Q. How long are records kept?

A. For the retention period your organisation has set. The default is 12 months, and an admin can choose 6, 12, 24 or 36 months, or keep forever. See Automatic transcript deletion and align it with the retention period in your internal rules. Meeting audio is deleted as soon as it has been transcribed.

Q. Can it be used for occupational health or HR interviews?

A. For interviews where sensitive personal information such as health or medical history may come up, we recommend not using it as a rule. Where its use is unavoidable, obtain the individual's prior consent. The Act on the Protection of Personal Information requires the individual's consent, as a rule, for acquiring sensitive personal information.

Q. Do we need consent from external attendees every time?

A. Japanese law contains no provision generally requiring consent from everyone present in order to record a meeting. For details see How far you can rely on AI meeting notes (a guide for teams). Giving notice is, however, strongly recommended. Where a contract with a client or industry practice requires individual consent, follow that.

Q. Can we check whether notice was given?

A. No. {{PRODUCT}} does not record whether the notice was sent. Make notice a rule through internal rules and by telling people.

#Points to note as monitoring of employees

This bears on trust between employer and employees

If you are introducing ongoing recording and transcription of meetings employees attend, consider its place in your internal rules. The Personal Information Protection Commission's guideline Q&A sets out points to bear in mind when monitoring employees: (i) specify the purpose of the monitoring in advance, set it down in internal rules and make it clear to employees; (ii) designate who is responsible and what authority they have; (iii) establish the rules for how it is done in advance and make sure those operating it understand them; and (iv) check that it is being carried out properly in accordance with those rules. Notifying and consulting a labour union, and informing employees, are also regarded as desirable.

Where rules on recording and transcribing meetings apply across the company, Article 89 of the Labour Standards Act may require them to go into the work rules. When amending work rules, Article 90 requires you to hear the opinion of the union representing a majority of workers at the workplace, or, failing that, a person representing a majority of the workers.

LegislationLabour Standards Act, Article 90 (procedure for preparation)

In preparing or amending work rules, the employer must hear the opinion of the union organised by a majority of the workers at the workplace, or, where there is none, of a person representing a majority of the workers. Where rules on the use of a meeting recording tool go into the work rules, or into internal rules made under them, this procedure has to be followed.

Please note

Prohibiting covert recording in the workplace through the work rules is generally considered possible in itself, but there is a body of opinion questioning the validity of a blanket prohibition extending to recording done by a victim of harassment to preserve evidence, and treating it as a disciplinary matter. When setting internal rules on recording, check with your legal department or external counsel.

consent-security-privacy/transparency-so.html:
When you start recording, {{PRODUCT}} shows a short notice for you to give the other side. {{PRODUCT}} never posts in the meeting chat by itself, so paste the notice yourself or read it out. This article covers when the notice appears, how to paste it into the meeting chat, how to open the card again, sample wording for different situations, and what to do when a participant objects.

Note

The notice card appears when you start recording in the desktop app (macOS / Windows) or in a browser on your computer (Chrome / Edge).

#When the notice card appears

  • when you start recording on this device. A card headed “Let the other side know you're recording” opens above the recording pill
  • for a recording started by “Start recording automatically”, the first time the note is shown
  • the card opens by itself only once per recording. Reopening the note during the same recording does not open it again
  • it does not appear when the recording is being made on another device or by another member. Whoever is recording should tell the others

#Pasting the notice into the meeting chat

  1. 1

    Start recording

    Press Start recording in the note. A card headed “Let the other side know you're recording” opens above the recording pill.

  2. 2

    Press Copy

    Both lines of the notice, Japanese and English, are copied together.

  3. 3

    Paste it into the meeting chat

    Paste it into the chat of your meeting app (Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams and so on) and send it. In a meeting with no chat, read the notice out.

  4. 4

    Close the card

    Close the card with the × at the top right. Recording carries on.

The notice reads:

この会議は {{PRODUCT}} で録音・文字起こしし、議事録を作っています。音声は文字起こしの後に削除します。

This call is being recorded and transcribed with {{PRODUCT}} to take notes. The audio is deleted after transcription.

Note

{{PRODUCT}} does not record whether the notice was sent, and recording never waits for it.

#Opening the card again

Press the speaker button on the recording pill (Tell them) to open the card again, for example when someone joins partway through.

#Sample notice wording

If you want wording suited to the situation instead of the notice {{PRODUCT}} shows, use the samples below. The longer the message posted in meeting chat, the less it is read. One or two sentences with only what is needed works best in practice. The wording below can be copied as-is. For wider situations — a line for a meeting invitation, draft internal policy clauses — see How far you can rely on AI meeting notes (a guide for teams).

#1. For internal meetings (casual, polite form)

この会議は議事録作成のため、{{PRODUCT}}で文字起こしをしています。不都合があれば言ってください。

Wording for a short regular meeting or a discussion within a team. For meetings held with the same people each time, this length sits about right.

#2. For external and customer meetings (formal, concise)

本日の打ち合わせは、議事録作成のため{{PRODUCT}}で録音・文字起こしをしております。ご都合が悪い場合はお知らせください、停止いたします。

Saying explicitly that you can stop makes it easier for the other party to ask. If they do ask, stop recording there and then.

#3. For a first sales meeting (covering purpose and retention)

本日の商談は、社内での内容共有と議事録作成のために録音・文字起こしをしております。記録は弊社内でのみ利用し、〔保存期間の月数〕か月で削除いたします。ご希望があれば停止いたします。

With someone you are meeting for the first time, covering what the record is for and how long it is kept is reassuring. Put the retention period your organisation has set, as a number, at 〔保存期間の月数〕. You can check the retention setting under Automatic transcript deletion.

#4. For meetings with English speakers (Japanese and English)

この会議は議事録作成のため文字起こしをしています。ご不都合があればお知らせください。/ This meeting is being transcribed for meeting notes. Please let me know if you'd prefer we stop.

The Japanese and English are separated by a slash to fit on one line. Depending on who is in the meeting, putting the English first can get it read more reliably.

Tip

Where you would rather not name the tool, you can replace “{{PRODUCT}}” in the wording with something like “an automatic transcription tool”. What matters is not the tool's name but two things: that a record is being kept, and that it can be stopped.

#When a participant objects

If a participant objects, stop recording there and then. Press Stop on the recording pill; recording stops and the note is made from what was recorded so far. There is no way to pause a recording.

If you are asked to delete what has already been recorded, delete the note. Part of a transcript cannot be deleted on its own. A note can be permanently deleted by its owner or an admin. The steps are in Deleting and restoring notes. Options for carrying on after stopping (switching to typed notes, stopping only for a sensitive item and so on) are set out in How far you can rely on AI meeting notes (a guide for teams).

Please note

Do not use {{PRODUCT}} to record a conversation you are not part of. Leaving a device in a meeting room while you step out, or continuing to record while the other party is away, means you are no longer recording as a party to the conversation, and civil liability becomes possible. For guidance, see How far you can rely on AI meeting notes (a guide for teams).

#If “Start recording automatically” is on

If you turn on “Start recording automatically” in settings (it is off by default), recording starts without a confirmation when the call of a scheduled meeting starts (desktop apps). The other side's voice is then recorded without a confirmation too, so say it out loud at the start of the meeting and paste the notice shown in the note into the chat as well. Calls with no scheduled meeting still ask first.

#If something is not working

  • The card does not appear: it opens by itself only once per recording. Open it with the speaker button on the recording pill. If the recording is being made on another device, the card appears there.
  • Copy does not work: your browser settings may block access to the clipboard. Select the notice text on the card and copy it, or read it out.
  • The meeting has no chat: on a phone call or in person, read the notice out.

consent-security-privacy/transparency-so.html:
{{PRODUCT}} does not send a recording bot into meetings. It therefore never posts in the meeting chat, overlays anything on your camera feed, edits the meeting invitation or emails participants. Only the person recording can tell the others that they are being recorded. To make that easy, {{PRODUCT}} shows a notice when you start recording. This article sets out the means of giving notice that {{PRODUCT}} provides, and the methods you can combine with it.

Note

The notice card appears when you start recording in the desktop app (macOS / Windows) or in a browser on your computer (Chrome / Edge).

#Where the notice sits

Japanese law has no general prohibition on recording meetings or calls. Recording and transcribing a meeting you are yourself part of is generally understood not to be unlawful. The notice described here is therefore not a procedure for obtaining legal consent; it is there to let participants know what is happening. Think of it as the means by which your internal rules, or an arrangement with a client, are put into practice. Giving notice makes “nobody told me” far less likely afterwards, and makes it easier to explain yourself when you share the record of a meeting.

For the legal picture — when consent is required under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information and where the position is merely a recommendation — see How far you can go with AI minutes (a guide for teams). This article covers only the means of giving notice that {{PRODUCT}} provides, and how to use them.

Note

For meetings with people from outside your organisation, or a first sales conversation, we recommend saying a word at the start of the meeting as well as pasting the notice. Chat gets missed, and on a phone call or in person there is no chat panel at all.

#What {{PRODUCT}} provides

When What appears Who sees it
When you start recording a card headed “Let the other side know you're recording” opens above the recording pill, with the notice in Japanese and English and a Copy button the person who started recording on that device
While recording the speaker button on the recording pill (Tell them) opens the card again the person recording on that device
Before a scheduled meeting starts the “Record this meeting?” card shown in the browser says “Let the other party know you are recording” people with {{PRODUCT}} open in a browser on their computer
The “Start recording automatically” setting the setting's description tells you to let the other side know you are recording the person who turns the setting on

#The notice shown when recording starts

When you start recording, the notice below appears above the recording pill. Because the other side's language is unknown, it is shown in both Japanese and English, whatever language your screen is in.

この会議は {{PRODUCT}} で録音・文字起こしし、議事録を作っています。音声は文字起こしの後に削除します。

This call is being recorded and transcribed with {{PRODUCT}} to take notes. The audio is deleted after transcription.

Copy puts both lines on the clipboard; paste them into the meeting chat. In a meeting with no chat, read it out. The card opens by itself only once per recording, and does not appear when the recording is being made on another device or by another member; in that case, whoever is recording should tell the others.

{{PRODUCT}} does not record whether the notice was sent, and recording never waits for it.

#Reminders before meetings and for automatic recording

With {{PRODUCT}} open in a browser on your computer, a “Record this meeting?” card appears before a scheduled meeting starts, reminding you to “Let the other party know you are recording”.

If you turn on “Start recording automatically” in settings (it is off by default), recording starts without a confirmation when the call of a scheduled meeting starts (desktop apps). Because the other side's voice is then recorded without a confirmation, the setting's description also tells you to let them know. A recording started automatically still opens the notice card the first time the note is shown.

#Your meeting app's own notices

Zoom and Microsoft Teams have features of their own, separate from {{PRODUCT}}, that display a notice of their own wording when a meeting starts or is joined. These are administration features provided by those companies, and they are configured by your own organisation, not by {{COMPANY}}. They can be used alongside {{PRODUCT}}'s notice where you want the same wording company-wide, or a uniform notice that covers tools other than {{PRODUCT}}.

  • Zoom: an account owner or administrator can set a custom disclaimer shown on joining. The title and body are editable, and you can target it at participants inside your organisation, outside it, or both. Plan conditions apply.
  • Microsoft Teams: an IT administrator can change the wording of the in-meeting recording and transcription notice, and the privacy policy URL shown to participants.

These are configured in each platform's admin console; {{COMPANY}} cannot configure them on your behalf. Deciding what notice to give is a matter for the organisation using the product.

#Combining the methods

If you are unsure, use these rules of thumb.

  • Mostly regular internal meetings: explain once out loud at the first meeting, then pasting the notice into the chat is enough.
  • Many external sales meetings and interviews: say it out loud at the start of the meeting and paste the notice into the chat as well. A line in the invitation lets the other side decide in advance (sample wording in How far you can rely on AI meeting notes (a guide for teams)).
  • Phone calls and in-person meetings: there is no chat, so say it out loud at the start.
  • “Start recording automatically” is on: recording starts without a confirmation, so always say it out loud at the start of the meeting as well.
  • A single rule across the company: {{PRODUCT}} has no way to send a notice centrally. Set the method in your internal rules, and use your meeting app's own notices alongside it if needed.

managing-your-account/affiliate-program.title: Affiliate programme
managing-your-account/affiliate-program.description: How referral commission works, how to apply, and the advertising disclosure required under the stealth-marketing rules.
managing-your-account/affiliate-program.html:
The affiliate programme lets you introduce {{PRODUCT}} on a blog, on social media, in videos or on comparison sites, and receive performance-based commission on sign-ups that come through your own link. This article covers how to apply, how applications are assessed, how commission works, and the advertising disclosure everyone taking part is required to make.

Referral programmeA separate scheme for users introducing friends→Plans and paymentWhat the plan your referral signs up to includes→
Note

The “Disclosing that it is advertising” section of this article applies to both the affiliate programme and the referral programme. Posts recommending {{PRODUCT}} in return for a benefit or commission can be caught by the rules in either case, so the guidance on wording is gathered here.

#How it differs from the referral programme

The affiliate programme and the referral programme are separate schemes. The referral programme is a way for {{PRODUCT}} users to pass a link to someone they know and receive a benefit; there is no assessment to take part. The affiliate programme is for people with a channel of their own: {{COMPANY}} reviews the application, and commission is paid according to results.

#From application to payment

  1. 1

    Apply from the application page

    Apply from the affiliate programme application page on {{COMPANY}}'s website. You will be asked for details of the channel you run (blog, social account, video channel and so on) and how you plan to introduce {{PRODUCT}}.

  2. 2

    Wait for the outcome

    {{COMPANY}} reviews your application and your channel. The outcome is sent to your registered email address.

  3. 3

    Introduce {{PRODUCT}} with your own link

    Approved applicants receive their own link. Whenever you publish, always include the advertising disclosure described below.

  4. 4

    Confirmation and payment

    A result is recorded when a new workspace is created through your link and a paid plan is taken out. Recorded results are confirmed after the confirmation period set by {{COMPANY}}, and confirmed amounts are paid together.

#If your application is not approved

{{COMPANY}} runs with a small team, so reviews focus on a limited set of areas. The main reasons an application is not approved are these.

  • The application was incomplete and did not contain the information needed to assess it
  • The contact email address did not match the business details given or the social media profile
  • The proposed approach did not fit the areas {{COMPANY}} is currently focusing its outreach on
  • The main audience was in a region {{COMPANY}} is not currently marketing to

If the content or audience of your channel changes, you are welcome to apply again. New applications are reviewed regularly. We are unable to give a detailed explanation of individual decisions.

#Disclosing that it is advertising (please read)

When you introduce {{PRODUCT}} through the affiliate programme, you must make it possible for ordinary consumers to tell that it is advertising. This follows from the designation made under the Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations (designated 28 March 2023, in force from 1 October 2023) — the rules commonly known as the stealth-marketing regulations.

LegislationAct against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5, item 3 (prohibition of misleading representations)

This provision prohibits representations concerning transactions in goods or services that are liable to mislead ordinary consumers and that are designated by the Prime Minister. On 28 March 2023 the Consumer Affairs Agency designated “representations where it is difficult for ordinary consumers to tell that the representation is that of a business”, in force from 1 October 2023. Under the operational guidance, affiliate programmes are characterised as arrangements “under which an advertiser pays an affiliate performance-based commission in accordance with conditions set in advance”, and introductions made on a performance-commission basis are treated in principle as representations of the advertiser.

#How to display it

  • Use one of “advertisement”, “promotion”, “sponsored” or “PR” (in Japanese: 広告, 宣伝, プロモーション, PR).
  • Or make the benefit you receive clear, for example “I receive commission from {{COMPANY}} for this introduction”.
  • Place the disclosure where the reader sees it first, such as at the very start of the article or post.
  • Make the text size, colour and contrast against the background at least equal to the body text.

Even where you use these words, the representation as a whole may still be judged not to make the advertising nature clear. Rather than inserting the word as a formality, make sure it can actually be read in the first place the reader looks.

#Wording that is unlikely to pass

What to avoid Why
A small “PR” at the end of an article or post It is only noticed by someone who reads to the end, and risks being judged a representation that is difficult to identify.
Slipping “#PR” into a row of hashtags It is buried among the other tags and hard to notice, and may not be accepted as a disclosure at all.
Putting it behind “read more” or inside a collapsed section A position that is invisible until expanded is not the first place the reader looks.
Putting it only at the end of a video description It is not visible while watching, so viewers cannot tell. Display it at the start of the video itself as well.
Matching the background colour, or making it extremely small A disclosure that is present but unreadable is not a clear disclosure.

#Guidance by medium

Medium Where to place the disclosure
Blog articles and comparison sites Before the first paragraph of the body, at the same size as the body text, stating “advertisement” or “PR”.
Social media posts At the start of the post text. Put it in the body, not in the hashtag section.
Video State it on screen or in the audio at the start of the video itself, and also put it at the top of the description.
Email newsletters In the subject line or at the start of the body. Also state the sender's details and how to unsubscribe.

#When no disclosure is needed

For exchanges that are not seen by the public — sending a link to a friend or colleague in a direct message, a chat or an email — this disclosure is not required. What the rules cover is representations in places ordinary consumers can view.

#Claims that are not permitted

Do not make statements that are contrary to fact, or unsubstantiated claims of superiority, about {{PRODUCT}}'s features, accuracy, pricing or comparison with other services. The accuracy of transcription and summarisation varies with audio quality, the number of speakers, background noise and the presence of specialist terms. Expressions such as “100% accurate”, “number one in the industry” or “used by N companies” require material showing a reasonable basis, so do not state figures you have not verified yourself.

LegislationAct against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5, items 1 and 2 (prohibition of misleading representations)

These provisions prohibit representations that present the quality or content of a service as being significantly better than it actually is (misleading representation of superiority), and representations that lead ordinary consumers to believe that price or other terms are significantly more advantageous than they actually are (misleading representation of advantage). Where you mention pricing or a discount, state the plan it applies to, the period it is available and who is eligible alongside it.

#Introducing {{PRODUCT}} by email

Where you introduce {{PRODUCT}} in a newsletter or direct mail, that email is an electronic message sent for advertising or promotional purposes. You must have obtained the recipient's consent to receive it in advance, and you are required to keep a record of that consent. Where a recipient notifies you that they do not wish to receive further messages, stop sending to them.

LegislationAct on Regulation of Transmission of Specified Electronic Mail, Article 3, paragraph 1 (restrictions on sending specified electronic mail)

This provision limits the sending of email for advertising or promotional purposes to people who have notified their consent to receiving it, people who have given you their own email address, people with whom you have a business relationship, and similar. Paragraph 2 of the same article requires records evidencing consent to be kept, and paragraph 3 prohibits sending after a notice of refusal has been received. Article 4 requires the sender's name, the address for notices of refusal, a postal address and contact details to be displayed.

{{COMPANY}} does not take email addresses of people registered through an affiliate from participants and send to them. Do not provide {{COMPANY}} with the email addresses of prospects who have not yet registered.

#Communication, and what happens on a breach

Legal responsibility under the stealth-marketing rules rests with {{COMPANY}} as the advertiser. An affiliate is not themselves made the addressee of an administrative order. Because of this structure, {{COMPANY}} communicates the disclosure rules to participants and reviews published content on an ongoing basis. When you register to take part, you agree to the disclosure rules set out in this article.

Where we find a post without a disclosure, or a claim contrary to fact, {{COMPANY}} will ask you to correct it. Where it is not corrected, we may, as a measure under the programme terms, cancel the commission concerned and suspend your eligibility to take part in the programme.

#If something is not working

Symptom What to check
No result is being recorded Check that your own link is installed correctly and that the person you introduced has created a new workspace.
Commission is not being confirmed A set period passes before results are confirmed. See the last step under “From application to payment” for the conditions.
You are unsure how to word the disclosure Judge it by whether the place can be viewed by the public. If you are unsure, it is safer to include the disclosure.
The outcome of your application has not arrived Check your spam folder, then contact us at {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

Referral programmeReferral benefits for users→Plans and paymentWhat the plans include, and pricing→Terms of serviceThe terms that apply when you take part in the programme→
