managing-your-account/account-and-email-.title: Account and email address changes
managing-your-account/account-and-email-.description: Changing the email address you sign in with, merging accounts, and carrying notes across.
managing-your-account/account-and-email-.html:
Your email domain has changed because the company was renamed; your address has changed because you moved jobs or teams; you want to bring a personal and a work account together. This article sets out what happens to your {{PRODUCT}} account and notes in situations like these, and which route you can use to move across.

Moving notes from another accountThe steps, and what carries over→WorkspacesHow company workspaces and members work→Deleting your accountTidying up accounts you no longer use→
The email address on an existing account cannot be changed directly

In {{PRODUCT}}, you cannot rewrite the email address registered on an account that has already been created. The one exception is a domain change carried out by a Google or Microsoft workspace administrator (see 1 below), where the same account is kept. In every other case, you sign in with the new email address to create a new account, then use the in-app note import to bring your earlier notes across.

#Working out which route applies

Situation Route to take Account
The domain or address changes within the same Google or Microsoft workspace Your organisation makes the change; nothing else is needed The same account is kept
You want to move to a different address while you can still access the old one Create an account with the new address and import your notes It becomes a new account
You cannot access the old email address Migration is not possible You start again with a new account

#1. A domain change within the same Google or Microsoft workspace

Where your employer's domain changes, or your email address is edited within the same Google or Microsoft workspace (from @example.co.jp to @example.jp, say), nothing special is required.

Note

{{PRODUCT}} identifies accounts using the unique identifier issued by Google or Microsoft, not the text of the email address. So even when your organisation reassigns the address, it is treated as the same account.

  • Your organisation can update the domain or address.
  • You carry on signing in the same way as before (Google or Microsoft).
  • Your past notes and history stay as they are.

In Enterprise workspaces with single sign-on (SSO) configured, the SSO connection settings have to be changed. An administrator should contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} so the change can be made together with {{COMPANY}}.

The auto-join domain does not switch over automatically

A workspace's auto-join domain (the setting that lets people with an address on that domain find and join the workspace) is not updated automatically when the company domain changes. This domain is fixed when the workspace is created, and an administrator cannot rewrite it from the settings screen; all an administrator can do is turn auto-join on or off. If you want employees on the new domain to be able to join the existing workspace, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

If what you see or your history is not as expected after your organisation makes the change, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} as well and we will look into it.

#2. Where you can still access the old email address

To change email address, or to bring several accounts together, use the in-app note import. Since there is no feature for renaming an existing account, creating an account with the new address and importing the notes from the earlier account into it is what amounts to “changing your email address”.

  1. 1

    Create the new account

    Sign in to {{PRODUCT}} with the new email address and create an account.

  2. 2

    Start the import

    Start a note import from the new account.

  3. 3

    Confirm you own the old address

    A verification code is sent to the old email address; enter it to confirm you own it.

  4. 4

    Wait for the import to finish

    Depending on how many notes there are, this can take a while. Wait for it to complete without quitting the app.

Check

Once the import has finished, check that your earlier notes appear in the note list on the new account. If the count does not match, check what carries over in Moving notes from another account.

Which notes can be migrated, how folders and sharing settings are handled, and how long an import takes are all covered in Moving notes from another account. Check what carries over before you start the import.

If you want to move notes between workspaces, that is a move across workspaces rather than across accounts, so use the steps in Moving notes between workspaces instead.

#3. Where you cannot access the old email address

Where you can no longer receive mail at the address tied to your earlier account, notes cannot be imported from that account.

Before an import, you have to confirm that the email address is yours to use, and that confirmation is done with a verification code sent to that address. There is no other safe way to confirm ownership, so if you cannot receive the code, the position is this.

  • You cannot complete the in-app import.
  • There is no way to retrieve the notes from the earlier account.
  • You will be starting afresh on the new account.
Act early once you know you are leaving or moving

A company-issued email address usually stops receiving mail after your last day. From the moment it stops, there is no way to retrieve notes from the account on that address. If there are notes you want to carry over to a personal address, complete the steps in Moving notes from another account while you are still employed. Note that the treatment of notes stored in your employer's workspace depends on your company's information-management rules and your employment contract. {{COMPANY}} cannot judge whether moving notes created for work to a personal account is permitted, so always check with your organisation's administrator before taking anything with you. For permissions and member management on the workspace side, see Workspaces.

If you are an administrator and a member is leaving, check before you remove them from the workspace that they have finished exporting or migrating any notes they need. Once they are removed, their account is disabled within the workspace and they lose access even to notes they saved themselves.

#Effect on billing

Creating a new account does not automatically cancel a paid plan taken out on the earlier account. The workspace's subscription remains in place, so cancel any subscription you no longer need from Settings > Billing. The steps, and how long you can carry on using the product after cancelling, are covered in About cancellation. To use a paid plan on the new account, you need to take out a new subscription on the new workspace.

Where someone who has left still has a payment method registered, charges continue to that card. For what to do when the person responsible changes, see Plans and payment.

#If something is not working

Symptom What to check
You cannot sign in after a domain change Check you are choosing the same sign-in method as before (Google or Microsoft). If you use SSO, ask your administrator to change the settings.
Colleagues on the new domain cannot join the workspace The auto-join domain is not updated automatically. Contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.
The import verification code does not arrive Check the spam folder on the old address. If you cannot receive it, the import cannot be completed.
Some notes are missing after the import What carries over is set out in Moving notes from another account. For working out why something is missing, see Notes are missing as well.
You want to switch to a Microsoft account Migrating to a Microsoft account has the steps.

If your situation is not covered above, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with your old email address, your new email address and the workspace name.

managing-your-account/referral-program.title: Referral programme
managing-your-account/referral-program.description: The benefits and conditions for referring people you know, and the advertising disclosure a referral needs.
managing-your-account/referral-program.html:
The referral programme lets you give your own referral link to friends or colleagues who are not yet using {{PRODUCT}}, so that they receive a benefit when they sign up. This article covers where to find your link, the conditions for the benefit to be granted, and the advertising disclosure you need when you post a referral link on social media or a blog.

Affiliate programmeA separate scheme paying performance-based commission→Plans and paymentWhat the plan the benefit applies to includes→WorkspacesHow the workspace the person you refer creates works→

#How a referral works

  1. 1

    Find your referral link

    In the {{PRODUCT}} app, open Settings > Referrals and find your own referral link.

  2. 2

    Pass the link on

    Give the link to a friend or colleague who has not used {{PRODUCT}} before.

  3. 3

    They sign up

    Once they sign up from that link and finish creating a workspace, the benefit is applied to their workspace.

The benefit is granted at the point the person you referred completes registration and creates a workspace. Merely clicking the link, or dropping out partway through registration, does not qualify.

#Conditions for the benefit to be granted

The benefit applies where the person referred meets all of the following.

  • They are using {{PRODUCT}} for the first time (they do not already have an account)
  • They register with an email address issued by their employer. Personal addresses such as free webmail do not qualify
  • No {{PRODUCT}} workspace has yet been created at their employer

Where the conditions are not met, no benefit is granted even if someone registers through the link. Registering with your own address, or another address you control, in order to obtain a benefit, and referring someone you know does not meet the conditions, are treated as misuse of the programme and may lead to the benefit being cancelled.

#Posting your referral link on social media or a blog

Under the referral programme, a benefit is granted to the referrer or the person referred when someone registers through the link. Where you post a recommendation of {{PRODUCT}} having received that economic benefit, in a place the public can view — a blog, social media, a video, a comparison site — that post may fall within the stealth-marketing rules under the Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations. In that case, include a disclosure that makes the advertising nature clear to the reader.

LegislationAct against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5, item 3 (prohibition of misleading representations)

This provision prohibits representations concerning transactions in goods or services that are liable to mislead ordinary consumers and that are designated by the Prime Minister. On 28 March 2023 the Consumer Affairs Agency made “representations where it is difficult for ordinary consumers to tell that the representation is that of a business” the subject of this designation, in force from 1 October 2023. What the rules cover are endorsements made in return for an economic benefit provided by a business, where it is not made clear that the representation is the business's own.

#How to word the disclosure

  • Use one of “advertisement”, “promotion”, “sponsored” or “PR” (in Japanese: 広告, 宣伝, プロモーション, PR)
  • Or make the benefit you receive clear, for example “I receive a referral benefit for this” or “I am recommending this having received a benefit from {{COMPANY}}”
  • Place the disclosure where the reader sees it first, such as at the very start of the post or article
  • Make the text size, colour and contrast against the background at least equal to the body text, so that it is not skipped over

Placing it small at the end, slipping it into a row of hashtags, or putting it inside a collapsed section all risk being judged difficult to identify even though a disclosure is present. A list of wording that is unlikely to pass, and guidance on where to place the disclosure by medium, is gathered in Affiliate programme. The approach to disclosure is the same for the referral programme.

#When no disclosure is needed

For exchanges that are not seen by the public — sending a referral link to a friend or colleague in a direct message, a chat or an email — this disclosure is not required. The same goes for sharing the link with members of your own team in an internal chat. What the rules cover are representations in places ordinary consumers can view.

#What {{COMPANY}} communicates, and what happens on a breach

Legal responsibility under the stealth-marketing rules rests with the business making the representation — that is, {{COMPANY}} as the advertiser. The individual making the referral is not made the addressee of an administrative order. Because of this structure, {{COMPANY}} has to communicate the disclosure rules to people taking part in the programme and check what is actually being posted.

Where we find a post without a disclosure, {{COMPANY}} may ask you to correct it. Where it is not corrected, or where statements contrary to fact are made about {{PRODUCT}}'s features, accuracy, pricing or comparison with other services, we may, as a measure under the programme terms, cancel the benefit and suspend your eligibility to take part.

Do not make unsubstantiated claims of superiority

The accuracy of transcription and summarisation varies with audio quality, the number of speakers, background noise and the presence of specialist terms. Using expressions such as “100% accurate” or “number one in the industry” in a referral post makes {{COMPANY}} answerable for a misleading representation of superiority or of advantage. Write what you have actually found in using it.

#How it differs from the affiliate programme

The referral programme is a way for {{PRODUCT}} users to pass a link to someone they know and receive a benefit; there is no assessment to take part. The affiliate programme, which pays commission according to results, is a scheme for people with a channel of their own, who take part after a review by {{COMPANY}}. In both cases, a referral in a place the public can view requires a disclosure that it is advertising.

#If something is not working

Symptom What to check
You referred someone but no benefit was granted Check that they registered with their employer's email address, and that their company does not already have a workspace.
Settings > Referrals is not there Update the app to the latest version and open settings with the workspace concerned open.
Opening the referral link goes to the sign-in screen Someone who already has a {{PRODUCT}} account does not qualify. Pass the link to someone else instead.
You cannot tell whether a post needs a “PR” label Judge it by whether the place can be viewed by the public. If you are unsure, it is safer to include the disclosure.

For questions about the programme, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

#Related articles

Affiliate programmePerformance-based commission, and the disclosure rules in full→Plans and paymentBilling once the benefit has been applied→Terms of serviceThe terms that apply when you take part in the programme→

managing-your-account/understanding-your.title: Reading your invoice
managing-your-account/understanding-your.description: What a qualified invoice must state, how pro-rating works, and how to read unused-period adjustments.
managing-your-account/understanding-your.html:
A {{PRODUCT}} invoice is made up of the base charge for the number of seats, plus adjustment lines for any change in seat count partway through the billing period. This article explains what each line represents, where the items required of a qualified invoice appear, and how the pro-rating is calculated.

Plans and paymentWhat the plans include, and payment methods→About cancellationBilling and refunds on cancellation→WorkspacesThe actions that change the seat count→
Note

Billing is per workspace and per seat. The number of members in the workspace is the seat count, and the base charge is that seat count multiplied by the plan's unit price. Every amount on the invoice is built up from this.

#How the invoice is made up

The seat count multiplied by the plan's unit price appears at the foot of the invoice as the Subscription charge for the next billing period. Where the seat count did not change during the previous billing period, this is the only line on the invoice.

Where the seat count changed partway through the billing period, adjustment lines settling that change are stacked above it. Adjustment lines always appear as a pair.

#What is stated for the purposes of a qualified invoice

{{PRODUCT}} invoices are produced so as to contain everything a qualified invoice must state. The six items required by the Consumption Tax Act, and where each appears on the invoice, are as follows.

# Item required by law Where it appears on the invoice
1 The name of the registered invoice issuer and its registration number {{COMPANY}}'s name in the invoice header, with “Registration number {{INVOICE_NO}}” beneath it
2 The date of the taxable transfer of assets (or, where a period is covered together, that period) The Service period on the line item (for example, 1 September 2026 – 30 September 2026)
3 The nature of the assets or services covered by the taxable transfer The item name on the line, giving the plan name and the seat count (for example, {{PRODUCT}} Team plan subscription (10 seats))
4 The tax-exclusive or tax-inclusive total, separated by tax rate, and the rate applied The Subtotal (excl. tax) in the totals box, with subject to 10% beside it
5 The consumption tax calculated separately for each tax rate The Consumption tax (10%)
6 The name of the business receiving the document The addressee box on the invoice (for example, XYZ Co., Ltd.)
LegislationConsumption Tax Act, Article 57-4, paragraph 1 (obligations of a registered invoice issuer)

A qualified invoice issued by a registered invoice issuer must state the issuer's name including its registration number, the date of the transaction, what the transaction covers, the total separated by tax rate together with the rate applied, the consumption tax separated by tax rate, and the name of the business receiving it. The six items in the table above correspond to this provision.

LegislationConsumption Tax Act, Article 29 (tax rate)

The standard rate of consumption tax is 7.8%, which together with local consumption tax (22/78ths of the consumption tax) comes to 10%. The reduced rate never applies to {{PRODUCT}} subscription charges, so the invoice shows everything in a single band, “subject to 10%”.

#The labels used on line items

The items shown in the invoice detail are as follows. Not every line appears every time; they appear according to what happened during that billing period.

Label What it means
Subscription charge The plan's base charge for the next billing period, with the plan name and seat count.
Service period The period that line covers. Pro-rated lines also show the number of days.
Seats added (pro-rated) The charge for seats added partway through the billing period, with the date added, the number of days and the unit price.
Seats removed (pro-rated adjustment) The reduction for seats removed partway through the billing period. Shown as a negative.
Pro-rated charge An amount apportioned over a period following a plan change or similar. The start date and number of days used for the apportionment are given.
Unused period adjustment The refund of the part of what was prepaid at the previous seat count that corresponds to the unelapsed period. Shown as a negative.
Credit balance applied Credit granted through a referral benefit or similar, applied against the invoice. Shown as a negative.
Discount A coupon or annual discount. The name and the rate or amount are given.
Subtotal (excl. tax) The tax-exclusive total subject to 10%.
Consumption tax (10%) The consumption tax, separated by tax rate.
Total (incl. tax) The amount actually payable.
Registration number {{COMPANY}}'s registered invoice issuer number.

#How pro-rating works

When the seat count changes partway through a billing period, {{PRODUCT}} settles it by refunding what was prepaid and then recalculating the remaining days at the new seat count. That is why adjustment lines come in pairs.

  • Unused period adjustment (negative): of the charge taken at the previous seat count, the days from the date of the change to the end of the billing period are refunded. This is the “that configuration is no longer in use, so here are the remaining days back” line.
  • Pro-rated charge (positive): for those same remaining days, the charge calculated at the new seat count. This is the “the seat count has changed, so here are the remaining days charged again” line.

Adding the two lines together gives the net charge, which is the charge for the remaining days on the seats added or removed. On an increase the net is positive; on a decrease it is negative (a refund). Days are counted from the day the seat count changed, up to the last day of that billing period.

#A worked example

The figures here are illustrative

The unit price and amounts used here are made up for the sake of the explanation. For the actual unit price see {{COMPANY}}'s pricing page, and for the amount actually charged see your own invoice.

Suppose the billing period runs for the 30 days from 1 to 30 September 2026, and the Team plan unit price is ¥10,000 per seat per month (excluding tax). You had 3 seats on 1 September and added 2 seats on 16 September. From 16 to 30 September there are 15 days remaining.

Line item Calculation Amount (excl. tax)
Unused period adjustment (3 seats, 16–30 September, 15 days) ¥10,000 × 3 seats × 15 days ÷ 30 days -¥15,000
Pro-rated charge (5 seats, 16–30 September, 15 days) ¥10,000 × 5 seats × 15 days ÷ 30 days +¥25,000
Subscription charge (1–31 October, 5 seats) ¥10,000 × 5 seats ¥50,000
Subtotal (excl. tax) ¥60,000
Consumption tax (10%) ¥60,000 × 10% ¥6,000
Total (incl. tax) ¥66,000

The net of the adjustment lines is ¥25,000 − ¥15,000 = ¥10,000, which matches the charge for using the 2 added seats for 15 days — half the billing period.

#Why the date ranges differ between lines

Each pair of adjustment lines covers a different length of time because the number of days left until the next renewal differed at the moment of each change. A change early in the billing period leaves more days, so the adjustment is larger; a change close to the last day leaves fewer, so it is smaller. This is the calculation being proportional to the number of days, not a sign that anything is wrong.

#One pair of lines per change

Every change to the seat count adds another pair of adjustment lines. In the example below there were four changes within a single billing period (15 September to 14 October), giving eight adjustment lines, plus the Subscription charge line for the next period — nine lines in all.

Date What happened Seats
15 September (start of the billing period) Starts with 2 seats 2
27 September 1 seat added 2 → 3
2 October 1 seat added 3 → 4
7 October 1 seat added 4 → 5
13 October 1 seat added 5 → 6
15 October (renewal date) The next billing period begins with 6 seats 6

A change made on the renewal date itself produces no adjustment line, because there are no remaining days. The new seat count is simply reflected in the Subscription charge for the next billing period.

Keeping the number of lines down

Adding members one at a time on different days adds a pair of adjustment lines each time. Adding several people together, at a hiring or reorganisation point, keeps it to one change and keeps the invoice shorter.

#When a member leaves

Removing a seat works the same way, with the signs reversed. An unused period adjustment (negative) is made for the higher, previous seat count, and a pro-rated charge (positive) for the remaining days at the lower, new seat count. The net is a negative for the remaining days on the seats removed, and is deducted from your next invoice. You are never charged on an ongoing basis for a seat that is not in use.

Removing a member from the workspace does not automatically detach the payment method they registered from the subscription. What to do when the person responsible changes is covered in Plans and payment.

#Rounding of consumption tax

Consumption tax is not calculated line by line; it is calculated once per invoice for each tax rate. Every {{PRODUCT}} charge is subject to 10%, so a single rounding is applied to the tax-exclusive total for the whole invoice, and the result is shown as Consumption tax (10%).

Pro-rating can leave fractions of a yen on line item amounts. Where that happens, multiplying each line by 1.1 and adding them up may not match the total shown on the invoice to the yen. Under the National Tax Agency's treatment of qualified invoices, rounding is applied once per tax rate per invoice, so the total stated on the invoice is the correct amount.

#Changing the addressee and billing details

To change the addressee on an invoice, register the company name and department under the billing details at Settings > Billing. If you want a registration number or business details on the invoice, register those on the same billing details screen.

What you register takes effect from the next invoice issued. To change the addressee on an invoice already issued, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the date of the invoice concerned.

#Viewing and downloading invoices

  1. 1

    Open the billing screen

    In the {{PRODUCT}} app, open Settings > Billing. Your current seat count and next renewal date are on this screen too.

  2. 2

    Open subscription management

    Manage subscription takes you to the payment provider's management screen.

  3. 3

    Open the invoice

    From the list of past invoices and receipts, open the one you want and download it.

Check

Manage subscription not being shown, with a billing contact's email address in its place, means billing for that workspace is managed by a different administrator. Ask them to send you a copy, or to add you as a billing contact.

#If something is not working

Symptom What to check
The amount is higher than expected Check whether seats were added during the billing period. The net of the adjustment lines is the pro-rated charge for those additions.
There are nine lines and you cannot make sense of them The pairs of adjustment lines come first, and the bottom line is the base charge for the next period. Match the period and seat count up pair by pair.
Adding up the lines misses the total by a yen Consumption tax is calculated once for the invoice as a whole. The total on the invoice is the correct amount.
The addressee still shows the old company name Changes to billing details take effect from the next invoice issued. For invoices already issued, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.
You cannot find the registration number It is in the invoice header, or below the totals box. If it is not shown, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

If anything on your invoice is unclear, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the issue date of the invoice concerned and your workspace name.

managing-your-account/understanding-your.text: A {{PRODUCT}} invoice is made up of the base charge for the number of seats, plus adjustment lines for any change in seat count partway through the billing period. This article explains what each line represents, where the items required of a qualified invoice appear, and how the pro-rating is calculated. Plans and payment What the plans include, and payment methods → About cancellation Billing and refunds on cancellation → Workspaces The actions that change the seat count → Note Billing is per workspace and per seat. The number of members in the workspace is the seat count, and the base charge is that seat count multiplied by the plan's unit price. Every amount on the invoice is built up from this. # How the invoice is made up The seat count multiplied by the plan's unit price appears at the foot of the invoice as the Subscription charge for the next billing period. Where the seat count did not change during the previous billing period, this is the only line on the invoice. Where the seat count changed partway through the billing period, adjustment lines settling that change are stacked above it. Adjustment lines always appear as a pair. # What is stated for the purposes of a qualified invoice {{PRODUCT}} invoices are produced so as to contain everything a qualified invoice must state. The six items required by the Consumption Tax Act, and where each appears on the invoice, are as follows. # Item required by law Where it appears on the invoice 1 The name of the registered invoice issuer and its registration number {{COMPANY}}'s name in the invoice header, with “Registration number {{INVOICE_NO}}” beneath it 2 The date of the taxable transfer of assets (or, where a period is covered together, that period) The Service period on the line item (for example, 1 September 2026 – 30 September 2026) 3 The nature of the assets or services covered by the taxable transfer The item name on the line, giving the plan name and the seat count (for example, {{PRODUCT}} Team plan subscription (10 seats)) 4 The tax-exclusive or tax-inclusive total, separated by tax rate, and the rate applied The Subtotal (excl. tax) in the totals box, with subject to 10% beside it 5 The consumption tax calculated separately for each tax rate The Consumption tax (10%) 6 The name of the business receiving the document The addressee box on the invoice (for example, XYZ Co., Ltd.) Legislation Consumption Tax Act, Article 57-4, paragraph 1 (obligations of a registered invoice issuer) A qualified invoice issued by a registered invoice issuer must state the issuer's name including its registration number, the date of the transaction, what the transaction covers, the total separated by tax rate together with the rate applied, the consumption tax separated by tax rate, and the name of the business receiving it. The six items in the table above correspond to this provision. Legislation Consumption Tax Act, Article 29 (tax rate) The standard rate of consumption tax is 7.8%, which together with local consumption tax (22/78ths of the consumption tax) comes to 10%. The reduced rate never applies to {{PRODUCT}} subscription charges, so the invoice shows everything in a single band, “subject to 10%”. # The labels used on line items The items shown in the invoice detail are as follows. Not every line appears every time; they appear according to what happened during that billing period. Label What it means Subscription charge The plan's base charge for the next billing period, with the plan name and seat count. Service period The period that line covers. Pro-rated lines also show the number of days. Seats added (pro-rated) The charge for seats added partway through the billing period, with the date added, the number of days and the unit price. Seats removed (pro-rated adjustment) The reduction for seats removed partway through the billing period. Shown as a negative. Pro-rated charge An amount apportioned over a period following a plan change or similar. The start date and number of days used for the apportionment are given. Unused period adjustment The refund of the part of what was prepaid at the previous seat count that corresponds to the unelapsed period. Shown as a negative. Credit balance applied Credit granted through a referral benefit or similar, applied against the invoice. Shown as a negative. Discount A coupon or annual discount. The name and the rate or amount are given. Subtotal (excl. tax) The tax-exclusive total subject to 10%. Consumption tax (10%) The consumption tax, separated by tax rate. Total (incl. tax) The amount actually payable. Registration number {{COMPANY}}'s registered invoice issuer number. # How pro-rating works When the seat count changes partway through a billing period, {{PRODUCT}} settles it by refunding what was prepaid and then recalculating the remaining days at the new seat count. That is why adjustment lines come in pairs. Unused period adjustment (negative): of the charge taken at the previous seat count, the days from the date of the change to the end of the billing period are refunded. This is the “that configuration is no longer in use, so here are the remaining days back” line. Pro-rated charge (positive): for those same remaining days, the charge calculated at the new seat count. This is the “the seat count has changed, so here are the remaining days charged again” line. Adding the two lines together gives the net charge , which is the charge for the remaining days on the seats added or removed. On an increase the net is positive; on a decrease it is negative (a refund). Days are counted from the day the seat count changed, up to the last day of that billing period. # A worked example The figures here are illustrative The unit price and amounts used here are made up for the sake of the explanation. For the actual unit price see {{COMPANY}}'s pricing page, and for the amount actually charged see your own invoice. Suppose the billing period runs for the 30 days from 1 to 30 September 2026, and the Team plan unit price is ¥10,000 per seat per month (excluding tax). You had 3 seats on 1 September and added 2 seats on 16 September. From 16 to 30 September there are 15 days remaining. A change early in the billing period leaves more days, so the adjustment is larger; a change close to the last day leaves fewer, so it is smaller. This is the calculation being proportional to the number of days, not a sign that anything is wrong. # One pair of lines per change Every change to the seat count adds another pair of adjustment lines. troubleshooting/calendar-sync.title: Calendar is not syncing
troubleshooting/calendar-sync.description: What to check when events do not appear, appear twice, or do not update.
troubleshooting/calendar-sync.html:
This brings together what to check for symptoms such as meetings not appearing under “Coming up” on the home screen, a calendar shared with you not showing, or times being shifted. For setting the calendar connection up in the first place, see Connecting your calendar.

Connecting your calendarThe initial setup steps→Signing in with a Microsoft accountConnecting with Microsoft 365, and admin approval→Network and allowlistsWhere traffic is being blocked→
Note

{{PRODUCT}} supports Google Calendar and Microsoft calendars. It pulls events from the calendar of the Google or Microsoft account you signed in with and shows them under “Coming up” on the home screen of the desktop app (macOS and Windows). Only events visible on the calendar of the account you signed in with can be pulled in. Change which calendars are shown from Settings > Calendar, or from the gear icon beside “Coming up”.

#Checks by symptom

If that is not what you are seeing, work through the section for your symptom, from the top.

#No events at all appear under “Coming up”

  1. 1

    Check there are events on the calendar itself

    Open Google Calendar or the Outlook calendar with the email address you are signed in to {{PRODUCT}} with, and confirm the events appear there.

  2. 2

    Check which calendars are shown

    Click the gear icon beside “Coming up” and confirm the calendars you want are ticked.

  3. 3

    Grant the permission again

    If neither is the problem, {{PRODUCT}} may not have been granted calendar permission. Open “Settings” from the menu at the bottom left, choose “Sign out”, and sign in again with the same account. You are asked for calendar access during sign-in; allow it.

If it still does not appear, your network or IT department's restrictions may be blocking the connection to the calendar. Go on to “Where your corporate network is involved” below.

#Events from a calendar shared with you do not appear

Where you cannot see events from a calendar someone has shared, that calendar may not have been shared correctly with the email address you are signed in with.

The case to watch is where the shared calendar's provider differs from the provider you signed in with. If, for example, you are signed in with a Microsoft account and someone shares a Google Calendar with you, sharing to that email address is not enough on its own. The events have to appear on the calendar of the provider you signed in with — the Microsoft calendar, in this example. How to share a Google Calendar is explained in Google's help.

Where sharing has been set up correctly, that calendar appears as a checkbox in {{PRODUCT}}'s calendar settings.

  1. Click the gear icon beside “Coming up” to list the calendars visible from the connected account.
  2. Tick the calendar you want. It can take a few minutes for the sync to come through.

If it still does not appear, check the sharing permissions. Some company policies prohibit sharing calendars externally. Also, where the sharing permission is “free/busy only”, {{PRODUCT}} cannot retrieve the events; a permission that shows all event details is required. Ask them to choose the setting equivalent to “See all event details” in the per-person permission dropdown.

#Meeting times appear shifted

{{PRODUCT}} shows the time exactly as stored on the connected calendar.

Where a time looks shifted, open Google Calendar or the Outlook calendar and check what time the event is stored at. Correcting the time zone setting on the calendar side comes through to {{PRODUCT}} as well; it can take a few minutes.

If you have many meetings with overseas offices or clients, a per-event time zone on the calendar may have been set to something unintended. Events created by someone else in a different time zone are worth checking too.

Where the calendar is right and only the app's display is shifted, check the time and time zone on your computer.

System Settings > General > Date & Time — open it and confirm “Set time and date automatically” and “Set time zone automatically using your current location” are on. Where a company device-management policy has fixed them, check that the time zone set matches where you actually work.

Settings > Time & language > Date & time — open it and confirm “Set time automatically” and “Set time zone automatically” are on. If they are off, check that the “Time zone” field matches where you actually work.

Settings > Time & language > Date & time — open it. The items have the same names as on Windows 11: check “Set time automatically” and “Set time zone automatically”.

#An Outlook or Exchange calendar will not connect

{{PRODUCT}} supports calendars on cloud Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online). On-premises Exchange servers are not supported. If you use Outlook against an Exchange server other than Microsoft 365, calendar integration may not be available.

If you cannot connect on Microsoft 365, sign out and sign in again following Signing in with a Microsoft account. Calendar permission is requested again during sign-in.

Where your organisation's settings require administrator approval, an administrator in your IT department has to approve {{PRODUCT}} in the Microsoft admin centre. The approval steps are also covered in Signing in with a Microsoft account.

#A calendar in an Outlook “public folder” does not appear

Calendars placed in an Outlook “public folder” work differently from ordinary calendars and cannot be read by {{PRODUCT}}. That applies on cloud Microsoft 365 too.

If your team runs its shared schedule in a “public folder”, you will need either to recreate it as an ordinary calendar and share that, or to switch to copying events onto personal calendars.

#It used to appear and now does not

Where events have stopped appearing, or you have changed calendar sharing settings, disconnecting and reconnecting can resolve it.

  1. 1

    Sign out

    Click your workspace name at the bottom left and choose “Sign out” from “Settings”.

  2. 2

    Sign in again

    Sign in again with the same Google or Microsoft account.

  3. 3

    Allow the permission

    When calendar permission is requested, allow it again.

  4. 4

    Check the calendars

    Settings > Calendar — open it and confirm the calendars you need are on.

Check

It takes a few minutes for the sync to catch up. If meetings still do not appear under “Coming up” after a few minutes, go back to checking whether the events exist on the calendar itself.

#The Google Calendar connection keeps dropping

Where it drops again soon after reconnecting, your organisation’s Google Workspace security settings may be revoking {{PRODUCT}}’s access.

Ask an administrator in your IT department to add {{PRODUCT}} to the allowlist under “Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage third-party app access” in the Google Workspace admin console. Where tokens for apps that are not allowlisted are set to expire periodically, reconnecting on the user side simply repeats the same cycle.

#Where your corporate network is involved

Calendar sync works over traffic to {{PRODUCT}}’s servers and to the Google or Microsoft services. Where sign-in works but only the calendar fails to sync, authentication has gone through and it is only the later token refresh or calendar API traffic that is being blocked.

Try with network tools such as a VPN turned off; if that helps, talk to your IT department. How to recognise blocking on a corporate network — proxies and SSL inspection, always-on VPN, blocking by endpoint protection products — and the list of destinations that need to be allowed are covered in Network and allowlists.

#Where you cannot get approval on a company-issued machine

Where administrator approval is required and you cannot proceed yourself, ask your IT department. For calendar integration there are three things to ask for.

  • On Microsoft 365: application approval for {{PRODUCT}} in the Microsoft admin centre (the permission needed is reading calendar events)
  • On Google Workspace: allowing {{PRODUCT}} under API controls in the admin console
  • On the network: allowing HTTPS to {{PRODUCT}}’s destinations, and, where SSL inspection is in use, confirming certificate distribution

A template for the request is in Network and allowlists. Keep the “calendar integration approval” item and use it as it stands.

#If none of this resolves it

If the steps above do not resolve it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Including the following helps us investigate faster.

  • The type of account you sign in with (Google or Microsoft) and the domain of that email address
  • The date and time of the meeting that does not appear (in a form that shows the time zone) and the calendar name
  • Whether it is an event on your own calendar or on a shared calendar
  • Settings > Calendar — whether that calendar appears in that list
  • Whether no events appear at all, or only events on a particular calendar
  • Your network environment (corporate LAN, VPN or not, proxy or not)

Where only the note for a particular meeting is missing, see Notes are missing as well.

#Related articles

Connecting your calendarInitial setup, and choosing which calendars are shown→Signing in with a Microsoft accountAdmin approval, and signing in again→Network and allowlistsBlocked traffic, and a template request→Notes are missingWhere the event appears but the note cannot be found→

troubleshooting/increased-file-limits.description: The limits on files you can upload, and how to have them raised.
troubleshooting/increased-file-limits.html:
This sets out the limits that apply when you add material to a folder or attach a file in chat. Where an upload fails, work out whether you have hit a limit or the traffic is being stopped by your network.

Spaces and foldersHow material is organised→Asking questions about a note (chat)Attaching a file to give context→Network and allowlistsWhere traffic is being blocked→
Note

Three limits apply: the total size per folder, the size of an individual file, and the number of files per folder. Exceeding any one of them stops the upload completing. When you get an error, work out which limit you have hit first.

#The current limits

Item Current limit Previous limit
Total size per folder 1 GB 50 MB
Size of an individual file 30 MB 5 MB
Number of files per folder 200 20

The right-hand column shows the values before the increase. Since you can now keep more material together in one folder, there is no longer any need to add folders purely to spread the volume. Where an old internal guide still says 50 MB or 5 MB, read it as the current limit instead.

#What you see when you hit a limit

Trying to add a file that exceeds a limit stops the upload completing and shows an error. What to do depends on which of these it is.

  • An individual file is over 30 MB — the file itself has to be made smaller.
  • The folder total is close to 1 GB — delete files you no longer need from that folder, or split them across another one.
  • The folder has reached 200 files — that is the file-count limit. Split the folder by purpose.

To work out which it is, check the size of the files you have. How you do that depends on your operating system.

Select the file in Finder and choose File > Get Info (command + I) to see its size. Selecting several files together and doing the same shows the combined size. To see a folder's total, select the folder and get info on it.

Right-click the file in File Explorer and choose Properties to see its size. Where the right-click menu is the short version and the item is not there, open the classic menu from Show more options. Selecting several files together and opening properties shows the combined size.

Right-click the file in File Explorer and choose Properties to see its size. Selecting several files together and opening properties shows the combined size. Right-clicking a folder and opening properties shows that folder's total size and file count.

How to use folders and spaces is explained in Spaces and folders.

#Working with large files

  • PDFs shrink considerably if you delete pages you do not need, or re-export them at a lower image resolution. Scanned paper documents benefit most.
  • In presentation decks, embedded video and high-resolution images usually account for most of the size. Replace those parts, or pull just the parts you need out into a separate file.
  • Spreadsheets get lighter if you delete old sheets you do not refer to.
  • Bundling files into an archive does not help where the content has to be read. Making each file smaller is the reliable approach.

#Where an upload fails for another reason

Where you are within the limits and the upload still does not complete, it may be being stopped by your corporate network. The most common cause with file transfers is a per-request size limit configured on a proxy or web filtering product. Where small files go through but anything over a few MB fails, suspect that limit. Some organisations block sending files to external services altogether as a data-loss measure; in that case everything other than file operations works normally.

To narrow it down, try the same file on a different network, such as tethering to a mobile connection. If it succeeds there, your corporate network is the cause. How to recognise blocking by endpoint protection products, which destinations to allow, and a template request for your IT department are all in Network and allowlists.

#Things worth checking before you upload

The contents of files you add to a folder or to chat are passed to AI processing in order to generate answers. Where you are working with material covered by a confidentiality agreement with a client, unannounced personnel information, or material containing customers' personal data, check against your internal rules and your contracts whether it may be processed by an external service.

Where you handle files containing personal data, the Act on the Protection of Personal Information requires that you do not go beyond the purpose of use specified in advance, and that you supervise your processors. For how to think about this, see Security and privacy FAQ.

#Asking about raising a limit

Where the current limits are not enough for your work, get in touch at {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Tell us what it is for and how much you need, and we will check what is possible and come back to you.

  1. 1

    Establish where you stand

    Work out which limit you are hitting (total size, individual file size, or file count) and what you are currently using.

  2. 2

    Decide the figures you need

    Estimate, in concrete numbers, how far the limit needs to go up. Note too whether you need it temporarily or on an ongoing basis.

  3. 3

    Get in touch

    Contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the information below.

The information to include is as follows.

  • Your workspace name and the folder concerned
  • The limit you are hitting, and the figure you need
  • What the files are used for in your work
  • Whether this is a temporary need or an ongoing one
  • When you need it by

#If none of this resolves it

Where you are within the limits and still cannot upload, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Including the following helps us investigate faster.

  • The file format and size, and the number of files
  • Where you are adding them (the folder name, or whether it is an attachment in chat)
  • The error message shown on screen (in its exact wording, if there is one)
  • The result of trying on a different network (tethering, for example)
  • Your network environment (corporate LAN, VPN or not, proxy or not)
  • The date and time it failed (in a form that shows the time zone)
  • Your operating system and version, and the {{PRODUCT}} app version

#Related articles

troubleshooting/missing-notes.title: Notes are missing
troubleshooting/missing-notes.description: The order to check things in when a note does not appear in the list.
troubleshooting/missing-notes.html:
When a note looks as though it has vanished from the list, it has almost never actually been deleted. Usually it is one of three things: you are signed in with a different account, you are looking at a different workspace, or the recording never started. Work through these in order.

WorkspacesChecking which you belong to, and member management→How transcription worksThe conditions under which recording starts→Deleting and restoring notesWhat happens to deleted notes→

#Work through these in order

  1. 1

    Check which account you are signed in with

    If you have more than one Google or Microsoft account, you may be signed in with one you do not normally use. This happens most often on a company-issued machine where both a work account and a personal account are registered in the browser.

    In the app, opening “Settings” from the menu at the bottom left shows which account you are currently signed in with. Look in your inbox for a notification email from {{PRODUCT}} (sent from {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}) and compare the address it arrived at. If you are signed in with a different account, sign out and sign in again with the right email address.

  2. 2

    Check which workspace you are looking at

    You may be viewing a different workspace from the one the notes are saved in. Clicking the workspace name at the bottom left lists the workspaces you belong to. Switch to another one and check whether the notes are there.

    Notes stay in the workspace they were created in. Switching workspace does not bring notes with it. To move them to another workspace, see Moving notes between workspaces.

  3. 3

    Check you have not been removed from the workspace

    Once you are removed from a workspace's members, the notes saved in that workspace are no longer visible to you. The notes themselves remain, so asking an administrator to add you back makes the notes you could see before reappear exactly as they were. Permissions and member management are covered in Workspaces.

    The same symptom occurs when a reorganisation or a transfer changes how workspaces are arranged. Where notes remain in a former team's workspace and are no longer visible from where you are now, check with your IT department or with the administrator of your former team.

  4. 4

    Check whether that meeting was recorded at all

    Where the note for one particular meeting is missing rather than all of them, that meeting may never have been recorded. {{PRODUCT}} simply running in the menu bar or system tray does not start recording or transcription. It starts only when you do one of the following.

    • Clicked the notification at the start of a meeting
    • Opened an event whose start time had passed from “Coming up” on the home screen
    • Clicked “+ New note”
    • Left an upcoming event open and reached its start time

    If none of these happened, the audio for that meeting was never captured and cannot be recovered afterwards. The conditions for starting and stopping are covered in How transcription works.

  5. 5

    Check whether it was deleted

    Where you or another member of the same workspace deleted it, it can sometimes be restored for a period. How deletion is handled, and the steps to restore, are in Deleting and restoring notes.

  6. 6

    Clear any filters

    Where the list is filtered by folder or space, or a search term is still in place, notes that do not match are not shown. Clear the filters, return to showing all notes, and check again. How folders and spaces relate to each other is explained in Spaces and folders.

Check

Are you viewing the list with the right account, in the right workspace, with filters cleared? With those three in place, a note appears in the list as long as it still exists. If it is still not there, either it was never recorded or it has probably been deleted.

#Where notes are missing after a company account migration

Where your organisation has moved its account platform from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365, or your email domain has changed, {{PRODUCT}} treats the new account as a different account. Your earlier notes remain in the workspace of the earlier account.

What to do depends on the shape of the migration.

  • Where only the sign-in method changes, see Migrating to a Microsoft account.
  • Where you have started again as a separate account, you can move them with the steps in Moving notes from another account.
  • Where changing the email address covers it, see Account and email address changes.

What happens to notes left in a leaver's account depends on your internal rules and how the workspace is administered. Making it routine to move the notes you need into the workspace before deleting a personal account prevents them becoming unretrievable later.

#If none of this resolves it

It may just be that syncing has not caught up, so before getting in touch, sign out and back in, wait a few minutes and check the list again. If it is still not there, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Including the following helps us investigate faster.

  • The email address you sign in with
  • The name of the workspace you belong to, and whether its membership changed recently
  • The date and time of the meeting whose note is missing (in a form that shows the time zone) and the meeting name
  • Whether no notes are visible at all, or only a particular one
  • When you last saw that note, and on which screen
  • The {{PRODUCT}} app version

#Related articles

WorkspacesChecking which you belong to, and being added back→Deleting and restoring notesRestoring a deleted note→Moving notes from another accountMigrating across accounts→Moving notes between workspacesMigrating across workspaces→Calendar is not syncingWhere the event itself does not appear→

troubleshooting/network-troubleshooting.title: Network and allowlists
troubleshooting/network-troubleshooting.description: Diagnosing connection failures on corporate networks and behind proxies, and the destinations to allow.
troubleshooting/network-troubleshooting.html:
Where {{PRODUCT}} works on one network but not another, or stops working once a corporate VPN, proxy, firewall or web filtering product is enabled, traffic is probably being blocked on the network side. This article brings together what a user can narrow down themselves, and the list of destinations to share with an IT department. It is the general network article that the other troubleshooting articles refer to.

Transcription is not workingProblems capturing audio→Calendar is not syncingWhere events do not appear→Notes are not being generatedWhere no summary is produced→
Note

The {{PRODUCT}} desktop app (macOS and Windows) communicates with {{COMPANY}}'s servers and those of its processors over HTTPS and secure WebSocket. Since no recording bot joins the meeting, what matters is whether traffic from this machine is allowed, not the meeting tool's own network settings.

#Running the app's network diagnostics

The {{PRODUCT}} app has a feature that checks in one go whether it can reach the destinations it needs.

  1. 1

    Open the diagnostics screen

    Open Settings > Troubleshooting in the app.

  2. 2

    Run the check

    Choose Run check under “Network connectivity”.

  3. 3

    Read the result

    Where a problem is found, it says which features are affected.

  4. 4

    Follow the remedy shown

    Choose whether you manage the machine and network yourself or your company's IT department does, and steps for that situation are shown.

  5. 5

    Share the report

    Copy report copies the full diagnostic result to share with your IT department or with support. On a company-managed machine or network, Copy request for IT gives you a request you can send as it stands.

Where several features are failing at once, check {{PRODUCT}}'s service status page before changing any network settings. If it is an incident on the service side, no work is needed internally.

#Symptoms that point to the network

Blocking and filtering show up in forms like these.

  • Sign-in does not complete, stalls partway, or does not return to the app after authentication
  • Transcription does not start, disconnects partway, or keeps reconnecting
  • Notes or share links never finish loading
  • An AI summary or a chat response stops partway and does not continue
  • An uploaded file never finishes sending
  • Downloading an update or an installer fails
  • It does not work on the office Wi-Fi or VPN, but does work over mobile tethering
  • Certificate errors, or a message such as “cannot establish a secure connection”
  • An unexpected sign-in screen, warning page or captive portal appears

It can also simply hang with no symptom at all. Where a filtering product blocks the connection and returns a warning page or sign-in page in place of the real response, the app sees “a response, but not the right one”, and the screen stays stuck loading.

#Narrowing it down yourself

  1. 1

    Run the diagnostics

    Run the app's network diagnostics and follow the remedy shown.

  2. 2

    Try a different network

    Try mobile tethering or your home network. If it works there, the cause is most likely the corporate network, the VPN, a proxy or a filtering product.

  3. 3

    Try with the VPN or proxy off

    Where your internal rules allow it, turn the VPN or proxy off temporarily and try again. Where they do not, do not force it — share the results from the other network with your IT department instead.

  4. 4

    Check the settings on your machine

    Use “Checking the proxy settings and certificates on your machine” below to establish which proxy is in use and whether an inspection certificate is present.

  5. 5

    Share it with your IT department

    Where the symptom only occurs on the company-managed network, share the copied diagnostic report, or the template request below, with your IT department.

Check

It works normally over mobile tethering, and the symptom occurs only on the corporate network. Once you have confirmed those two things, you can take it to your IT department as a matter of the corporate network's configuration.

#Checking the proxy settings and certificates on your machine

Which proxy is in use, and whether an inspection certificate authority certificate is installed, can be seen from your operating system's settings. Including what you find in the request shortens the exchange with your IT department.

For proxy settings, select the connection in use under System Settings > Network and open Details > Proxies. Where an automatic proxy configuration (PAC file) URL is set, note that URL too.

To see whether an inspection certificate authority certificate is installed, open the Keychain Access app, select “System” and “System Roots” on the left, and search for the name of the certificate authority used internally. If no matching certificate is found, it may not have been distributed.

Proxy settings are under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy. Where “Use setup script” is enabled, note that script's URL too.

For the inspection certificate authority certificate, type certlm.msc into Run to open the certificate manager and look under Trusted Root Certification Authorities > Certificates.

Proxy settings are under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy. The items are laid out much as on Windows 11.

Checking the inspection certificate authority certificate works the same way as on Windows 11: open certlm.msc and go to Trusted Root Certification Authorities > Certificates.

#Behaviour with an always-on VPN

In configurations that route all traffic through a VPN, the long-lived WebSocket connection used for transcription can be cut by an idle timeout or a session re-authentication. Where the start of a meeting is transcribed but it stops after a few or a dozen minutes, suspect this. Where it disconnects after roughly the same elapsed time every occasion, a timeout setting is very likely involved. Ask your IT department to compare the elapsed time until disconnection against the VPN logs for that moment.

#Proxies and SSL inspection

Where a corporate proxy decrypts and inspects traffic and re-encrypts it with the organisation's own certificate authority certificate (SSL inspection), connections can fail for the following reasons.

  • The inspection certificate authority certificate has not been distributed to that machine
  • The certificate has been distributed, but is not in the certificate store the app uses
  • The inspection appliance does not let the WebSocket upgrade request through
  • The inspection appliance receives the whole response before forwarding it (buffering), so progressively delivered responses never arrive

What it comes down to is two things: whether the machine trusts the substituted certificate, and whether the inspection appliance can relay the traffic with its shape intact. The practice of substituting certificates is not itself a problem where those two things hold.

#Where file uploads stall

Corporate proxies and web filtering products often have a limit on the size that can be sent in a single request. Where small files go through but anything over a few MB fails, suspect that limit. For the file limits themselves, see File size limits.

#Blocking by security products used in Japan

Endpoint protection and data-loss prevention products distributed internally sometimes restrict traffic on a per-application basis. Where correcting the firewall and proxy settings does not help, check the blocking logs of the product on the machine. Some products return no error to the app when they block: the connection simply times out. For narrowing down cases where access to audio devices themselves is restricted, see Transcription is not working.

#A template request for your IT department

This is a template for an internal request. Every {{PRODUCT}} request is gathered here in one place. Keep only the items you need, from network allowances, operating system permissions and calendar integration approval.

Subject: Settings needed to use our meeting-notes app ({{PRODUCT}})

Hello,
This is [team / name].
{{PRODUCT}}, which we use to record meetings, is not working correctly
on our internal environment. Please could you consider the settings below.

■ What is happening
- Symptom: [e.g. transcription does not start / stops N minutes after starting /
        calendar events do not appear / no summary is generated]
- On the corporate network: reproducible
- On mobile tethering: not reproducible
- Machine: [asset number / OS and version]
- App network diagnostics: see attached

■ What we would like allowed on the firewall and proxy
- HTTPS (TCP 443) to the destinations listed below
- Secure WebSocket (wss, TCP 443) to the same destinations
  * The WebSocket upgrade and long-lived connections must be preserved
- For the streaming hosts, response buffering and content inspection
  disabled
- Where SSL inspection is in use:
  - Confirmation that the inspection CA certificate is on this machine
  - The streaming hosts above excluded from inspection
- Where DNS filtering is in use: the CNAME targets allowed as well
- Where file attachments are used: confirmation of the request size limit

■ Operating system permissions (where audio is not captured)
[On macOS]
- System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone: allow {{PRODUCT}}
- System Settings > Privacy & Security >
  Screen & System Audio Recording: allow {{PRODUCT}}
[On Windows]
- Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone:
  enable “Microphone access”
- Same screen: enable “Let desktop apps access your microphone”

■ What we would like allowed in the endpoint protection product
- In application control, allow traffic from the {{PRODUCT}} executable
- In audio device access control, add {{PRODUCT}} to the allowed list
- Confirmation of whether the traffic appears in the blocking logs

■ Calendar integration approval (where events do not appear)
[On Microsoft 365]
- Approve the {{PRODUCT}} application in the Microsoft admin centre
- Permission required: reading calendar events
[On Google Workspace]
- Allow {{PRODUCT}} under Admin console > Security > Access and data control
  > API controls > Manage third-party app access

■ Notes
- This app does not add a recording participant to the meeting tool; it captures
  the audio playing on the machine and the microphone audio on the machine itself.
- The only calendar information the app reads is the events visible to my account.
- The list of destinations is published on {{PRODUCT}}'s network requirements page.
- Audio captured will be handled in accordance with [internal request number /
  policy name].

Thank you for your help.

#For network administrators: destinations to allow

This section is for whoever configures firewalls, proxies, SSL inspection and web filtering products (including SASE products).

{{PRODUCT}} communicates over HTTPS and secure WebSocket. Let the following domains through without rewriting responses or redirecting them.

For the ordinary HTTPS domains, TLS/SSL inspection can be left enabled provided managed machines trust the inspection certificate authority and the proxy relays requests and responses without altering them.

Hosts that deliver progressively (streaming) have to return the response body in parts, in order. For those hosts, disable response buffering and content scanning. Where your product cannot inspect without buffering, exclude them from TLS inspection.

Transcription requires outbound secure WebSocket on TCP 443. Allow the WebSocket upgrade and long-lived connections. {{PRODUCT}} may connect directly or go through the operating system's proxy settings.

Domain Purpose

The delivery CDN host name Delivery of the macOS and Windows installers and automatic update files

The delivery CDN host name is a fixed host name issued by the CDN provider. Rather than allowing it with a wildcard, register the value given on the network requirements page exactly as it stands.

Where your security product supports wildcards, allowing the processor's whole domain with a wildcard prevents endpoints added later from being missed. Where it does not, register the host names individually.

The notification delivery service's endpoint Delivery of in-app notifications (including the WebSocket for real-time updates)

Allow both HTTPS and secure WebSocket for real-time notifications.

#DNS CNAME targets (for SASE and DNS filtering)

Products that judge traffic by inspecting DNS responses need the CNAME resolution targets allowed as well.

Domain Purpose
auth.{{DOMAIN}} CNAME target The DNS target of the identity platform providing sign-in and SSO
docs.{{DOMAIN}} CNAME target The DNS target of the documentation platform providing the help centre
The second hop of the CNAME chain above The DNS target of the hosting provider the documentation platform uses

#Five settings that usually do the trick in filtered environments

  1. Allow secure WebSocket traffic on TCP 443 to the transcription hosts.
  2. Disable response buffering for the hosts that deliver progressively.
  3. Check that your security product is not substituting a warning page or sign-in screen for the response.
  4. Check that name resolution succeeds on the DNS resolver you manage.
  5. Check that managed machines trust the certificate authority used for TLS inspection. Where they cannot be made to, exclude the domains concerned from inspection.

#About disclosing destinations

The lists in this article are for configuring a corporate network. What information {{PRODUCT}} sends from a user's machine to parties other than {{COMPANY}} is published separately under the Telecommunications Business Act.

LegislationTelecommunications Business Act, Article 27-12 (notices concerning instructions to transmit information)

Providers of certain telecommunications services must, before instructing a user's device to transmit information about that user to a third party's equipment, either notify the user in advance of the content of the information transmitted, the name of the party that will handle it and the purpose of use, or place that information where users can readily learn it. {{PRODUCT}} publishes the content of the information transmitted and its destinations as a list on the “Disclosures concerning external transmission” page.

Meeting audio, transcribed text and the body of notes {{PRODUCT}} generates are not among the information transmitted externally for analytics or fault detection. These are handled only to the extent needed to provide the {{PRODUCT}} service.

#If none of this resolves it

Where reviewing the network settings does not help, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} with the app's diagnostic report attached. The following helps us investigate faster.

  • The results of trying both on the corporate network and on another network (tethering, for example)
  • Your network environment (whether a VPN is in use and its product name, whether a proxy is in use, whether SSL inspection is in use, and the type of filtering product)
  • Which diagnostic items failed, and which features are affected
  • Where blocking is suspected, the proxy or endpoint protection logs for the time concerned
  • Your operating system and version, and the {{PRODUCT}} app version

On a network managed by an IT department, getting in touch with someone from that team involved reduces the back-and-forth of checking and correcting settings.

On a company-managed machine or network, Copy request for IT gives you a request you can send as it stands. Where several features are failing at once, check {{PRODUCT}}'s service status page before changing any network settings. If it is an incident on the service side, no work is needed internally. # Symptoms that point to the network Blocking and filtering show up in forms like these. Sign-in does not complete, stalls partway, or does not return to the app after authentication Transcription does not start, disconnects partway, or keeps reconnecting Notes or share links never finish loading An AI summary or a chat response stops partway and does not continue An uploaded file never finishes sending Downloading an update or an installer fails It does not work on the office Wi-Fi or VPN, but does work over mobile tethering Certificate errors, or a message such as “cannot establish a secure connection” An unexpected sign-in screen, warning page or captive portal appears It can also simply hang with no symptom at all. Check It works normally over mobile tethering, and the symptom occurs only on the corporate network. Including what you find in the request shortens the exchange with your IT department. macOS Windows 11 Windows 10 For proxy settings, select the connection in use under System Settings > Network and open Details > Proxies . Where an automatic proxy configuration (PAC file) URL is set, note that URL too. To see whether an inspection certificate authority certificate is installed, open the Keychain Access app, select “System” and “System Roots” on the left, and search for the name of the certificate authority used internally. If no matching certificate is found, it may not have been distributed. Proxy settings are under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy . Where “Use setup script” is enabled, note that script's URL too. For the inspection certificate authority certificate, type certlm.msc into Run to open the certificate manager and look under Trusted Root Certification Authorities > Certificates . Proxy settings are under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy . The items are laid out much as on Windows 11. Where the start of a meeting is transcribed but it stops after a few or a dozen minutes, suspect this. Where it disconnects after roughly the same elapsed time every occasion, a timeout setting is very likely involved. Ask your IT department to compare the elapsed time until disconnection against the VPN logs for that moment. # Proxies and SSL inspection Where a corporate proxy decrypts and inspects traffic and re-encrypts it with the organisation's own certificate authority certificate (SSL inspection), connections can fail for the following reasons. The inspection certificate authority certificate has not been distributed to that machine The certificate has been distributed, but is not in the certificate store the app uses The inspection appliance does not let the WebSocket upgrade request through The inspection appliance receives the whole response before forwarding it (buffering), so progressively delivered responses never arrive What it comes down to is two things: whether the machine trusts the substituted certificate, and whether the inspection appliance can relay the traffic with its shape intact. For the file limits themselves, see File size limits . # Blocking by security products used in Japan Endpoint protection and data-loss prevention products distributed internally sometimes restrict traffic on a per-application basis. Where correcting the firewall and proxy settings does not help, check the blocking logs of the product on the machine. Some products return no error to the app when they block: the connection simply times out. For narrowing down cases where access to audio devices themselves is restricted, see Transcription is not working . # A template request for your IT department This is a template for an internal request. Every {{PRODUCT}} request is gathered here in one place. Keep only the items you need, from network allowances, operating system permissions and calendar integration approval. Please could you consider the settings below. ■ What is happening - Symptom: [e.g. transcription does not start / stops N minutes after starting / calendar events do not appear / no summary is generated] - On the corporate network: reproducible - On mobile tethering: not reproducible - Machine: [asset number / OS and version] - App network diagnostics: see attached ■ What we would like allowed on the firewall and proxy - HTTPS (TCP 443) to the destinations listed below - Secure WebSocket (wss, TCP 443) to the same destinations * The WebSocket upgrade and long-lived connections must be preserved - For the streaming hosts, response buffering and content inspection disabled - Where SSL inspection is in use: - Confirmation that the inspection CA certificate is on this machine - The streaming hosts above excluded from inspection - Where DNS filtering is in use: the CNAME targets allowed as well - Where file attachments are used: confirmation of the request size limit ■ Operating system permissions (where audio is not captured) [On macOS] - System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone: allow {{PRODUCT}} - System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording: allow {{PRODUCT}} [On Windows] - Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone: enable “Microphone access” - Same screen: enable “Let desktop apps access your microphone” ■ What we would like allowed in the endpoint protection product - In application control, allow traffic from the {{PRODUCT}} executable - In audio device access control, add {{PRODUCT}} to the allowed list - Confirmation of whether the traffic appears in the blocking logs ■ Calendar integration approval (where events do not appear) [On Microsoft 365] - Approve the {{PRODUCT}} application in the Microsoft admin centre - Permission required: reading calendar events [On Google Workspace] - Allow {{PRODUCT}} under Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage third-party app access ■ Notes - This app does not add a recording participant to the meeting tool; it captures the audio playing on the machine and the microphone audio on the machine itself. - The only calendar information the app reads is the events visible to my account. - The list of destinations is published on {{PRODUCT}}'s network requirements page. - Audio captured will be handled in accordance with [internal request number / policy name].
