troubleshooting/notes-not-generating.title: Notes are not being generated
troubleshooting/notes-not-generating.description: Retrying, and working out the cause, when no summary is produced after a meeting.
troubleshooting/notes-not-generating.html:
This covers what to do when a meeting has finished but no formatted note appears, when you see a message saying generation failed, or when a blank note is produced. Working through it in order separates the cases a retry fixes from those where no transcript was captured in the first place.

AI-formatted notesRegenerating, and changing template→Transcription is not workingWhere no audio was captured→Network and allowlistsWhere you suspect traffic is being blocked→
Note

{{PRODUCT}} generates a note automatically once a meeting has ended and a transcript has been captured. The summary is built from the transcript, so generation cannot succeed for a meeting with no transcript. A notification arrives when generation finishes. If your settings mean no notification arrives, check Notification settings.

#Try these in order

  1. 1

    Wait a few minutes

    For a long meeting, or on a slow connection, generation can take a few minutes. A notification arrives when it is ready.

  2. 2

    Press the retry button

    Where the message saying generation failed has a retry button, click it. A retry connects to the AI model over a different route from the first attempt. Where the cause was a temporary connection failure, this generates the note.

  3. 3

    Regenerate it by hand

    Where there is no retry button, or where a blank note was produced, run the regeneration yourself. At the top of the note, switch to the tab showing the formatted note, click the downward arrow beside the tab name, and in the menu that appears click the regenerate button (🔁) beside the template in use. You can also open the template list from the “✨” button at the top right of the note and use the same regenerate button. That, and how to rebuild it with a different template, are explained in AI-formatted notes.

  4. 4

    Check whether a transcript was captured

    Where regenerating still produces nothing, check whether a transcript exists at all. Clicking the three-vertical-lines icon on the floating bar at the bottom of the note opens the transcript panel.

    Where there is no transcript at all, there is nothing for the summary to work from and generation cannot succeed. That means no audio was captured. The same goes for an extremely short transcript: where only the other person's voice, or only your own, is present, permission for either system audio or the microphone may be missing. Check your audio device settings and operating system permissions using the steps in Transcription is not working.

  5. 5

    Check the language setting

    Where the transcript or the note is in an unintended language, see Multi-language support to set the meeting language, then regenerate. In meetings that mix Japanese and English, the output can be inconsistent depending on the setting.

Check

There is a reasonable amount of the meeting in the transcript panel, and running a regeneration still produces no note. In that state, the cause lies on the generation side. Go on to the network checks below.

A meeting that was not recorded cannot be recovered later

A note cannot be rebuilt afterwards for a meeting with no transcript. Audio is captured on your machine as it happens, so there is no way to obtain the audio alone after the meeting has ended. Before an important meeting, check everything works using the test steps in Transcription is not working.

#Where the network is the cause

On a corporate network, a VPN or behind a firewall, traffic needed for generation can be blocked and the process fail. The summary is delivered progressively, so where a proxy is configured to receive the whole response before forwarding it (buffering), generation can stall without progressing. Where the transcript is fine and only the summary stalls, suspect this.

Switching to a different network and seeing whether the symptom disappears narrows it down. The steps for doing that, the symptoms blocking produces, the list of destinations to allow and a template request for your IT department are all in Network and allowlists.

#If none of this resolves it

If the steps above do not resolve it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Including the following helps us investigate faster.

  • The date and time of the meeting concerned (in a form that shows the time zone) and roughly how long it was
  • Whether a transcript remains in the transcript panel, and roughly how much
  • The name of the template in use
  • How many times you tried a retry or a regeneration, and what happened
  • The error message shown on screen (in its exact wording, if there is one)
  • Your network environment (corporate LAN, VPN or not, proxy or not)
  • The {{PRODUCT}} app version

Please do not delete the note concerned until the investigation is finished. Deleting it loses the transcript with it, and the cause can no longer be identified.

troubleshooting/transcription-issues.title: Transcription is not working
troubleshooting/transcription-issues.description: What to do, by operating system, when no audio is captured, it stops partway, or accuracy is poor.
troubleshooting/transcription-issues.html:
This brings together how to narrow down symptoms such as transcription not starting, picking up only your own voice, or stopping partway. Most causes are one of three: the system's default audio device does not match the meeting tool's settings, an operating system permission has not been granted, or traffic is blocked on the corporate network. Working through it from the top gets you to the cause quickly.

How transcription worksThe conditions under which transcription starts and stops→Network and allowlistsWhere a proxy or firewall is the cause→Notes are not being generatedWhere there is a transcript but no summary is produced→
Note

{{PRODUCT}} transcribes by capturing your computer's microphone and system audio (the sound your computer is playing) directly in the desktop app. No recording bot joins the meeting tool, and no separate recording app is used. Two things are needed for it to work: the desktop app (macOS or Windows) running, and the note for the meeting concerned open (or a new note created). Simply sitting in the menu bar or system tray does not start recording. The macOS version requires macOS 14 or later. The web version (in a browser) only supports viewing and editing notes that already exist; it cannot record or transcribe.

When transcription starts and stops is explained in How transcription works.

#Six things to try first

Before going into the detailed steps, work through these six in order. They resolve it in most cases.

  1. 1

    Restart the app

    Right-click the {{PRODUCT}} icon — in the Dock on macOS, in the system tray on Windows (under the “^” at the right of the taskbar) — and choose “Restart {{PRODUCT}}”. Where the transcription connection has been left dropped, this brings it back.

  2. 2

    Match your audio devices to your meeting tool

    The system's default microphone and speaker (on Windows, the default communication device) have to be the same as the devices selected in your meeting tool. The steps are under “Matching your system audio devices to your meeting tool”.

  3. 3

    Check permissions

    Both microphone permission and permission to capture system audio are needed. The steps are under “Checking audio permissions”.

  4. 4

    Review Bluetooth and external devices

    Where you use Bluetooth headphones or external speakers, set them as the default device (and the default communication device). Some Bluetooth and USB devices drop out; where transcription stops after a few minutes, try the built-in microphone or a different device.

  5. 5

    Check your macOS version

    {{PRODUCT}} requires macOS 14 or later. On anything older, updating macOS can resolve it. The version is under “Apple menu > About This Mac”.

  6. 6

    Check the language setting

    Where notes or transcripts come out in an unintended language, see Multi-language support and set the meeting language. Transcription uses the language set on the account or the workspace.

If that has not fixed it, work through the sections below in order.

#Checking transcription is working

You can test this on its own, without waiting for a real meeting.

  1. 1

    Play some audio

    Play a video or some music with speech in it on your computer. Using the demo meeting video {{COMPANY}} provides reproduces a situation with several people speaking.

  2. 2

    Create a new note

    Create a “New note” in {{PRODUCT}}.

  3. 3

    Check system audio

    A green bar moving in time with the sound at the bottom of the note means system audio is being captured.

  4. 4

    Open the transcript panel

    Clicking that bar opens the transcript panel. The audio playing appearing in grey text means it is working.

  5. 5

    Check your own voice

    Now speak yourself. Your own voice is added in green text.

Check

Both grey text (system audio) and green text (microphone) appearing means audio capture is working. Where only one of them appears, check the settings and permissions for that device. Where neither appears, it is most likely that the app cannot reach the servers that do the transcription, so go on to the network checks.

#Matching your system audio devices to your meeting tool

{{PRODUCT}} captures meeting audio using the operating system's default audio devices. Where the devices selected in a meeting tool such as Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Zoom or Slack do not match the operating system's defaults, you get symptoms such as only the other person's voice missing, or only your own. Where the settings live depends on your operating system.

System Settings > Sound — open it and check the “Output” and “Input” tabs. On some macOS versions it is “System Preferences > Sound”.

  • Output: check the device selected on the “Output” tab is the speaker or headphones actually playing the sound. Do not select a USB microphone as the output. Some USB microphones are recognised as both an input and an output device, and choosing one as the output makes it impossible to capture other participants' audio separately. Match it to the speaker selected in your meeting tool.
  • Input: check the microphone selected on the “Input” tab is the same as the one selected in your meeting tool. Where you use an external microphone, select that microphone directly rather than going through a virtual audio device.

Settings > System > Sound — open it. {{PRODUCT}} uses the output and input set as the default devices. The default device is selected with the round button to the left of each device.

Where different devices are set as the default device and the default communication device, {{PRODUCT}} uses the default device for output (other people's voices and system audio) and the default communication device for input (your own voice).

To change this, scroll down the sound settings screen and open “More sound settings”. In the window that opens, right-click the device you want and choose “Set as Default Communication Device”. Do the same for your microphone on the “Recording” tab.

Once set, check it matches the device selected in your meeting tool. Testing with the meeting tool actually running is the reliable way.

Settings > System > Sound > Playback — open it. What {{PRODUCT}} uses is the same as on Windows 11: the default device for output and the default communication device for input.

To change it, right-click the device you want on the “Playback” tab and choose “Set as Default Communication Device”. Do the same for the microphone you want on the “Recording” tab.

Here too, check it matches what is selected in your meeting tool.

Type The Windows setting {{PRODUCT}} uses
Output (other people's voices and system audio) Default device
Input (your own voice) Default communication device

#Turning audio enhancements off (Windows only)

Enhancement features that come with audio devices can interfere with {{PRODUCT}}'s audio capture. Where transcription is unstable, turn them off. macOS has no such setting.

Type “sound settings” into the Start menu, or open Settings > System > Sound.

  1. Click the right-facing arrow on the row for each sound device to open that device's properties.
  2. Find the item called “Audio Enhancements” and change it to “Off”.
  3. Do the same for input devices.

While you are there, try switching “Mono audio” on under Settings > System > Sound. Some audio devices do not sit well with {{PRODUCT}} in stereo.

Type “sound settings” into the Start menu and open it, or open the sound control panel from Settings > System > Sound > Playback.

  1. Right-click the device you use and choose “Properties”.
  2. Clear the “Enable audio enhancements” checkbox and click “OK”.
  3. Do the same for your microphone on the “Recording” tab.

If that does not help, try switching “Mono audio” on.

#Checking audio permissions

Permission is needed for both system audio and the microphone. With only one of them, you end up recording only your own voice, or only the other person's. Where the settings live depends on your operating system.

  1. Open “System Settings”. On some macOS versions it is “System Preferences”.
  2. Open “Privacy & Security” and choose “Microphone”.
  3. Find {{PRODUCT}} in the list and switch it on.
  4. Switch {{PRODUCT}} on under “Screen & System Audio Recording” in the same “Privacy & Security” section too. On some macOS versions the item is shown simply as “Screen Recording”.

Immediately after changing a permission, you may be asked to restart the app. If you are, restart it and test again.

Check that microphone use by desktop apps is not blocked across the board.

  1. Open “Settings”.
  2. Open “Privacy & security > Microphone”.
  3. Switch “Microphone access” on.
  4. Scroll down and switch “Let desktop apps access your microphone” on.

Check that microphone use by desktop apps is not blocked across the board.

  1. Open “Settings”.
  2. Open “Privacy > Microphone”. On Windows 11 it is called “Privacy & security > Microphone”.
  3. Switch “Microphone access” on.
  4. Scroll down and switch “Let desktop apps access your microphone” on.
Check

Once permissions are set, run the test under “Checking transcription is working” again. Both grey and green text appearing means the permissions are granted correctly.

#Antivirus and endpoint protection products (Windows)

Where permissions and audio devices are both correct and audio still is not captured, check whether a security product on the machine is blocking access to audio devices.

#Kaspersky

Kaspersky antivirus products are known to block {{PRODUCT}}'s access to audio devices, stopping transcription working. Where you have Kaspersky and transcription does not work, add {{PRODUCT}} to Kaspersky's allowlist. The steps are in Kaspersky's help (allowing an application to access audio devices).

#Other endpoint protection products

At Japanese companies, endpoint protection products distributed to machines (EDR, asset management and data-loss prevention software of various kinds) sometimes restrict applications' access to the microphone or system audio, or their traffic to the outside. Check the following with your IT department.

  • Whether per-application control of audio device use is enabled
  • Whether {{PRODUCT}}'s executable is being monitored or blocked as an unknown application
  • Whether {{PRODUCT}}'s destinations appear in the traffic blocking logs

Some products return no error to the app when they block: the audio is simply treated as silence. “Permissions are right but the green bar does not move at all” is the classic sign of this kind of blocking.

#Reviewing audio mixing hardware and software

Where you use hardware or software that adds extra processing to the audio — a USB microphone amplifier, an audio interface, mixing software that combines several microphone inputs — it can interfere with {{PRODUCT}}'s capture. If none of that applies to you, skip this section.

If disabling or bypassing them temporarily makes {{PRODUCT}} work, that is where the cause lies. To carry on using them, check the following.

  • Turn pass-through (loopback) off — this is the setting that sends microphone input to both the input and the output. Left on, your own microphone audio is transcribed as another participant's voice.
  • In stereo, send the audio to the left channel — {{PRODUCT}} assumes mono audio. Where the device is set to stereo it reads the left channel, so make sure audio is sent to the left (or to both).
  • Make sure audio reaches both your call software and {{PRODUCT}} — where the voice chat or microphone path goes only to the meeting tool, no sound reaches {{PRODUCT}}.

#Virtual desktop environments (VDI / Citrix / Azure Virtual Desktop)

Where you run {{PRODUCT}} inside a virtual desktop session, only microphone audio may be captured and other participants' audio (system audio) may not. In that case only what you say is transcribed and the other side is missing.

The remedy is to install and run {{PRODUCT}} on the machine in front of you rather than inside the virtual desktop session. Where your internal rules require it to be used on the virtual desktop, you will need to discuss an audio redirection configuration with your IT department.

#Audio quality drops on a Bluetooth headset

Where quality drops the moment transcription starts, that is a constraint of how Bluetooth headsets work. Most headsets cannot handle high-quality audio output and microphone input at the same time. When {{PRODUCT}} uses the headset's microphone, the headset switches to the lower-quality call mode.

To avoid this, set your computer's built-in microphone as the default input device in the system sound settings. The headset is then output only, and keeps its quality.

Note

On macOS, the default input device setting can revert every time a Bluetooth headset is disconnected and reconnected. Set it again after each reconnection.

#Restarting your computer

Where the process used to capture system audio is left stopped, restarting the app does not bring it back but restarting the computer can. If the steps so far have not resolved it, restart the whole machine.

#Where the network is the cause

Where you have been through audio devices, permissions and restarting and transcription still does not work, the network, a VPN, a proxy, a firewall or a web filtering product may be the cause. Transcription uses a long-lived secure WebSocket connection, which makes it particularly sensitive to how a corporate network is configured. Where the start of a meeting is transcribed but it stops after a few minutes, a VPN or proxy connection-lifetime setting may be involved.

The steps for narrowing it down, the symptoms blocking produces, the list of destinations to allow and a template request for your IT department are all in Network and allowlists. Where you are on a company-issued machine and cannot change operating system permissions or audio device settings yourself, that same template has a section for permissions.

#If none of this resolves it

If the steps above do not resolve it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Including the following helps us investigate faster.

  • What the symptom is (nothing transcribed at all / only your voice / only the other person's / stops partway)
  • Where it stops partway, roughly how long it runs before stopping
  • The audio device you were using (built-in microphone, Bluetooth headset, USB microphone and so on, including the model)
  • The meeting tool you were using (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and so on)
  • Your operating system and version (for example macOS 15.3, Windows 11 23H2) and the {{PRODUCT}} app version
  • The result of the test under “Checking transcription is working” (whether grey text and green text appeared)
  • Your network environment (corporate LAN, VPN or not, proxy or not)

On a company-issued machine, where you do not know how the endpoint protection product or proxy is configured, getting in touch together with someone from your IT department reduces the back-and-forth.

signing-in-and-connecting-your-calendar.title: Signing in and connecting your calendar
signing-in-and-connecting-your-calendar.description: Signing in with Google, Microsoft or SSO, and how multi-factor authentication works.
signing-in-and-connecting-your-calendar.html:
There are three ways to sign in to {{PRODUCT}}: a Google account, a Microsoft account, or single sign-on (SSO). All three take you through to connecting your calendar in one go, and the events on the connected calendar are what {{PRODUCT}} uses to work out when meetings begin and end. This article covers what is common to all three.

Enterprise plan

Signing in with a Microsoft accountWhat to do where administrator approval is required→Connecting your calendarUsing several calendars, and what is shown→Calendar is not syncingThe order to check things in when events do not appear→
Note

Signing in and connecting your calendar are done from the desktop app (macOS and Windows). The web version supports viewing and editing notes that already exist; it cannot change sign-in method or connect a calendar. Single sign-on (SSO) is available on the Enterprise plan only.

#Choosing a sign-in method

Choose according to the email and calendar environment at your workplace. You can change later.

Your workplace environment Sign-in method to choose Calendar connected
Google Workspace or Gmail Sign in with Google Google Calendar
Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online) Sign in with Microsoft The Outlook calendar
Centrally managed on an internal identity platform (SAML / OIDC) Sign in with SSO Choose Google or Microsoft to connect after signing in
On-premises Exchange is not supported

{{PRODUCT}} can connect to calendars on cloud Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online). It cannot connect to an on-premises Exchange Server run in your own data centre or server room. In a hybrid setup where some users' mailboxes remain on premises, those users may not be able to retrieve their calendar even after signing in with Microsoft.

#Signing in with a Google account

These are the steps where you use a Google Workspace or Gmail account. Google Calendar is connected as you sign in.

  1. 1

    Choose Sign in with Google

    Start {{PRODUCT}} and click Sign in with Google.

  2. 2

    Choose the account your calendar is on

    On the account selection screen, choose the account whose calendar you normally use. If you have both a work and a personal account, choose the one your meetings are in.

  3. 3

    Allow calendar access

    Read what the permission screen says and allow it. This permission is needed to read event titles, start and end times and participants, to show notifications around meetings, and to use that as context for your notes.

Once allowed, you are returned to {{PRODUCT}} automatically and are signed in.

#Signing in with a Microsoft account

These are the steps where you use Microsoft 365 and the Outlook calendar.

  1. 1

    Choose Sign in with Microsoft

    Start {{PRODUCT}} and click Sign in with Microsoft.

  2. 2

    Choose your work account

    On the account selection screen, choose the account your work calendar is on.

  3. 3

    Allow calendar access

    Read what the permission screen says and allow it.

Once done, you are returned to {{PRODUCT}} with the Outlook calendar connected.

Where a screen appears partway through saying administrator approval is required, your organisation's tenant settings prevent individual users granting permissions to new apps. The permissions requested, how to ask for approval, an example request to send to your IT department, and what the administrator does are all covered in Signing in with a Microsoft account.

#Signing in with SSO (Enterprise plan)

Signing in with single sign-on (SSO) is available on the Enterprise plan. If you are considering it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. It is configured individually for each organisation.

With SSO, authentication and connecting the calendar are two separate stages.

  1. 1

    Start the app and choose SSO

    Install and start {{PRODUCT}} and choose Sign in with SSO.

  2. 2

    Authenticate on your organisation's screen

    Authenticate the same way you normally sign in to internal systems. Depending on your organisation's settings, administrator approval may be required at this point.

  3. 3

    Choose your calendar provider

    Once authenticated, you move on to the screen for connecting a calendar. Choose whichever your organisation uses, Google Calendar or Microsoft / Outlook calendar.

  4. 4

    Allow calendar access

    On the chosen provider's screen, allow access to the calendar.

Even where SSO authentication succeeds, skipping the last two steps means no calendar events are pulled in. Where events do not appear in the list, check first whether the calendar connection was completed.

Check
  • Today's and the next few events are listed on the home screen
  • The email address you signed in with is shown at the bottom left
  • Opening an event shows the meeting start time and the participants

#How multi-factor authentication (MFA) works

{{PRODUCT}} has no multi-factor authentication mechanism of its own. Authentication itself is delegated to Google, Microsoft or your organisation's SSO platform.

So to apply multi-factor authentication to signing in to {{PRODUCT}}, configure it at the provider. Enabling two-step verification on a Google account, multi-factor authentication in Microsoft Entra ID, or a policy on your SSO platform means the requirement applies when signing in to {{PRODUCT}} too. Conditional access (allowing only from particular networks or managed devices, for example) applies in the same way.

#Using more than one account

You can register several accounts — work and personal, for example — and switch between them. The arrow icon beside the email address at the bottom left lets you add and switch accounts. Notes and calendars are separate per account, so switching changes what you see.

Where you are moving from a Google account to a Microsoft account, how notes carry over depends on your situation. See Switching to a Microsoft account.

#Signing out

  1. Click your workspace name at the bottom left.
  2. Settings — open it.
  3. Scroll the settings sidebar to the bottom and click Sign out.

Signing out does not delete your notes. Signing in again with the same account returns everything to how it was. When you part with a device, or finish using a shared one, sign out and also remove the app itself following Uninstalling and reinstalling.

#If something is not working

Q. With a Gmail account it says “join the waiting list”

A. Just press the join the waiting list button shown. There is no actual wait; sign-in completes straight away. It appears while acceptance of personal Gmail addresses is being opened up in stages.

Q. It says “administrator approval required” and will not go further (Microsoft / SSO)

A. Your organisation’s tenant settings prevent users granting permissions to apps themselves. Ask your IT department for approval. Once approved, other users in the same organisation are not asked again. The exact steps for the person approving, and an example request email, are in Signing in with a Microsoft account.

Q. It says “Access blocked: this app must be reviewed by your administrator” (Google)

A. Your Google Workspace administrator restricts third-party app access. Ask them to open Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage third-party app access in the Google admin console, add {{PRODUCT}} to the allowlist and set it to “trusted”. Once set, try signing in again.

Q. I cannot sign in from the corporate network

A. Your firewall or proxy may be blocking the authentication traffic. Ask your IT department to add HTTPS traffic to the authentication domain (auth.{{DOMAIN}}) to the allowlist. The list of destinations that need allowing, and how to narrow the problem down, are in Network and allowlists.

Q. I signed in but no calendar events appear

A. Where you signed in with SSO, authentication and connecting the calendar are separate steps; check that you completed the calendar connection. Where you signed in with Google or Microsoft, check you did not untick the calendar item on the permissions screen. If they still do not appear, narrow it down using Calendar is not syncing.

Q. I want to change the email address I sign in with

A. Changing the email address tied to an account and moving to a different account are different procedures. See Account and email address changes. To carry notes over to an account on a different email address, use the steps in Moving notes from another account.

All three take you through to connecting your calendar in one go, and the events on the connected calendar are what {{PRODUCT}} uses to work out when meetings begin and end. This article covers what is common to all three. Enterprise plan Signing in with a Microsoft account What to do where administrator approval is required → Connecting your calendar Using several calendars, and what is shown → Calendar is not syncing The order to check things in when events do not appear → Note Signing in and connecting your calendar are done from the desktop app (macOS and Windows). The web version supports viewing and editing notes that already exist; it cannot change sign-in method or connect a calendar. sign-in-with-microsoft.title: Signing in with a Microsoft account
sign-in-with-microsoft.description: How to sign in with a Microsoft 365 account, and what to do when administrator consent is required.
sign-in-with-microsoft.html:
Signing in to {{PRODUCT}} with a Microsoft 365 account connects your Outlook calendar as you go, and meeting notes are created to match your events. This article explains what users and administrators each need to do where “administrator approval required” appears partway through signing in.

Signing in and connecting your calendarChoosing between the three sign-in methods→Switching to a Microsoft accountMoving from a Google account→Bulk installation and updates by an administratorDistribution to devices, and updates→
Note

This article covers only signing in with a Microsoft account. The only calendars that can be connected are those on cloud Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online); on-premises Exchange Server is out of scope. Choosing a sign-in method, SSO and multi-factor authentication are covered in Signing in and connecting your calendar. These steps are carried out in the desktop app (macOS and Windows).

#When it says “approval required”

A screen asking for approval can appear partway through signing in. That is because {{PRODUCT}} is requesting permission to read your calendar events, and your settings do not let individual users decide to grant it. In Japanese companies' Microsoft 365 tenants this setting is often left at its default, so it is nothing unusual.

#The permissions {{PRODUCT}} asks for

{{PRODUCT}} asks Microsoft 365 for the three permissions below. All are read-only: it does not ask to write to your calendar or mail, or to access files.

Permission What it covers
User.Read Reading basic profile information: your name and email address
Calendars.Read Reading events on your own calendar
Calendars.Read.Shared Reading events on shared calendars you have access to

In addition, it uses the standard authentication scopes needed for sign-in itself (openid, email, profile and offline_access). offline_access is what saves you signing in again every time you start the app.

How the calendar information obtained is handled is set out in the privacy policy and the security and privacy FAQ.

#For users: asking for approval

Where a Request approval button appears on screen, you can apply to your administrator there and then.

  1. 1

    Click Request approval

    Click Request approval on the consent screen.

  2. 2

    Give a reason and send it

    A field for your reason appears; fill it in so the purpose is clear and send it. There is an example at the end of this section.

  3. 3

    Sign in again once approved

    When an administrator approves it you will usually be notified by email. Start {{PRODUCT}} again and retry from Sign in with Microsoft.

For the reason, something like this works.

Used to create meeting notes automatically. Permission to read calendar events is needed
so that the start and end of meetings are identified correctly and the events can be used
as context when summarising what was discussed.
The permissions requested are read-only; nothing is written to the calendar or to mail.

#An example request to your IT department

Where your organisation has a separate approval process, or where no request button appears, you will need to ask your IT department directly. Here is a template containing the items Japanese companies typically need. Replace the bracketed parts with your own details.

Subject: Request for tenant approval of our meeting-notes tool ({{PRODUCT}})

To the IT team

Hello. This is [name] in [team].

We are considering using a tool called {{PRODUCT}} to make writing up meetings more efficient.
Signing in with a Microsoft 365 account requires tenant administrator approval, so I am
writing to ask you to look at it.

■ Purpose
　[e.g. writing up the weekly team meeting and client meetings]

■ Permissions requested (all read-only)
　- User.Read (reading name and email address)
　- Calendars.Read (reading events on my own calendar)
　- Calendars.Read.Shared (reading events on shared calendars I have access to)
　* No write permission to calendar, mail or files is requested.

■ How to approve
　Microsoft Entra admin centre > Entra ID > Enterprise applications >
　Admin consent requests > Pending requests, and approve the request there.
　The detailed steps are in the help centre article “Signing in with a Microsoft account”.

■ Notes
　- The only calendars connected are those on cloud Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online).
　- If you need material on how recordings and transcripts are handled, where they are
　　stored and for how long, I can provide it separately.
　- Trial period: [e.g. DD/MM to DD/MM]
　- Cost: [e.g. team budget / none, as it is the free plan]

Please let me know if you have any questions. Thank you.
Where there is an internal information security review

In organisations where the information security team reviews any new SaaS, you are often asked, on top of the list of permissions, for where data is stored, for how long, whether there are processors, and what encryption is used. Reading Our security arrangements and the security and privacy FAQ beforehand makes filling in the review form easier. If there are items you cannot answer, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

#For administrators: approving the request

These are the steps for handling a user's approval request as a Microsoft 365 tenant administrator.

  1. 1

    Open the Microsoft Entra admin centre

    Microsoft Entra admin centre — sign in with an administrator account.

  2. 2

    Open pending requests

    Entra ID > Enterprise applications > Admin consent requests > Pending requests — open it.

  3. 3

    Select the request

    Select the request for {{PRODUCT}} from the list.

  4. 4

    Review the permissions and approve

    Review permissions and consent — click it, check the permissions shown and click Approve.

Once approved, users in the same tenant can sign in without being asked for approval again.

About the scope of the approval

The approval here permits the {{PRODUCT}} application across the whole tenant. Where you want to limit it to particular teams, the usual approach is to enable “User assignment required” in the enterprise application settings afterwards and specify the groups to assign. Decide according to your organisation's policy.

#Where there is no “Request approval” button

Sometimes a user sees only “administrator approval required”, with no Request approval button. That is because admin consent requests are disabled in the tenant.

An administrator should make the following setting.

  1. 1

    Open the Microsoft Entra admin centre

    Microsoft Entra admin centre — sign in with an administrator account.

  2. 2

    Open admin consent settings

    Entra ID > Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions > Admin consent settings — open it.

  3. 3

    Allow consent requests

    Switch “Users can request admin consent to apps they are unable to consent to” to Yes.

  4. 4

    Ask the user to sign in again

    When the user tries signing in again, the Request approval button now appears. Approve the request that arrives following the steps in the previous section.

#Where “admin consent requests” cannot be enabled

Where your organisation's policy does not allow this feature to be enabled, an administrator can sign in to {{PRODUCT}} themselves and give tenant-wide consent there and then.

  1. 1

    Start the app with an administrator account

    Install and start {{PRODUCT}} with an administrator account.

  2. 2

    Choose Sign in with Microsoft

    Sign in with Microsoft — click it.

  3. 3

    Tick consent on behalf of the organisation

    Tick the Consent on behalf of your organisation checkbox on the consent screen.

  4. 4

    Accept

    Accept — click it.

Doing this completes the administrator's own sign-in and at the same time makes {{PRODUCT}} usable across the tenant.

Check
  • Users can sign in from Sign in with Microsoft without an approval screen
  • Outlook events appear on the home screen
  • {{PRODUCT}} is listed among the enterprise applications in Entra ID
Take care not to miss the checkbox

Consent on behalf of your organisation — accepting without ticking it grants the permission only to the administrator's own account. Other users still cannot sign in. Check the box is ticked before accepting.

#Where the administrator cannot sign in either

Where none of the approaches above is possible, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. We will look at your tenant's configuration and advise.

#If something is not working

Q. I approved it, but the user still cannot sign in

A. Approval can take a few minutes to take effect. Ask the user to quit {{PRODUCT}}, start it again and try signing in. If the same screen still appears, “User assignment required” may be enabled in the enterprise application settings and that user may not be in an assigned group.

Q. I can sign in, but no calendar events appear

A. Where the calendar is on an on-premises Exchange Server, events cannot be retrieved. Also, where a conditional access policy allows access only from particular networks or managed devices, syncing can stop in environments that do not meet the conditions. For how to narrow it down, see Calendar is not syncing.

Q. I want to revoke an app permission I approved

A. Select {{PRODUCT}} under Enterprise applications in the Microsoft Entra admin centre and either delete the application or remove the assignment. Revoking it means users in that tenant can no longer sign in with a Microsoft account, and syncing of connected calendars stops. For what happens to notes already created, see Deleting your account.

Q. I cannot reach the Microsoft sign-in screen from the corporate network

A. A proxy or firewall may be blocking the authentication traffic. The destinations that need allowing, and how to narrow it down, are in Network and allowlists.

#Related articles

Signing in and connecting your calendarSigning in generally, including Google and SSO→Switching to a Microsoft accountMoving over from a Google account→Connecting your calendarWorking with several calendars→Our security arrangementsThe items asked about in internal reviews→

migrating-to-a-microsoft-account.title: Switching to a Microsoft account
migrating-to-a-microsoft-account.description: Moving from a Google account to a Microsoft account, and carrying your notes over.
migrating-to-a-microsoft-account.html:
This article is for people who use the Outlook calendar but have been signing in to {{PRODUCT}} with a Google account as a stopgap. Switching to signing in with a Microsoft account connects the calendar directly and makes pulling in events more reliable. Here are the steps for switching, and how to carry your past notes over to the new account.

Signing in with a Microsoft accountWhere administrator approval is required→Moving notes from another accountThe import in detail, and its limits→Signing in and connecting your calendarSigning in generally→
Note

This article covers only the switch. The only calendars that can be connected are those on cloud Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online). Where you run an on-premises Exchange Server, switching will not let the calendar be retrieved, so check first. Signing in generally is covered in Signing in and connecting your calendar, and the case where administrator approval is required in Signing in with a Microsoft account. These steps are carried out in the desktop app (macOS and Windows).

#Before you start

The steps differ depending on whether the email address you use now and the email address of the Microsoft account you are moving to are the same.

Situation What you need to do What happens to your notes
The Google account and the Microsoft account have the same email address (your employer moved from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365, say) Just sign out and sign in again with Microsoft They stay as they are. No import needed
The email addresses differ (you were using a personal Gmail address and your employer is on Microsoft 365, say) Sign out, sign in with Microsoft, then import your notes Moved by the import. It is a move, not a copy

Where the email address is the same, the account itself does not change, so notes, folders, templates and recipes are all kept exactly as they are.

#The steps

  1. 1

    Sign out of your current account

    Click your workspace name at the bottom left and open Settings. Scroll the sidebar to the bottom and click Sign out. Signing out does not delete the account or your notes. Signing in again with the original account returns everything to how it was.

  2. 2

    Sign in with a Microsoft account

    On the sign-in screen click Sign in with Microsoft and follow the Microsoft authentication screens. When asked to allow calendar access, read what it says and allow it. Where it says administrator approval is required, your tenant administrator has to approve it. How to ask for approval, and what the administrator does, are covered in Signing in with a Microsoft account.

  3. 3

    Carry your past notes over

    Where you signed in with the same email address as before, you go straight into your existing account and this step is not needed. Where you signed in with a different address, a new empty account is created, so go to Settings > Profile and use Import notes from another account, entering your previous email address. Entering the six-digit verification code sent to that inbox starts the import. The import moves the notes; none are left in the previous account. The code's expiry, and what to do if the import item is not shown, are covered in Moving notes from another account.

Check
  • Outlook events appear on the home screen
  • The Microsoft account's email address is shown at the bottom left
  • If you ran an import, your earlier notes are in the list

#Where you end up

  • Outlook events now sync directly through the Microsoft account. The workaround of connecting through a Google account is no longer needed.
  • Imported notes appear in the new account, in the workspace that was open when you ran the import.
  • How folders, templates and paid subscriptions are handled is the same as for the import generally. What comes across and what does not is covered in Moving notes from another account.
  • The paid subscription stays with the old account. To use paid features on the new account, take out a new subscription from Settings > Billing. Once the old account's subscription is no longer needed, cancel it there. For the steps, see About cancellation.

You can also keep the old Gmail account and use it for personal events. The arrow icon beside the email address at the bottom left lets you add and switch accounts.

Timing a switch at work

Where your employer is moving everyone from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365, switching {{PRODUCT}} after the internal email migration is complete makes the verification code less likely to trip you up. The import requires access to the old address's inbox, so do it before the old account is shut down.

#If something is not working

Q. An administrator approval screen appears and I cannot go further

A. Your organisation's tenant requires administrator consent before permissions are granted to a new app. Ask your IT department for approval. An example request, and the steps for the administrator, are in Signing in with a Microsoft account.

Q. My notes have not come across

A. Check you got as far as entering the six-digit verification code. Where the code was not entered, or an expired one was entered, the import does not run. If the code does not arrive, check your spam folder and any quarantine folder on your mail service. If it is still not there, you can request a resend after 10 minutes.

Q. The import item is not in the settings screen

A. This feature can be disabled by the settings of the workspace you are moving from. Ask an administrator of that workspace to enable the two settings under Settings > Workspace > General > Data export permissions. The order they need to be set in, and how they depend on each other, are covered in Moving notes from another account.

Q. The email address is the same but it was treated as a new account

A. Check you are not signing in with a Microsoft 365 alias or an address on an old domain. Differences of upper and lower case are normally ignored, but an address on a different domain is treated as a different account. In that case, carry the notes over using the import.

Q. I forgot to cancel the old account's subscription

A. Sign in again with the old account and cancel from Settings > Billing. If you cannot get into the account, write to {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} from the email address concerned. How long you can carry on using it after cancelling is covered in About cancellation.

migrating-to-a-microsoft-account.text: This article is for people who use the Outlook calendar but have been signing in to {{PRODUCT}} with a Google account as a stopgap. Switching to signing in with a Microsoft account connects the calendar directly and makes pulling in events more reliable. Here are the steps for switching, and how to carry your past notes over to the new account. Signing in with a Microsoft account Where administrator approval is required → Moving notes from another account The import in detail, and its limits → Signing in and connecting your calendar Signing in generally → Note This article covers only the switch. The only calendars that can be connected are those on cloud Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online). Where you run an on-premises Exchange Server, switching will not let the calendar be retrieved, so check first. Signing in generally is covered in Signing in and connecting your calendar , and the case where administrator approval is required in Signing in with a Microsoft account . workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: The difference between personal and team workspaces; creating, joining, inviting, leaving and deleting; and who can see your notes.
workspaces.html:
In {{PRODUCT}}, a “workspace” is the container that holds your notes, spaces, folders and meeting records. You can have a workspace you use on your own, join your employer's workspace and use it as a team, or use both and keep work and personal records apart. This article covers everything from creating a workspace to deleting one, and what to settle before rolling it out across an organisation.

Plans and paymentBilling per workspace, and adding or removing seats→Spaces and foldersHow things are organised inside a workspace→Moving notes between workspacesThe steps, and their limits→Sharing notesHow to show an individual note to someone→
Note

Creating a workspace, changing settings, managing members, leaving and deleting are all done in the desktop app (macOS and Windows). The web version supports viewing and editing existing notes and has no settings screen.

#Personal versus team

{{PRODUCT}} has no distinction between “personal” and “business” account types. The only difference is whether a workspace has one member or several. The same account can belong both to a workspace of one and to a team workspace.

Charges arise per workspace. You can keep a personal workspace on the free plan while your employer's workspace is on the Team plan, or the other way round — your employer's workspace on the free plan and only your own workspace paid for. For how billing works, see Plans and payment.

#A workspace you use on your own

For keeping your records to yourself. You can do the following.

  • Notes are private by default. Until you share one, nobody else can see it.
  • Chat lets you ask questions across your own notes and transcripts.
  • Create folders inside a space, and set up templates and recipes to suit how you work.
  • You are the administrator, so every setting is yours to decide.

You can create a team workspace, or join an existing one, later on.

#A workspace you use as a team

For sharing with colleagues while deciding for yourself what they see.

  • Notes are private by default. Simply belonging to a team workspace does not make your notes visible to colleagues.
  • Shared notes and shared folders let you gather notes by recurring meeting, retrospective, client and so on.
  • Templates and recipes can be shared with colleagues so that the format of minutes and the shape of post-meeting follow-ups are consistent.
  • Chat lets you ask questions across the notes shared with you.

#Who can see your notes

This is the thing most worth checking when deciding how to set your workspaces up. Joining a workspace does not, on its own, make your notes visible to other members. There are three levels of sharing, and a new note starts out private.

Sharing level Who can view it
Private (default) Only the person who created it
Within the workspace Anyone authenticated with a workspace email address
Anyone with the link Anyone given the link — which can be passed outside your organisation

Beyond that, putting a note in a shared folder lets members with access to that folder view it, and you can invite people individually by email address. Changing the sharing level is covered in Sharing notes, and the settings that cap what an organisation permits are in Controlling sharing.

Notes and transcripts contain participants' names, what they said, and details of clients' staff. Decide whether to split workspaces against your internal rules on handling information. How to think about telling participants is covered in How far you can go with AI minutes (a guide for teams).

#Creating a workspace

You create a workspace, with a name and a picture, when you first set {{PRODUCT}} up. You can add more later.

  1. Click your workspace name at the bottom left of the desktop app.
  2. Choose Add workspace from the menu.
  3. Enter a workspace name.
  4. Set “let colleagues on the same email domain join automatically” as you wish.
Untick automatic joining when creating a personal workspace

Creating it with your work email address and automatic joining left on means colleagues on the same domain can join without approval. For a workspace you intend to use on your own, always untick it before creating it.

#Joining an existing workspace

Where your employer already has a workspace, you can join it from the list. For a private workspace, you send a request to join to an administrator. If nothing in the list fits, you can create a new one.

Joining a workspace is treated as agreeing to the terms of service.

Accepting an invitation or joining a new workspace switches you to that workspace. Your existing notes remain in the original workspace and are neither moved nor deleted. To see them, choose the original workspace from your workspace name at the bottom left.

#Switching workspace

Clicking your workspace name at the bottom left lists the workspaces you belong to. Choose the one you want.

#Inviting colleagues

When creating a workspace you can invite people by entering email addresses, or by choosing from a list of people you meet with often. That list is built from people on the same company email domain you have had meetings with using {{PRODUCT}}.

You can also distribute an invitation link. To add invitations after creating the workspace, or to change the automatic joining setting, open Settings > Workspace > Members.

On a paid plan, a seat is charged for each person who joins. Anyone joining partway through a term is pro-rated and reflected in the next invoice.

#What administrators can do that members cannot

From the member management screen, an administrator can do the following.

  • Review and manage members — see who belongs, whether their role is administrator or member, and remove them where necessary.
  • Change roles — promote a member to administrator, or return an administrator to member.
  • Copy the invitation link — share the link for people to join with. The per-domain automatic joining setting applies.
  • Invite new colleagues — enter an email address, or choose from the list of people you have had meetings with. On a paid plan this adds a seat, pro-rated into the next invoice.
Action Administrator Member
Changing workspace settings Yes No
Inviting, removing and changing the role of members Yes No
Viewing the billing screen Yes Yes
Upgrading the workspace Yes Yes
Cancelling an existing subscription, changing plan, changing payment method Yes No

Where an administrator has left or is on extended leave and cannot be reached, and a role needs changing, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

#Adding and removing members

When you add someone — they can start using the workspace. On a paid plan they count as a seat from the day they join. Adding them does not let them see other members' private notes. What they can see is notes in folders they have access to, and notes shared with them individually.

When you remove someone — an administrator finds them in the All members list on the member management screen in settings and chooses Remove from the menu beside their name.

Removal means losing access to notes, folders, templates and recipes

Someone who is removed can no longer open the notes, folders, templates and recipes that were in that workspace — including private notes they created themselves, and equally where they left of their own accord. Where you remove someone on the basis that they will carry on using {{PRODUCT}} in another workspace, allow time for them to move their notes first. Notes they had put in a shared folder stay in that folder and remain visible to other members.

Removal from a workspace affects access to that workspace only. Their {{PRODUCT}} account itself remains valid: they can still sign in, use other workspaces, and will still receive email from {{PRODUCT}}. To stop the email, use the unsubscribe link in the message, or delete the account itself following Deleting your account.

Where someone who has been removed needs to retrieve notes they left behind, ask a workspace administrator to add them back temporarily. Once they are a member again, running Move notes to another workspace lets them take the notes with them before leaving.

#Leaving a workspace

Note

Two conditions apply to leaving: you must belong to at least one other workspace, and you must not be the only administrator. Where you belong to only one workspace, create a new one first. Where you are the only administrator, promote another member to administrator before leaving. Leaving means losing access to notes, folders, templates and recipes, so if there is anything you want to keep, move it first with Move notes to another workspace.

  1. Settings > Workspace > General — open it.
  2. Scroll to the Danger zone section at the foot of the page.
  3. Leave workspace — click it.
  4. To confirm, type “leave [workspace name]” as instructed on screen.

#Workspace settings

From Settings > Workspace > General, an administrator can set the following.

  • Workspace name — rewrite the “Workspace name” field and click outside it to save.
  • Workspace logo — click the logo on the settings screen to change it.
  • Allow colleagues to join automatically — lets users on the same email domain join without requesting it.
  • Data export permissions — Data security — a separate page beneath it, where an administrator decides how far users may take data outside the workspace. There are three settings.
    • Allow data export — whether bulk export to CSV is allowed. The steps are in Exporting notes in bulk.
    • Allow notes to be moved to another workspace — the steps are in Moving notes between workspaces.
    • Allow notes to be moved to another account — cannot be changed unless the setting above it is enabled. The steps are in Moving notes from another account.
  • Make the workspace discoverable — controls whether this workspace appears in the list when a user on the same email domain is choosing one to join.
  • Internal terminology — register company names, product names, team names and other words used internally to improve transcription accuracy. An administrator edits them from the Language settings. How to register them is covered in Customising transcriptionMoving notes between workspaces

#Moving notes between workspaces

You can move notes between workspaces you belong to.

To move an individual note, hover over it and choose Move to workspace from the three-dot menu that appears, then pick the destination.

To move all your notes at once, use Settings > Workspace > General → Danger zone → Move notes to another workspace. Your notes, and folders you are the only member of, move. A preview of what will move and how is shown before it runs. The full steps and limits are in Moving notes between workspaces.

An administrator can disable the feature entirely. Even where it is enabled, whether your internal rules permit moving a note is the user's responsibility. Check your internal rules before moving notes containing client information into a personal workspace.

#Deleting a workspace

An administrator can delete a workspace that is no longer needed once a migration is finished. Deletion cannot be undone, and all the data in that workspace is lost.

Note

Only an administrator of the workspace who also belongs to at least one other workspace can delete it.

  1. 1

    Move the notes you want to keep

    Settings > Workspace > General > Danger zone > Move notes to another workspace — move the notes you want to keep to another workspace. After deletion, notes that were in that workspace cannot be restored.

  2. 2

    Remove every other member

    Every other member has to have left or been removed. Only a workspace where you are the last remaining member can be deleted.

  3. 3

    Cancel the paid plan

    Where a subscription is still in place, cancel it first from Settings > Billing. For the steps, see About cancellation.

  4. 4

    Delete the workspace

    Settings > Workspace > General > Danger zone — click Delete workspace and type the workspace name to confirm.

Check
  • You have moved or exported the notes you want to keep
  • You are the only member left
  • The paid plan is cancelled and no next renewal date is shown

#Where you alone want a paid plan

Upgrading is per workspace, not per company. Where you belong to a workspace on the free plan and want the Team plan features for yourself alone (unlimited note history, integrations with external services, the higher model in chat), do this.

  1. Create a new workspace — choose Add workspace from your workspace name at the bottom left and give it a name. Untick automatic joining.
  2. Move your notes — from your current workspace to the new one, either all at once with Move notes to another workspace or note by note with Move to workspace.
  3. Subscribe on the new workspace — switch to the new workspace and take out the Team plan from Settings > Billing > Manage subscription. You are the only member, so that is one seat.
  4. Tidy up the original workspace if need be — where you were an administrator of the original workspace, promote another member to administrator before leaving.

The original workspace stays on the free plan and only the new one is paid for.

#What to settle before rolling it out in a Japanese organisation

Changing how workspaces are arranged later means everybody moving their notes. Settling these three things at the outset saves rework.

#Whether to have a workspace per team

It comes down to whether you want to search across everything. Search and chat do not cross workspaces, so splitting means teams can no longer look back at each other's past meetings.

Approach Suits Watch out for
One for the whole company Lots of cross-team projects; wanting minutes to accumulate as a company-wide asset You have to decide how shared folders are designed and how sharing is managed at the outset
One per team HR, legal, corporate planning and others with a lot of material other teams cannot see Billing is split per workspace, and every transfer means moving notes
One for the company plus separate ones for sensitive teams You want to share most things but keep a few teams apart You have to set separate rules for the teams kept apart

In most cases, one company-wide workspace with visibility controlled through the design of shared folders is easier to manage. Notes are private by default, so belonging to the same workspace does not by itself expose anything. For designing folders and spaces see Spaces and folders, and for granting permissions by group see User groups.

#Members who leave or move team

What causes most trouble when someone leaves or moves team is what happens to private notes only they can see. We recommend agreeing a procedure internally in advance.

  1. Have them put notes to be handed over in a shared folder — before their last day, have them moved to a folder their successor can access. Left private, the content becomes unretrievable the moment the account is deleted.
  2. Export the notes you need — for anything that has to be kept as a record, export it to CSV following Exporting notes in bulk.
  3. Remove them from the workspace — after their last day, an administrator removes them from the member management screen. The seat count drops and is reflected in the next invoice.
  4. Decide what happens to the account — closing their company email account does not remove their {{PRODUCT}} account, which remains theirs. Settle how that is handled in your internal rules.

Administrator rights do not let you open other members' private notes. Unless “move notes to be handed over into a shared folder” is on your leaver checklist, there is no way to retrieve the contents after they have gone. Deleting the account itself is something the individual does; a company cannot do it on their behalf. How it works is covered in Deleting your account.

#Central management by an IT department

Where an organisation wants control, these are the points to cover.

  • Distribution and updates — distribution to devices and version updates can be done in bulk from MDM or a distribution tool. For the steps, see Bulk installation and updates by an administrator.
  • Controlling who joins — combining the automatic joining and discoverability settings makes it easier to gather users into the intended workspace. There is no setting that technically prevents an individual creating their own workspace, so pair it with a position in your internal rules.
  • Controlling what leaves — data export permissions let you stop export, moving to another account, and moving to another workspace independently. Set these where you want to prevent information being taken out when someone leaves.
  • Controlling sharing — whether sharing outside the organisation is allowed is set in Controlling sharing.
  • Transcript retention — there is a setting that deletes meeting transcripts automatically after a period. Set it to match your document retention rules in Automatic transcript deletion.
  • Controlling authentication — single sign-on (SSO) and multi-factor authentication are configured on the identity platform. See Signing in and connecting your calendar.

#If something is not working

Q. My notes are not in the workspace I joined

A. When you switch workspace, your earlier notes stay in the original one. Choose the original workspace from your workspace name at the bottom left. If they are still not there, check using Notes are missing.

Q. I cannot leave a workspace

A. You cannot leave where it is the only workspace you belong to; create a new one first. And where you are the only administrator, promote another member to administrator before leaving.

Q. The button for deleting the workspace is greyed out

A. It may be that other members remain, that a paid subscription is still running, or that you do not belong to another workspace. Check you meet all the conditions in “Deleting a workspace” in this article.

Q. I cannot find the option to move notes to another workspace

A. A workspace administrator may have prohibited moving under data export permissions. Ask them to check the setting at Settings > Workspace > General > Data export permissions.

Q. Colleagues have joined although I did not invite them

A. With “allow colleagues to join automatically” enabled, users on the same email domain can join without requesting it. Check the setting at Settings > Workspace > General and disable it if need be. On a paid plan a seat is charged for each person who joins, so it affects the amount billed too.

#Related articles
