Workspace logo — click the logo on the settings screen to change it. Allow colleagues to join automatically — lets users on the same email domain join without requesting it. Data export permissions — Data security — a separate page beneath it, where an administrator decides how far users may take data outside the workspace. There are three settings. Allow data export — whether bulk export to CSV is allowed. The steps are in Exporting notes in bulk . Allow notes to be moved to another workspace — the steps are in Moving notes between workspaces . Allow notes to be moved to another account — cannot be changed unless the setting above it is enabled. The steps are in Moving notes from another account . Make the workspace discoverable — controls whether this workspace appears in the list when a user on the same email domain is choosing one to join. Internal terminology — register company names, product names, team names and other words used internally to improve transcription accuracy. An administrator edits them from the Language settings. How to register them is covered in Customising transcription Moving notes between workspaces # Moving notes between workspaces You can move notes between workspaces you belong to. To move an individual note, hover over it and choose Move to workspace from the three-dot menu that appears, then pick the destination. To move all your notes at once, use Settings > Workspace > General → Danger zone → Move notes to another workspace . Your notes, and folders you are the only member of, move. A preview of what will move and how is shown before it runs. The full steps and limits are in Moving notes between workspaces . An administrator can disable the feature entirely. Even where it is enabled, whether your internal rules permit moving a note is the user's responsibility. Check your internal rules before moving notes containing client information into a personal workspace. # Deleting a workspace An administrator can delete a workspace that is no longer needed once a migration is finished. Deletion cannot be undone, and all the data in that workspace is lost. Note Only an administrator of the workspace who also belongs to at least one other workspace can delete it. 1 Move the notes you want to keep Settings > Workspace > General > Danger zone > Move notes to another workspace — move the notes you want to keep to another workspace. After deletion, notes that were in that workspace cannot be restored. 2 Remove every other member Every other member has to have left or been removed. Only a workspace where you are the last remaining member can be deleted. 3 Cancel the paid plan Where a subscription is still in place, cancel it first from Settings > Billing . For the steps, see About cancellation . 4 Delete the workspace Settings > Workspace > General > Danger zone — click Delete workspace and type the workspace name to confirm. Check You have moved or exported the notes you want to keep You are the only member left The paid plan is cancelled and no next renewal date is shown # Where you alone want a paid plan Upgrading is per workspace, not per company. Where you belong to a workspace on the free plan and want the Team plan features for yourself alone (unlimited note history, integrations with external services, the higher model in chat), do this. Create a new workspace — choose Add workspace from your workspace name at the bottom left and give it a name. Untick automatic joining. Move your notes — from your current workspace to the new one, either all at once with Move notes to another workspace or note by note with Move to workspace . Subscribe on the new workspace — switch to the new workspace and take out the Team plan from Settings > Billing > Manage subscription . You are the only member, so that is one seat. Tidy up the original workspace if need be — where you were an administrator of the original workspace, promote another member to administrator before leaving. The original workspace stays on the free plan and only the new one is paid for. # What to settle before rolling it out in a Japanese organisation Changing how workspaces are arranged later means everybody moving their notes. Settling these three things at the outset saves rework. # Whether to have a workspace per team It comes down to whether you want to search across everything. Search and chat do not cross workspaces, so splitting means teams can no longer look back at each other's past meetings. Approach Suits Watch out for One for the whole company Lots of cross-team projects; wanting minutes to accumulate as a company-wide asset You have to decide how shared folders are designed and how sharing is managed at the outset One per team HR, legal, corporate planning and others with a lot of material other teams cannot see Billing is split per workspace, and every transfer means moving notes One for the company plus separate ones for sensitive teams You want to share most things but keep a few teams apart You have to set separate rules for the teams kept apart In most cases, one company-wide workspace with visibility controlled through the design of shared folders is easier to manage. Notes are private by default, so belonging to the same workspace does not by itself expose anything. For designing folders and spaces see Spaces and folders , and for granting permissions by group see User groups . # Members who leave or move team What causes most trouble when someone leaves or moves team is what happens to private notes only they can see. We recommend agreeing a procedure internally in advance. Have them put notes to be handed over in a shared folder — before their last day, have them moved to a folder their successor can access. Left private, the content becomes unretrievable the moment the account is deleted. Export the notes you need — for anything that has to be kept as a record, export it to CSV following Exporting notes in bulk . Remove them from the workspace — after their last day, an administrator removes them from the member management screen. The seat count drops and is reflected in the next invoice. Decide what happens to the account — closing their company email account does not remove their {{PRODUCT}} account, which remains theirs. Settle how that is handled in your internal rules. Administrator rights do not let you open other members' private notes. Unless “move notes to be handed over into a shared folder” is on your leaver checklist, there is no way to retrieve the contents after they have gone. Deleting the account itself is something the individual does; a company cannot do it on their behalf. How it works is covered in Deleting your account . # Central management by an IT department Where an organisation wants control, these are the points to cover. Distribution and updates — distribution to devices and version updates can be done in bulk from MDM or a distribution tool. For the steps, see Bulk installation and updates by an administrator . Controlling who joins — combining the automatic joining and discoverability settings makes it easier to gather users into the intended workspace. There is no setting that technically prevents an individual creating their own workspace, so pair it with a position in your internal rules. Controlling what leaves — data export permissions let you stop export, moving to another account, and moving to another workspace independently. Set these where you want to prevent information being taken out when someone leaves. Controlling sharing — whether sharing outside the organisation is allowed is set in Controlling sharing . Transcript retention — there is a setting that deletes meeting transcripts automatically after a period. Set it to match your document retention rules in Automatic transcript deletion . Controlling authentication — single sign-on (SSO) and multi-factor authentication are configured on the identity platform. See Signing in and connecting your calendar . # If something is not working Q. My notes are not in the workspace I joined A. When you switch workspace, your earlier notes stay in the original one. Choose the original workspace from your workspace name at the bottom left. If they are still not there, check using Notes are missing . Q. I cannot leave a workspace A. You cannot leave where it is the only workspace you belong to; create a new one first. And where you are the only administrator, promote another member to administrator before leaving. Q. The button for deleting the workspace is greyed out A. It may be that other members remain, that a paid subscription is still running, or that you do not belong to another workspace. Check you meet all the conditions in “Deleting a workspace” in this article. Q. I cannot find the option to move notes to another workspace A. A workspace administrator may have prohibited moving under data export permissions. Ask them to check the setting at Settings > Workspace > General > Data export permissions . Q. Colleagues have joined although I did not invite them A. With “allow colleagues to join automatically” enabled, users on the same email domain can join without requesting it. Check the setting at Settings > Workspace > General and disable it if need be. On a paid plan a seat is charged for each person who joins, so it affects the amount billed too. # Related articles Moving notes between workspaces The steps for moving them all at once → Moving notes from another account Carrying notes over from a different email address → Spaces and folders Designing what is shared → Plans and payment How seats relate to billing → Controlling sharing Whether sharing outside the organisation is allowed → User groups Granting permissions by group →

people-and-companies.title: People and companies
people-and-companies.description: How information about meeting participants is gathered, and where it appears.
people-and-companies.html:
Every time {{PRODUCT}} creates a meeting note, it builds a list of the people and companies involved. Being able to call up all your past notes from someone's name saves hunting for “when was it we discussed that?”. This article explains where the information comes from, where it appears, and what it cannot do.

Asking questions about a note (chat)Asking about one person in particular→Pre-meeting briefUsing participant information to prepare→Connecting your calendarWhere participant information comes from→
Note

The lists of people and companies are built from meeting notes created from calendar events. Where no calendar is connected, or a note was created by hand, no information is gathered into the lists. Viewing and searching are done in the desktop app (macOS and Windows).

#Where to open it

Open them from the icons in the sidebar at the bottom left. The person icon is the list of people; the building icon is the list of companies.

Choosing a person or a company from a list shows all the notes from meetings they attended. Use it to check how an exchange has gone, or to remind yourself of last time before a meeting you have not had in a while.

#How the information is gathered

Information about people and companies is extracted from calendar events automatically.

  1. When you start {{PRODUCT}} from a calendar event and create a note, the list of participants on that event is pulled in.
  2. From the email addresses pulled in, further information — profile picture, job title, employer — is filled in. This happens automatically in the background.
  3. As you have more meetings with the same person, more notes accumulate against them.

Company information is organised in the same way, from the domains of participants' email addresses.

Using chat with a particular person selected in the list lets you ask questions about meetings with just that person. You can ask things like “gather the requests that came up in meetings with this company”. You can also search directly by name or company name in the search box.

#What is shown

The lists show only participants in meetings for which a note was created in {{PRODUCT}}. They are not synchronised with a company address book or a business card system, so people you have not met, and participants in meetings where {{PRODUCT}} was not used, do not appear.

Internal colleagues and external contacts appear side by side. Clients' names and employers are included, so take care what is on screen when sharing your screen.

#What it cannot do

At present you cannot add people or companies by hand. The lists are built automatically from actual meetings and calendar events.

Where someone does not appear in the list, it is usually one of the following.

  • They were not listed as a participant on the calendar event.
  • The meeting was recorded from a note created by hand rather than from a calendar event.
  • They responded “no” to the calendar invitation.

Occasionally a name is spelt slightly differently from reality, or the company name or logo is another company's. This happens most easily with people who share a name, companies that use several domains, and just after a company changes its name. If you notice it, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} and we will check and correct it.

Do not copy what is shown straight into external documents

Job titles and company names are filled in automatically, so they can differ from reality. Check against primary sources such as a business card or an email signature before copying them into a quotation, a contract or a proposal.

#Things to watch in a Japanese organisation

Meeting participants' names, employers, job titles and email addresses are personal data under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information. Being able to view and search them within {{PRODUCT}} is ordinary use, but we recommend settling the following internally.

  • Taking it outside the company — where you export the lists and load them into another system, check that handling clients' contact details that way is within your internal rules. The export steps are in Exporting notes in bulk.
  • What happens when someone leaves — the lists are tied to the notes a person created. Deleting a leaver's account loses the notes tied to it as well. Agree a routine of moving anything that needs to be handed over into a shared folder beforehand. See Workspaces for details.
  • Administrator controls — there are settings restricting export and sharing at workspace level. See Controlling sharing.

#If something is not working

Q. Only internal colleagues appear in the list of people

A. External participants may not be listed on the calendar event. Where the practice is to book only the meeting room and invite the other side by a separate email, participant information is not pulled in. Add the other side's email addresses to the event before recording the meeting.

Q. The company name or logo is wrong

A. Companies are inferred from email domains, so mix-ups happen with companies that use several domains and groups with many subsidiaries. Contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} and we will look into it.

Q. I want to remove a particular person from the list

A. There is currently no way to remove an individual person or company from the list. The lists are built from notes, so deleting the notes concerned is reflected in the lists. For deleting notes, see Deleting and restoring notes.

#Related articles

Pre-meeting briefBuilding preparation material from past notes→Asking questions about a note (chat)Questions narrowed to a person or company→Exporting notes in bulkExporting your records→Privacy policyHow personal data is handled→

transfer-notes-between-accounts.title: Moving notes from another account
transfer-notes-between-accounts.description: How to import notes from an old account into a new one, and the limits of doing so.
transfer-notes-between-accounts.html:
When you change email address, or want to bring a personal account and a work account together, you can import the notes from the old account into the one you use now. This article explains the steps, what is not imported, and what to check when it does not work.

Moving notes between workspacesMoving within the same account→Switching to a Microsoft accountMoving from Google to Microsoft→Account and email address changesChanging the address you sign in with→

#What this does

Importing notes moves all the meeting notes and transcripts from one {{PRODUCT}} account to another. Where notes older than 31 days have stopped being shown on the free plan, those hidden notes move too. There is no need to upgrade the old account in order to import.

Use it in situations like these.

  • You have switched to a new email address.
  • You are moving from a personal account to a work account (or the other way round).
  • You are bringing two accounts together.
An import is a move

Once the import finishes, not a single note remains in the old account. You cannot use it to view the same notes from both accounts. Check before you run it.

#When it cannot be used

Situation What to use
The same email address, with several workspaces in use Moving notes between workspaces
You want to import from another service (Notion, Apple Notes, Google Docs and the like) Not supported by this feature
The source and destination have the same email address No import needed. The account is the same, so the notes stay as they are

Because the verification code is sent to the old account's email address, the two accounts must have different email addresses.

#Before you start

Note
  • You must be signed in to the account you are importing into.
  • You must be able to get into the inbox of the old account's email address. The verification code arrives there.
  • This is done in the desktop app (macOS and Windows). The web version has no settings screen.
  • Imported notes go into whichever workspace is open when you start. Switch to the workspace you want before beginning.

#The import steps

  1. 1

    Open the destination workspace

    Sign in to the destination account and switch to the workspace you want the notes in.

  2. 2

    Open Profile in settings

    Click your workspace name at the bottom left to open Settings, then choose Profile in the settings menu.

  3. 3

    Start the import

    Account management section and click Import notes from another account → Import.

  4. 4

    Enter the old email address

    Enter the old account's email address and submit it.

  5. 5

    Enter the verification code

    A verification code arrives in the old address's inbox. It expires 10 minutes after it is sent. Entering it confirms you own the old account.

Once confirmed, the import starts automatically. When it finishes, no notes remain in the old account.

You can request a new code 10 minutes after the last one was sent. Entering the wrong code repeatedly locks retries for up to about an hour.

Check
  • The old account's notes are in the destination workspace
  • Signing in to the old account shows no notes at all
  • If you use paid features, you have taken out a subscription on the destination workspace

#What does not come with it

The subscription — a paid subscription stays with the old account. After importing, open Settings > Billing on the destination workspace in the new account and take out a new subscription. Without one, paid features including transcription are unavailable. Once the old account's subscription is no longer needed, cancel it there. How long you can use it after cancelling is covered in About cancellation.

Shared folders — a folder you are the only member of (with nobody else joined or invited) is imported into the destination workspace along with the notes inside it. A folder shared with others is not imported. The notes inside it do move, but they arrive detached from the folder, so you will need to reorganise them on the new account. Folders move on the same basis as in Moving notes between workspaces.

Templates and recipes — these do not carry over. Recreate them on the new account. How to create them is in Shaping notes with templates and Recipes (standing instructions).

#Before running it in a Japanese organisation

Notes created for work contain clients' names, what was said, and how internal thinking developed. Importing from a work account into a personal account can in substance amount to taking business information out of the company.

  • Check what your internal information-management rules say about taking business data out.
  • Where you are moving notes because you are leaving or changing teams, get approval from your manager or IT department before running it.
  • Administrators who want to prevent this can disable it in the workspace settings. See the next section.
Check your internal rules before running it

Moving notes cannot be undone. If it turns out afterwards that the information should not have been taken out, there is no feature for returning it to the original account. If you are unsure, check with the relevant team internally before running it.

#Administrator controls

Whether this feature is available is determined by the settings of the workspace you are importing from. On the Team and Enterprise plans it may be disabled by default.

In the source workspace, go to Settings > Workspace > General > Data export permissions and set these in order.

  1. Allow notes to be moved to another workspace — enable this. It is the prerequisite. How to open it and where it is on screen are covered in Moving notes between workspaces.
  2. Allow notes to be moved to another account — enable this. It cannot be changed until 1 is enabled.

If you are an administrator of that workspace you can enable them yourself. If someone else administers it, ask them. The full list of settings is in Workspaces.

#If something is not working

Q. The import item is not in the settings screen

A. Data export permissions may be disabled on the source workspace. Ask an administrator of that workspace to enable the two settings under Settings > Workspace > General > Data export permissions. The second cannot be changed until “Allow notes to be moved to another workspace” is enabled. Note too that this feature is desktop-app only.

Q. The verification email does not arrive

A. Check the “Promotions” and “Social” tabs of your mail service and your spam folder. On a work address, an internal mail gateway may have quarantined it, so checking the quarantine folder is worthwhile too. You can request a resend 10 minutes after the last one was sent.

Q. I have not created the destination account yet

A. The import starts from being signed in to the destination account. Where you have not yet created an account on the new email address, sign out, sign in with the new address and create the account, then start the import. Adding and switching workspaces is a different operation; this feature works only between accounts on different email addresses.

Q. I cannot get into the old email address

A. Being able to get into the old address's inbox is essential for confirming you own it. For security there is no alternative means of confirmation. Where a work email address is due to be shut off because you are leaving, complete the import before that happens.

Q. The imported notes are not in the workspace I wanted

A. The import runs against whichever workspace was open when you started. To move them to another workspace, you can move them all at once using Moving notes between workspaces.

Q. Paid features stopped working after the import

A. The subscription is still on the old account. Take out a new one from Settings > Billing on the destination workspace in the new account. Cancel the old account's subscription if you no longer need it.

#Related articles

Moving notes between workspacesMoving within the same account→WorkspacesJoining, leaving, deletion and permissions→Exporting notes in bulkExporting to CSV→Deleting your accountRemoving the old account after migrating→

Paid features stopped working after the import A. The subscription is still on the old account. Take out a new one from Settings > Billing on the destination workspace in the new account. Cancel the old account's subscription if you no longer need it. # Related articles Moving notes between workspaces Moving within the same account → Workspaces Joining, leaving, deletion and permissions → Exporting notes in bulk Exporting to CSV → Deleting your account Removing the old account after migrating →

transfer-notes-between-workspaces.title: Moving notes between workspaces
transfer-notes-between-workspaces.description: How to move notes to another workspace, the permissions needed, and what to watch out for.
transfer-notes-between-workspaces.html:
You can move your notes in bulk between the workspaces you belong to. Use it when you change team, when consolidating several workspaces into one, or when moving to a personal workspace. This article covers moving them in bulk, what does not come with them, and the administrator settings.

WorkspacesCreating, joining, leaving and deleting, in overview→Moving notes from another accountCarrying notes over from an account on a different email address→Plans and paymentWhat happens to the subscription after a move→
Note

You can only move between workspaces you belong to. This is done in the desktop app (macOS and Windows); the web version has no settings screen. Where an administrator has prohibited moving, the options in this article do not appear on screen.

#Two ways to move notes

What you want to do What to use What happens to folders
Move all your notes at once Settings > Workspace > General > Danger zone > Move notes to another workspace Folders you are the only member of move too
Move particular notes only From the note's three-dot menu, Move to workspace Folders do not move

To carry notes over from an account on a different email address, use Moving notes from another account rather than this feature.

#Moving them all at once

  1. 1

    Open the workspace settings

    Click your workspace name at the bottom left and choose Settings from the menu. Open General from the menu on the left.

  2. 2

    Open the danger zone

    Scroll to the Danger zone section at the foot of the page and find Move notes to another workspace.

  3. 3

    Choose the destination

    Move notes — click the button and choose the destination workspace from the list.

  4. 4

    Review the preview and run it

    It shows how many notes will move, which folders will move with them, and which shared folders notes will be detached from. To pick a different workspace click Back; to go ahead click Move notes.

Once the move finishes, it shows how many notes and folders arrived in the destination workspace, with a button to switch to it.

Check
  • Switching to the destination workspace shows the moved notes in the list
  • Notes you meant to leave behind have not moved unintentionally
  • You have reorganised notes detached from shared folders in the destination

#Moving individual notes

  1. In the note list, hover over the note you want to move.
  2. Click the three-dot menu that appears.
  3. Move to workspace — choose it.
  4. Choose the destination workspace.

This way, folders do not move. Reorganise the notes in the destination workspace.

#What does not come with them

The subscription — a paid subscription stays with the original workspace. To carry on using paid features in the destination, switch back to the original workspace and cancel from Settings > Billing, then switch to the destination workspace and take out a new subscription. How long you can use it after cancelling is covered in About cancellation.

Shared folders — a folder you are the only member of moves with the notes and arrives as a private folder in the destination. Where you were the only member of the original workspace, the workspace's folders and chat history move too. A folder shared with others stays behind, and your notes inside it are detached from it; reorganise them in the destination. Moving individual notes with Move to workspace never moves folders at all.

Templates — these are not included in the move. To use the same templates in the destination, open Manage templates from your workspace name at the bottom left and recreate them.

Notes are detached from shared folders

Where your notes were in a folder shared with others, running the move detaches them from that folder. Notes your team was referring to disappear from view, so check what is affected on the preview screen before running it, and tell your team beforehand if need be.

#Permissions needed

A workspace administrator can prohibit moving notes for security reasons. Where it is prohibited, neither the Move notes button nor the per-note Move to workspace item appears. Where you need to move notes, ask an administrator.

#How an administrator enables it

  1. Settings — open it and choose General.
  2. Data security — open Data export permissions beneath it.
  3. Allow notes to be moved to another workspace — enable it.
About how organisations use this

Enabling this setting lets users move their notes from a work workspace to a personal one. Organisations wanting to restrict information being taken out when someone leaves or changes team can leave it disabled and enable it temporarily, on request, when a move is needed. Whether a move is technically possible is decided by the setting; whether the information may be moved is a matter for your internal rules.

#Decide these before moving

In a Japanese organisation, settling the following beforehand saves rework.

  • How much to move — moving in bulk moves every one of your notes. You cannot leave some behind, so where you want to keep some, put them in a shared folder first or use the per-note move.
  • The effect on your team — where notes will be detached from shared folders, members who were referring to them lose access. Check the counts in the preview and share a copy before moving if need be.
  • Keeping records — for minutes your internal rules require to be retained for a period, the reliable approach is to export them to CSV with Exporting notes in bulk, separately from the move, and keep them in your document management system.
  • Timing around a transfer — where a change of team means a change of workspace, complete the move before you are removed from the old workspace. Once removed, you can no longer reach the notes.

#If something is not working

Q. I cannot find the option to move notes

A. Settings > Workspace > General — open it (your workspace name at the bottom left > Settings > General, under the Workspace heading) and look at the Danger zone section at the foot of the page. The item appears only where you have notes in that workspace and an administrator permits moving. If it is not there, ask an administrator to check the setting.

Q. I cannot choose a destination workspace (the list is empty)

A. You can only move to workspaces you belong to. Create one with Add workspace from your workspace name at the bottom left, or join an existing one, then run the move again.

Q. I moved them but the notes are not there

A. Check you have switched to the destination workspace; you can switch from your workspace name at the bottom left. If they are still not there, try the steps in Notes are missing.

Q. I want to undo a move

A. There is no feature to reverse a move automatically. You can move them back from the destination workspace to the original one with the same steps, but the links to shared folders are not restored; re-filing them into folders is manual.

Q. Paid features stopped working after the move

A. The subscription is still on the original workspace. Take out a subscription on the destination workspace from Settings > Billing. Where the original workspace's subscription is no longer needed, cancel it there.

#Related articles

WorkspacesJoining, leaving, deletion and permissions in overview→Moving notes from another accountCarrying notes over from another account→Spaces and foldersReorganising after a move→Exporting notes in bulkExporting for the record→

how-to-uninstall-and-reinstall.title: Uninstalling and reinstalling
how-to-uninstall-and-reinstall.description: How to uninstall on macOS and Windows, and how to reinstall without carrying settings over.
how-to-uninstall-and-reinstall.html:
{{PRODUCT}} normally updates itself to the latest version. Automatic updates can fail to work, for instance on a company-issued device with restricted permissions. This article covers uninstalling by hand and reinstalling the latest version, for macOS and for Windows.

Bulk installation and updates by an administratorDistribution and update control via MDM→Initial setup guideGranting permissions after reinstalling→Network and allowlistsChecking connectivity when updates do not arrive→
Note

The {{PRODUCT}} app is available for macOS and Windows. The web version runs in a browser and has nothing to install or remove.

#Before you reinstall

Notes and transcripts are tied to your account and stored on the server. Deleting the app does not delete them. Reinstalling and signing in with the same account shows your existing notes exactly as before.

What is deleted is the settings and temporary data on the device. After reinstalling you will need to sign in and grant permissions again.

Do not uninstall while notes are unsent

Notes that have not finished syncing can remain on the device, for instance just after recording a meeting offline. Before uninstalling, start the app, wait a while with an internet connection, and check the notes appear in the list.

#When reinstalling helps

  • Automatic updates are not working and it is stuck on an old version.
  • It does not start, or crashes immediately after starting.
  • The sign-in state is odd and signing out does not fix it.
  • You want to grant microphone or screen recording permission again, but toggling it in settings has no effect.

Where notes are not being generated or transcription is not being captured, try the checks in Notes are not being generated and Transcription is not working before reinstalling. Most of those are settings or permission problems that reinstalling does not solve.

#Uninstalling

  1. Finder — open it and show the Applications folder.
  2. Right-click the {{PRODUCT}} icon and choose Move to Bin.
  3. Finder — search for the product name and set the scope to This Mac. Check whether a copy remains anywhere outside the Applications folder, and move anything you find to the Bin too.
  4. Bin — open it, select the files concerned and choose Delete Immediately.
  5. Where the icon remains in the Dock, right-click it and choose Remove from Dock.
  1. Open the Start menu, type “Apps & features” or “Add or remove programs”, and open the settings screen.
  2. Find {{PRODUCT}} in the list and choose Uninstall.
  3. The uninstaller runs automatically. Follow the on-screen instructions to finish.

#Removing settings as well

To reinstall from scratch without carrying settings over, delete the settings files left on the device as well as the app itself. Do this before reinstalling.

Deleting settings cannot be undone

This removes settings stored on the device, such as template order, display settings and shortcuts. Settings stored on the server come back when you sign in again. If you cannot tell which is which, delete just the app first and reinstall, and only try deleting settings if the symptom persists.

  1. Finder — from its menu choose Go > Go to Folder.
  2. ~/Library/Application Support/ — open it and move the folder named after {{PRODUCT}} to the Bin.
  3. Do the same for ~/Library/Caches/ and ~/Library/Preferences/, deleting folders and files named after {{PRODUCT}}.
  4. Empty the Bin.
  1. Type %APPDATA% into the File Explorer address bar, open it and delete the folder named after {{PRODUCT}}.
  2. Do the same for %LOCALAPPDATA%, deleting the folder named after {{PRODUCT}}.

#Reinstalling

  1. Download the latest version from {{COMPANY}}'s website.
  2. Open the downloaded file and drag the {{PRODUCT}} icon into the Applications folder.
  3. Applications — open the folder and start it from there.
  1. Download the latest version from {{COMPANY}}'s website.
  2. Double-click the downloaded file and the installer runs automatically.
  3. Once it finishes, start it from the Start menu.

On first launch you are asked for microphone and screen recording permission. On macOS the app has to be restarted after screen recording permission is granted. For the permission steps in detail, see Initial setup guide.

Check
  • You have signed in with the same account and your existing notes appear in the list
  • Microphone and screen recording permission are granted
  • The version shown in settings is the latest

#On a company-issued device

On a device managed by an IT department, installing and uninstalling apps may be restricted. Where any of the following applies, talk to that team rather than doing it yourself.

  • Uninstalling asks for an administrator password.
  • Running the installer is blocked.
  • It is automatically reinstalled some time after you delete it.

In environments rolled out through MDM or a distribution tool, version updates are normally managed on the distribution side too. Rather than reinstalling locally, ask for the latest version to be distributed. See Bulk installation and updates by an administrator for details.

Updates usually stop because of permissions or the network

Where automatic updates do not work, it is usually either that write permissions on the device are restricted or that traffic to where update files are fetched from is blocked. If updates stop again after reinstalling, check connectivity using Network and allowlists and ask your IT department to allow the destinations needed.

#If something is not working

Q. My notes do not appear after reinstalling

A. Check you are signed in with the same account as before. If you use more than one account, you can switch from the icon beside the email address at the bottom left. The workspace may also have switched. See Notes are missing for details.

Q. The app is still there although I uninstalled it

A. A copy can remain somewhere outside the Applications folder. On macOS, set Finder's search to “This Mac”, find them and delete them all. On Windows, a non-default location may have been chosen at install time.

Q. The microphone is not captured after reinstalling

A. On macOS, an old version of the app can be left in the permission lists. In System Settings, under Privacy & Security, remove the {{PRODUCT}} entry from the Microphone and Screen Recording lists, then start the app and grant permission again. The detail is in Transcription is not working.

Q. Does uninstalling delete my notes?

A. No. Notes and transcripts are stored against your account, so reinstalling and signing in with the same account shows them exactly as before. To delete the data along with the account, use the steps in Deleting your account.

#Related articles

Initial setup guideGranting permissions and connecting your calendar→Bulk installation and updates by an administratorManaging distribution and updates→Transcription is not workingWhat to do when no audio is captured→Deleting your accountWhere you want to delete the data as well→

deleting-your-account.title: Deleting your account
deleting-your-account.description: How to delete, what data is deleted, and how long anything is kept afterwards.
deleting-your-account.html:
You can delete your {{PRODUCT}} account yourself from the app. Deleting it loses the account and the notes and transcripts attached to it, and it cannot be undone. This article explains the steps, what is deleted and what remains, and how data is handled afterwards.

Exporting notes in bulkExporting your records before deleting→Moving notes from another accountKeeping your notes by moving them to another account→Privacy policyHow personal data is handled, and requests for disclosure and the like→
Deletion cannot be undone

Deleting an account permanently loses the notes, transcripts and folders it held. There is no way to restore them. If there is anything you want to keep, export it or move it to another account first.

#Before you delete

  1. Export the notes you want to keep — Settings > Profile — you can export to CSV from there. For the steps, see Exporting notes in bulk. The exported file arrives by email.
  2. Move them first if moving to another account — to carry notes over to an account on a new email address, follow Moving notes from another account before deleting. They cannot be moved afterwards.
  3. Cancel your paid plan — where a subscription is still in place, cancel it first from Settings > Billing. The cancellation steps, and how long you can use it afterwards, are covered in About cancellation.
  4. Leave your team's workspaces — for what happens to notes you put in shared folders, see “What happens to notes and folders” below.
  5. Check internally if you used it for work — where your internal rules require meeting records to be kept for a period, deleting the account can leave that obligation unmet. Export the records you need before deleting and store them in your document management system.
Check
  • The CSV of the notes you want to keep has arrived by email and you have opened and checked it
  • Notes being carried over to another account have finished moving
  • The paid plan is cancelled and no next renewal date is shown
  • You have told the administrators of the workspaces you belonged to which notes need handing over

#The steps

Note

Deletion is done from the settings screen of the desktop app (macOS and Windows). The web version supports viewing and editing existing notes and has no settings screen.

  1. 1

    Open settings

    Start {{PRODUCT}} and open Settings from your workspace name at the bottom left.

  2. 2

    Open Profile

    Click Preferences → Profile in the sidebar, scroll down and find the Delete account button.

  3. 3

    Confirm the deletion

    Delete account — click it and follow the on-screen instructions to confirm.

Where you cannot get the app into a usable state, or cannot sign in to the account, write to {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} from the email address of the account you want deleted. We will act once we have confirmed your identity.

#What happens to notes and folders

What What happens on deletion
Private notes you own Permanently deleted
Private folders you created Permanently deleted
The “container” of a folder with other members in it May remain, so that the other members can carry on using it
Notes you own that were inside such a folder Permanently deleted
Notes you already moved to another account Not deleted. They remain as that account's notes

For a shared folder, only the folder itself remains; the contents of the notes you owned are gone. Where the minutes your team was referring to need to be kept, hand them over to another member or export and share them before deleting.

Notes in shared folders are deleted too

Deleting on the assumption that “it is in a shared folder, so others can see it” deletes the notes you created. For notes the team needs to keep, export and share the contents before deleting, or have someone else recreate them as notes they own.

#What happens to the calendar connection

Deleting your account also revokes {{PRODUCT}}'s access to the calendar you connected (Google Calendar or the Outlook calendar).

To confirm it has been revoked, or to revoke it by hand, you can do so from each provider's settings.

  • Google — remove {{PRODUCT}} from the list of third-party app connections in your Google account's security settings.
  • Microsoft — remove {{PRODUCT}} from the list of app permissions on your Microsoft account.

Where an administrator has given tenant-wide consent on your employer's Microsoft 365 tenant, it has to be revoked by the administrator rather than from your personal settings. See Signing in with a Microsoft account.

#How data is handled after deletion

Once you confirm deletion, the account and its notes become inaccessible immediately. Data on live systems is erased promptly.

Backups taken for disaster recovery temporarily continue to contain the data as it stood at the moment of deletion. Backups are kept in generations, and that data disappears as newer generations replace them. We do not extract and restore data from backups, and while it remains in a backup it is not available for ordinary use or search.

#Records we are required by law to keep

Even after an account is deleted, records we are required by law to keep are retained for the prescribed period. Where you were on a paid plan, that covers transaction records (contract date, amounts invoiced, payment records, copies of qualified invoices and the like). These follow from accounting and tax legislation and cannot be erased on request.

These records are kept separately from meeting content and transcripts, and are used only for billing and tax purposes.

#In relation to requests under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information

Deleting your account from the app is deletion as a feature {{PRODUCT}} provides. Separately from that, you may also make a request under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information.

The difference between deleting an account and requesting cessation of use

The app's Delete account is a feature that lets you erase your account and notes yourself. There is no fee and no paperwork.

A request to cease use of or erase data under the Act on the Protection of Personal Information, by contrast, is a request made as a legal right. It is made to the contact point set out in the privacy policy, with documents confirming your identity. It can also cover things account deletion does not erase, such as information contained in support correspondence.

In most cases deleting from the app achieves what you want. Use the latter procedure where you want to check what data remains after deletion, or to make a request as a legal right.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 35 (cessation of use etc.)

An individual may request that their personal data cease to be used or be erased. Under paragraph 5 of that article, a request may also be made where the data is no longer needed, where a leak or similar has occurred, or where there is otherwise a risk of harm to the individual's rights or legitimate interests. Data belonging to someone who has left {{PRODUCT}} falls within “no longer needed”, so {{COMPANY}} proceeds with erasure without waiting for a request.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 22 (keeping data accurate etc.)

Where personal data is no longer needed, a business must endeavour to erase it without delay. {{COMPANY}} treats erasure of data after account deletion, and the automatic transcript deletion setting, as practice in line with that provision.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 33 (disclosure)

An individual may request disclosure of retained personal data. Under paragraph 1 of that article, disclosure may also be received by specifying provision by electromagnetic record. In {{PRODUCT}}, the Exporting notes in bulk feature lets you obtain your own notes and transcripts in CSV form. For disclosure of anything else, apply to the contact point set out in the privacy policy.

There is no fee for requests to cease use, erase or correct. For requests for disclosure and for notification of the purpose of use, we may charge a fee reflecting the actual costs involved.

#If you want to use it again afterwards

Signing in again with the same email address lets you start using it as a new account. The earlier data cannot be restored, but nothing restricts you from using the service itself.

A paid plan would be a new subscription. Neither the earlier contract period nor any benefits carry over.

#If something is not working

Q. I cannot find the button for deleting my account

A. Settings > Profile — open it and scroll to the bottom of the screen. It is the Profile screen under Preferences, not the workspace settings screen. Deleting a workspace itself is elsewhere; see Workspaces.

Q. I want to delete an account I cannot sign in to

A. Write to {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}} from the email address of the account you want deleted. We will act once we have confirmed your identity. Where that email address itself no longer works, say so and we will explain how else we can verify who you are.

Q. As a company, we want to delete a leaver's account

A. A {{PRODUCT}} account belongs to the individual, and a company cannot delete it on their behalf. What a company can do is remove that member from the workspace. For the steps, see Workspaces. For handing over notes created for work, we recommend a routine of having them moved into a shared folder before the person leaves.

Q. I deleted it by mistake

A. There is no way to restore it. Where you ran a CSV export before deleting, the contents are in the file that arrived by email. Check your inbox.

Q. I deleted my account but still receive email from {{PRODUCT}}

A. There can be a lag in processing unsubscribes. Use the unsubscribe link in the email. If it still arrives, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

subscription-cancellation-terms.title: About cancellation
subscription-cancellation-terms.description: How to cancel, how long you can carry on using it, and our approach to refunds.
subscription-cancellation-terms.html:
You can cancel a {{PRODUCT}} paid plan at any time. After you cancel, you carry on using it until the last day of the billing period you have already paid for. This article explains how to cancel, what happens afterwards, and our approach to refunds.

Plans and paymentWhat the plans include, seats, and the notation under the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions→Reading your invoicePro-rating and qualified invoices→Deleting your accountWhere you want to delete the whole account rather than the subscription→

#How to cancel

Note

Cancellation is per workspace, and can only be done by an administrator of that workspace. It is done from the settings screen of the desktop app (macOS and Windows). The web version supports viewing and editing existing notes and has no billing screen.

  1. 1

    Open the billing screen

    Switch to the workspace you want to cancel and open Settings > Billing.

  2. 2

    Open subscription management

    Manage subscription — clicking it opens the payment provider's management screen.

  3. 3

    Confirm the cancellation

    Cancel subscription — choose it and follow the on-screen instructions to confirm.

Check
  • Settings > Billing no longer shows a next renewal date
  • The subscription shows as due to be cancelled in the payment provider's management screen
  • Where you subscribe on several workspaces, you have checked each of them

Where you cannot get into the account at all (because the email address used for the subscription no longer works, for example), contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. We will act once we have confirmed you are the subscriber.

Members cannot cancel

Workspace members can view the billing screen and upgrade, but cannot cancel an existing subscription, change plan or change the payment method. Where the administrator has left and there is nobody in the role, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. We are happy to discuss changing roles as well.

#What happens after you cancel

Cancelling does not stop you using it there and then.

When State
Immediately after cancelling Still on the paid plan, with automatic renewal stopped
Until the last day of the current billing period You carry on using the paid features as before
After the last day of the billing period It switches to the free plan automatically. No further charges arise

Where a free trial ends without a subscription being taken out, it switches to the free plan in the same way.

Switching to the free plan does not delete your notes. What changes is which features are available — for instance, a limit on how far back the note history goes in the app. The differences between plans are covered in Plans and payment. To keep your past notes to hand before it switches, export them to CSV with Exporting notes in bulk.

#Our approach to refunds

Refunds are considered separately for monthly and annual subscriptions. In both cases, after cancelling you can use it until the last day of the period you have paid for.

#Monthly subscriptions

We do not refund the current month's charge on cancellation, because you can use the service until the last day of the period you have paid for. Nor is there a pro-rated refund.

#Annual subscriptions

Annual billing is available on Enterprise subscriptions, paid a year in advance. Where you cancel partway through a term, automatic renewal stops from the point of cancellation and you carry on using it until the last day of the term.

LegislationConsumer Contract Act, Article 9 (voiding of clauses fixing damages payable by a consumer etc.)

Item 1 of that article voids, in a clause fixing the amount of damages on cancellation or providing for a penalty, any part exceeding “the average amount of loss” that would arise to a business on cancellation of contracts of the same kind. Any provision on mid-term cancellation of an annual subscription has to be designed within that constraint.

LegislationConsumer Contract Act, Article 8-2 (voiding of clauses making a consumer waive the right to cancel etc.)

A clause making a consumer waive a right to cancel arising from the business's non-performance, or giving the business the power to decide whether a right to cancel exists, is void. Where {{COMPANY}} fails to provide the service through its own fault, your right to cancel the contract or seek a refund is not limited by the terms.

#Where the cause lies with {{COMPANY}}

Where we are at fault and could not provide the service on an ongoing basis, we will consider a refund or other response individually, separately from the above. Contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

#About cooling-off

Cooling-off does not apply to {{PRODUCT}}. A contract applied for online is “mail-order sales” under the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, and mail-order sales have no cooling-off regime of the kind that applies to door-to-door sales.

The Act does provide an eight-day right of return for mail-order sales, but that regime applies to contracts of sale of goods or specified rights. A contract to use a service such as {{PRODUCT}} is a contract for the provision of services and falls outside it.

LegislationAct on Specified Commercial Transactions, Article 15-3 (cancellation of contracts in mail-order sales)

Paragraph 1 of that article provides that, for a contract of sale of goods or specified rights, an application may be withdrawn or the contract cancelled until eight days have passed from the day of delivery or transfer. It is limited to contracts of sale and does not apply to a contract for the provision of services such as the {{PRODUCT}} subscription.

LegislationAct on Specified Commercial Transactions, Article 11 (advertising in mail-order sales)

Advertising for mail-order sales must display the consideration, when and how payment is made, when the service is provided, the terms of any application period, and matters relating to withdrawal or cancellation of an application, among other things. Cancellation terms fall under item 5 of that article, so {{PRODUCT}} sets them out both in this article and in the notation based on the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions.

#For corporate customers

Where you subscribe to {{PRODUCT}} as a business or for business purposes, the mail-order sales provisions of the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions and the Consumer Contract Act do not apply. Cancellation and refund terms are as set out in the terms of service or in an individually concluded contract.

LegislationAct on Specified Commercial Transactions, Article 26 (exclusions)

Under paragraph 1, item 1 of that article, the mail-order sales provisions do not apply to contracts concluded as, or for the purposes of, a business. That covers corporate customers and sole traders contracting for business purposes.

#Cancelling versus deleting your account

What you want to do What to do
Stop being charged, but keep your notes The cancellation steps in this article. It switches to the free plan and your notes remain
Get rid of the whole workspace Cancel, then follow the deletion steps in Workspaces.
Delete the account and all your notes Deleting your account — those steps

Deleting your account alone does not stop the subscription. Where you are on a paid plan, cancel first.

#If something is not working

Q. I cancelled but I am still on the paid plan

A. After cancelling, you stay on the paid plan until the last day of the current billing period. Automatic renewal has stopped, and it switches to the free plan once that day passes. Check in Settings > Billing that no next renewal date is shown.

Q. I cancelled but I am still being charged

A. You may have subscriptions on more than one workspace. {{PRODUCT}} charges per workspace, so each one has to be cancelled. Switch between workspaces from your workspace name at the bottom left and check the state of Settings > Billing on each. If there is a charge you cannot account for, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

Q. There is no Manage subscription button, and someone else's email address is shown

A. Billing for that workspace is managed by a different administrator. Ask the person at the address shown to cancel, or to have the billing administrator changed.

Q. I only want to reduce seats, not cancel

A. Removing members from the workspace reduces the seat count; you do not need to cancel. The difference is pro-rated and reflected in your next invoice. For the steps see Workspaces, and for how it appears on the invoice see Reading your invoice.

Q. Does cancelling delete my notes?

A. No. Your notes stay with the account after it switches to the free plan. There may be a limit on how far back the history goes in the app, so to keep everything to hand, export it to CSV with Exporting notes in bulk.

#Related articles

Plans and paymentWhat the plans include, and the notation under the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions→Reading your invoiceHow to read the pro-rating→Terms of serviceThe body of the contract terms→Deleting your accountWhere you want to delete the whole account→

feature-requests.title: Common requests, and where they stand
feature-requests.description: The features asked for most often, whether they are supported today, and what you can do instead.
feature-requests.html:
This brings together the requests that come up most often in support enquiries: whether each is supported today and, where it is not, what you can do instead.

Note

This reflects the position when this article was last updated. Nothing here is a promise to provide anything that is not currently supported. For the latest position, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.

How transcription worksWhat is possible today→List of integrationsThe external services you can connect→Our security arrangementsInformation on storage and encryption→

#Transcription and speakers

The requests we hear most often about capturing audio and transcribing it.

#Speaker labels

A much-requested feature, now available.Speaker labels attribute what is said in the transcript to participants by their display names rather than “me” and “them”.

  • Google Meet — available on macOS and Windows using the browser extension. For the setup, see Using speaker labels in Google Meet.
  • Zoom — available on macOS. For the setup, see Using speaker labels in Zoom.

Even where it is not supported, notes are produced with speakers inferred from context. Where a name is wrong, you can correct it directly in the note or tell chat to fix it.

#Accuracy with Japanese honorifics and spoken language

We are asked about accuracy with honorific expressions such as “〜させていただきます” and “〜のほうでよろしかったでしょうか”, and with self-corrections, backchannelling and several people speaking at once. We do not currently guarantee any accuracy specific to Japanese.

Where accuracy is a problem, these can help.

  • Register internal terminology and proper nouns (see the next item).
  • Put the microphone near the speaker, and avoid several people sharing one device's microphone.
  • Reduce echo in the meeting room and noise from air conditioning.

The accuracy of transcription and summarisation varies with audio quality, the number of speakers, background noise and the presence of specialist terms. No particular level of accuracy is guaranteed. Ways to improve it are gathered in Transcription is not working.

#Registering internal terminology

Already supported. Registering company names, product names, team names and industry abbreviations makes those spellings more likely to be used in the transcript. Registration at workspace level is done by an administrator and applies to everyone in it. For the steps, see Customising transcription.

There are limits on how many terms can be registered and on how spelling variations are absorbed. Not every mis-transcription is resolved.

#More languages

The most-requested languages are supported, but not every language. For what is supported, see Multi-language support. If you need a particular language, contact {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}; we will look into it with our transcription supplier.

#Editing the transcript

Not currently supported. We recognise there are times when you want to correct something recorded wrongly, and we have noted it as something to consider improving.

The AI-formatted note can be edited. Correcting the content of the note, rather than the transcript itself, is possible today.

#Recording meetings

Requests about what triggers recording and which kinds of meeting can be recorded.

#Starting recording automatically for every meeting

Not currently supported. We have noted the request, but because of the risk of recording meetings and moments you did not intend, we are prioritising getting the features for deleting and editing transcripts in place first.

In Japanese organisations, a mechanism that starts recording automatically without telling participants is also apt to run into internal rules. For how to think about giving notice, see How far you can go with AI minutes (a guide for teams), and for the features that tell participants you are recording, see About telling people you are recording.

#Saving audio or video

Recording and saving audio files or video is not currently supported. {{PRODUCT}} is aimed squarely at producing notes, and does not offer a feature for storing recordings.

Where you need a recording of a meeting, use the recording feature of your meeting system, such as Zoom or Microsoft Teams.

#Notes and organisation

Requests about the shape of the notes produced, and organising them afterwards.

#Setting a default template

Not currently supported. A meeting note is first summarised using an automatically chosen template. You can rebuild it afterwards with a different template, but you cannot make a template other than automatic selection the default, or specify a template before or during a meeting.

We are including this use case in our thinking as we revisit how templates work. For what is possible today, see Shaping notes with templates.

#Filing into folders automatically

A frequent request. We are asked for a default folder for new notes, for notes to be filed into folders automatically by rule, and for a way to show only notes that are not in a folder. None of these is currently supported. Improving organisation is an area we work on continuously.

For how organisation works today, see Spaces and folders.

#Approval workflows and sign-off for minutes

In Japanese organisations it is common practice for a manager to review minutes and for them to be finalised as an official record through approval and a seal. {{PRODUCT}} has no feature for requesting approval, tracking approval status or applying an electronic seal. We have noted the request.

For now, there are these approaches.

  • Use export or sharing to take the note into your internal workflow or document management system for approval.
  • Keep a separate shared folder for approved minutes and collect only the finalised ones there.
  • Notion integration or the Slack integration — build a review request flow with either.

#Calendars and integrations

Requests about which calendars can be connected and about integrating with external services.

#Support for Apple Calendar

Not currently supported. The calendars that can be connected are Google Calendar and the Microsoft / Outlook calendar. This is a frequent request. For what is supported today, see Connecting your calendar.

#Deeper support for Microsoft Teams

Integration with the Microsoft 365 calendar is supported, and Teams meetings are pulled in as events. Obtaining speaker labels in Teams, however, is not currently supported; speaker labels are available in Google Meet and Zoom.

We are also asked about posting to Teams chat automatically and about working inside the Teams app. Neither is currently supported. For how to tell participants in a Teams meeting that you are recording, see Telling people you are recording (for individuals).

#Integrating with Salesforce or kintone

Direct integrations with Salesforce and kintone are not currently offered. Both are widely used in Japanese organisations and we have noted the request.

For now, there are two approaches.

  • Zapier integration — use it to send data to an external service when a note is created.
  • API — use it to retrieve notes and transcripts from your own systems.

The services you can connect are listed in List of integrations.

#Sending to an integration automatically

At present, sending a note to an integration requires an explicit action each time. A note is never sent to an external service automatically once it is created.

We hear requests for automation continuously. Even if we build it, it is likely to be triggered by some action such as adding a note to a folder — to avoid unintended transmission outside the company.

#Where data is stored, and how the product is offered

Requests about where data is kept and in what form the product is offered.

#A mobile app

Not currently supported. Use {{PRODUCT}} in the desktop app (macOS and Windows). You cannot record a meeting from a phone or tablet, and recording in-person meetings and phone calls is not supported either.

From a browser you can view and edit notes you have already created. For reading notes back or correcting wording while you are out, use a browser. Recording and transcription work by capturing the computer’s system audio and microphone, so they run only in the desktop app. The conditions for capture are covered in How transcription works.

#Running it on premises

Not currently supported. {{PRODUCT}} is offered as a cloud service; there is no form of it that is installed on your own servers or in your own data centre.

#Choosing storage in a Japanese region

A feature letting customers specify the region their data is stored in is not currently offered.

Where industry guidance sets requirements on where data is held and on processors — for financial institutions, healthcare providers and licensed professionals — see Use in healthcare, finance and the professions.

#Anything else

There are many more features we would like to build than the ones listed here. We work to priorities, so we cannot do everything.

Send requests to {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}. Telling us which part of what work you need it for gives us something to work with.

Put the microphone near the speaker, and avoid several people sharing one device's microphone. Reduce echo in the meeting room and noise from air conditioning.
